## PT-404 — World danger is a CEILING on the area tier, not a third term in the max.

**Atlas supplies `danger` per world, 1–4. ⚠ `LOOT-01 §4` had two inputs and no rule for a third.**

    ⚠ area tier = min( max(encounter, container), world danger + 1 )

### ⚠ Why a ceiling

    encounter level       how hard was this to REACH        ⚠ LOCAL
    container difficulty  how well was this PROTECTED       ⚠ LOCAL
    world danger          what KIND of place is this        ⚠ NOT LOCAL

> **⚠ A world danger of 4 does not make every room on Korriban tier 4.** **It makes the Valley of the Dark Lords tier 4 and the spaceport tier 1.**

**⚠ A rule letting it RAISE a tier puts Sith-vault loot in a Korriban cantina.** **A rule letting it CAP one stops an improvised room on a farming world producing a lightsaber crystal.**

**⚠ `+1` because a world's danger describes the place as a whole and one room may exceed it.**

### ⚠ And it closes the hole `§2.5b` flagged

**`AGENDA 2.5b`: a generated area defeats all three of `§4`'s layers, because the generator picked the contents FROM a tier — circular.**

> **⚠ World danger is the ONE input a generator does not pick. It comes from the setting, before the generator runs.**

**⚠ Which gives a procedurally generated area a ceiling even when everything else is circular.**

### ⚠ The cost, stated

**180 of 288 worlds are danger 1, capping most of the galaxy at area tier 2.**

**⚠ Deliberate. Most of the galaxy is quiet, and a party wanting tier-3 loot should have to go somewhere that earns it.**

**⚠ A GM may override. The field is a default, not a fence.**

### ⚠ My own sharpest instance is `PT-374`

**I searched every 2DA in holdings for a Force die base table and reported it absent.**

    ⚠ the scope was CORRECT — "not in any 2DA either game ships" was TRUE
    ⚠ the conclusion was WRONG — PT-148 had found the rule months earlier

### ⚠ The two rules, stated together

    ⚠ PT-386   a negative is scoped to WHAT WAS READ, never to the object containing it
    ⚠ PT-407   scoping does not certify the SEARCH. Before reporting an absence,
               name the trees NOT searched and say why they were excluded.

**⚠ The second is the harder discipline, because the excluded tree is by definition the one you did not think of.**

    Quara    +2 Strength, −2 Charisma       +2 Intimidate, +2 Athletics Tusked Charge

## PT-414 — CLOSED. `+4 Swim` was ported all along, and the repo already had it

**⚠ `SPECIES-MASTER` carried `⚠ +4 Swim` against `PT-408`'s `+2 Swim, +2 Survival`, with nothing recording the change.** **I flagged it as an unexplained edit.**

> **Aquala gain a `+4` species bonus on Swim checks, while Quara and Ualaq receive a `+2` bonus on Swim checks.**

**⚠ `SPECIES-MASTER` was right and `PT-408` was the departure.** **The unexplained edit was somebody correcting me.**

### ⚠ And Quara and Ualaq were owed a bonus nobody gave them

**Both take `+2 Swim` in the source. Our records gave them none.** **Added: `Quara` `+2 Swim, +2 Intimidate, +2 Athletics`; `Ualaq` `+2 Swim, +2 Alertness, +2 Stealth`.**

### The consequence, stated because it is not free

**A one-skill bonus list forces the racial skill.** **`SPECIES-RACIAL-SKILL` draws aptitude from the bonus list, so an Aquala at `+4 Swim` alone would have no choice.**

**⚠ The Quara/Ualaq `+2 Swim` addition incidentally fixes this for them.** **The Aquala joins the Nautolan on the automatic list at `SPECIES-RACIAL-SKILL §114` — now a PORTED consequence rather than a design choice, which is a better place for it to sit.**

## PT-416 — The `−2 Wisdom` is restored, and ⚠ the subrace split is recorded as OURS

**`UAA f.14`: `+2 Constitution, −2 Wisdom, −2 Charisma`.** **`PT-408` carried the Charisma penalty across and dropped the Wisdom one without recording the drop.**

**Restored. The `−2 Wisdom` and `−2 Charisma` are the SHARED Aqualish line; the `+2` is set per subrace.**

### It is inside the band

**Derived from `SPECIES-MASTER §2`, net ability sums run `−2` to `+2` across 26 records.** **Five species sit at net `−2`: Quarren, Gamorrean, Weequay, Wookiee, Devaronian (male).** **Four carry the `−2 Wis, −2 Cha` pair or a superset.**

**⚠ And nothing in the gate checks this.** **`audit_bands` and `audit_abilities` are CLASS checks. There is no species balance check, so the `−2` floor is a convention nobody wrote down.**

### ⚠ The Quarren collision, and why it is not ours to fix

**The Aquala lands on `+2 Con, −2 Wis, −2 Cha` — character-for-character our Quarren.** **Only the Aquala; the Quara is `+2 Str` and the Ualaq `+2 Dex`.**

> **⚠ Our Quarren line is itself ported from `RCR p.30`. Two published books independently gave two species the same spread.**

**Separated in play by skills (`+4 Swim` against `+2 Swim, +2 Intimidate`), by `Fins`, and by everything in prose.** **Accepted.**

### ⚠ The split has no source and that must be on the record

**NEITHER book splits the ability line.** **`UAA f.14` gives one spread for all three; Saga Edition gives one spread for all three.** **The per-subrace `+2` is authored, on the Nikto model.**

**⚠ The warrant is the Quarren adjacency itself:** porting the undifferentiated line would have produced a species mechanically indistinguishable from one we already had. **The split is what stops the Aqualish being a Quarren reskin.**

**The subraces ARE differentiated in the source — on Swim and on `Fins`.** **`PT-408` was right to split and wrong about where the source stopped.**

**I proposed both off a wiki page describing the Saga Edition entry.**

**`UAA f.14` carries neither.** **UAA is the RCR-era book and RCR governs mechanics — `PT-372`.**

**Nothing to port. Withdrawn before it was ruled.**

## PT-418 — `Fins` is ported as a PENALTY, narrowed, and the authored dryness cost is cut

**⚠ Our `Finned` and the source's `Fins` ran in opposite directions.**

| | `UAA f.14` | `RACIAL-FEATS-01` as it stood |
|---|---|---|
| **Nature** | **A penalty** | A benefit plus a cost |
| **Content** | `−4` on skill checks using equipment not built for fins — *"most weapons, computers, and control panels"* | Full swim speed, no submerged penalty |
| **Dryness** | **absent** | `−2` Constitution after a day out of water |

### The ruling

**Port the `−4`. Narrow it to fine-manipulation equipment — `Computer Use`, `Security`, `Repair`, `Slicing`, `Sleight of Hand`, and any control-panel or console task.** **⚠ Weapons are explicitly EXCLUDED.**

**⚠ Cut the `−2` Constitution dryness cost.** **Authored in `PT-408`, absent from every source, and once `Fins` is a real penalty the Aquala pays twice for one piece of anatomy.**

**Keep a swimming benefit as `6 metres swimming`, on the Nautolan's pattern.** **⚠ Authored — `UAA` gives the Aquala a skill bonus and no swim speed.**

### Why the narrowing, and it is a real departure

**Derived from `RACIAL-FEATS-01`: the largest penalty any species takes on ITSELF is `−2`** — Mon Calamari `−1` Will, Nikto `−2` Persuade, Bith `−2` Alertness beyond 10 metres. **Echani's `−4` falls on outsiders, not the Echani.**

> **⚠ `−4` on most weapons would be the harshest drawback in the game by a wide margin, and the only one that makes a subrace worse at fighting.**

**And `UAA f.14` itself says the typical Aqualish hero is a scoundrel or a soldier.** **A penalty that makes both unplayable contradicts the same paragraph it is printed beside.**

**The flavour reason survives intact** — fins are why the Aquala stay on Ando, which is what both books use them to explain.

## PT-420 — The species skill budget is `+4`, and ⚠ I broke it in the same batch that discovered it

**Owner asked whether any other species carries three skill bonuses. Derived from `SPECIES-CHAPTER-v2`, across the 48 entries with a skill line:**

| Shape | Count |
|---|---|
| **Two `+2`s** | **39** |
| **One `+4`** | **5** |
| Conditional | 1 *(Bith)* |
| **⚠ Three bonuses** | **2 — both mine** |

**⚠ 43 of 48 entries total exactly `+4`. No species in this game has three skill bonuses. The Quara and Ualaq were the only two, and I wrote them.**

### The one species that exceeds `+4`, and what it pays

**`Wookiee` — `+4 Intimidate, +2 Beast Handling`, totalling `+6`.**

**⚠ It is a COSTED outlier.** **`+4 Strength, −2 Dexterity, −2 Wisdom, −2 Charisma` is a net `−2` ability spread, and a Wookiee cannot speak Basic or any language but Shyriiwook.** **It buys the extra `+2`.**

> **⚠ The Quara and Ualaq bought nothing. They were `+6` for free.**

### The fix

**`Quara` → `+2 Swim, +2 Intimidate`. `Ualaq` → `+2 Swim, +2 Stealth`.**

**`Athletics` dropped from the Quara; `Alertness` dropped from the Ualaq.** **⚠ `Alertness` was the right one to cut: `Wide Field` already carries the four-eyed perception theme mechanically, so the bonus was saying the same thing twice.**

**`PT-414`'s three-way racial-skill choice disappears with it.** **Every entry in `SPECIES-RACIAL-SKILL` offers one of two again.**

### ⚠ How it happened, because the mechanism matters

**`UAA f.14` owed the Quara and Ualaq `+2 Swim`. I ADDED it to an authored pair instead of REPLACING one of them.**

> **⚠ A ported value arriving into an authored record is not an addition. It is a claim on the budget, and something already there has to leave.**

**Nothing caught this.** **`audit_bands` and `audit_abilities` are class checks; there is no species budget check in the gate at all — `PT-416` said so about ability spreads and it is equally true of skills.**

## PT-421 — `Fins` gets its benefit back, and the Aquala becomes the best swimmer in the game

**Owner ruling. `PT-418` ported `Fins` as a pure penalty. That was faithful to `UAA f.14` and wrong for our corpus — a subrace whose defining trait is only a cost.**

### The trait as it now stands

**`Fins`** — **cup-shaped hands where the other two have fingers.**

**Swim at your full land speed, and take no penalty fighting submerged.**
**⚠ And `−4` on any skill check using equipment not designed for fins** — Computer Use, Security, Repair, Slicing, Sleight of Hand, and any console or control-panel task. **Weapons are not affected.**

**Speed line becomes `10 metres, on land and in water`.** **⚠ This supersedes `PT-418`'s authored `6 metres swimming`.**

### ⚠ It makes the Aquala the fastest swimmer on the roster

**The Nautolan swims at `6` metres against a `10`-metre land speed.** **The Aquala now swims at `10`.**

**Defensible and stated deliberately:** **the Nautolan is a good swimmer with hands; the Aquala has fins instead of hands and pays `−4` for them.** **The speed is what the `−4` buys.**

> **⚠ Flagged for the Nautolan's owner-facing entry: it is now second-best at the thing its `+4 Swim` implies it is best at.** **Not changed. Recorded so the comparison is a decision rather than an accident.**

## PT-422 — `Wide Field` takes a condition, on `Antennal Sense`'s pattern

**Owner ruling. `Cannot be flanked by anything it can see.`**

**⚠ As written it was unconditional, and nothing else in the corpus is.**

| Trait | Species | Condition |
|---|---|---|
| **Antennal Sense** | Rodian | *"cannot be flanked by anything it can hear"* |
| **Wide Field** *(was)* | Aqualish, Ualaq | **⚠ none** |
| **Wide Field** *(now)* | Aqualish, Ualaq | **cannot be flanked by anything it can see** |

**⚠ The only precedent for unflankability was already conditional, and I wrote a strictly better version of it without noticing the one it copied.**

### What the condition costs, in play

**A Ualaq is still flanked by an attacker it cannot see** — in darkness beyond its vision, while blinded, by a `Stealth` chain that has not been beaten, or by anything invisible.

> **⚠ And it still beats the Rodian in a silent room, exactly as the Rodian beats it in a dark one.** **Two species, two senses, two blind spots. That is the shape the corpus already had.**

### ⚠ The second clause is kept, and it is not a contradiction

**`take no penalty for attacking a target you cannot see clearly` stands.**

**⚠ *"Cannot see clearly"* is not *"cannot see."*** **The first is smoke, glare, poor cover, partial concealment; the second is the flanking condition.** **A Ualaq shoots fine through a haze it can still see through, and is flanked by what it cannot see at all.**

**Flagged rather than assumed:** if `ACTION-ECONOMY-01` ever collapses concealment and invisibility into one condition, this trait carries a conflict and must be revisited.

## PT-423 — `PT-379`'s fork closed. ⚠ It was bidirectional, and deleting `rules/` would have destroyed live work

**Fork list: 39 → 0.** **`audit_duplicates` passes for the first time.**

### ⚠ The premise I started with was wrong

**I proposed deleting the `rules/` duplicates on the evidence of two files** — `PLAYTEST-RULINGS-01` at 72 rulings behind and `AGENDA-CURRENT` pre-S11 — **and generalised from them.**

**Derived per pair from `git log` and line-set comparison, `rules/` was AHEAD or diverged on 26 of 32.**

> **⚠ `rules/FORMS-01.md` held 248 lines absent from `force/`, including `§2.2` — the implementation of `PT-185`.** **`force/` is marked STALE in the bootstrap and it is, which is exactly why the `rules/` copy was the live one.**

**⚠ `PT-379` was not a bulk copy that was abandoned. It was a bulk copy after which BOTH sides kept receiving edits.** **That is why `audit_duplicates` could only ever say FORKED: the content genuinely differs in both directions.**

### Method — a real three-way merge, not a pick

**For each pair, the merge base is the earlier-created path's blob at the commit where the SECOND copy was added.** **At that instant the two were identical, which is what makes it a base.**

**`git merge-file --diff3` on all 29 pairs: 27 clean, 2 conflicts.**

| | |
|---|---|
| Byte-identical, deleted | **10** |
| Canonical ahead, deleted | **7** |
| **Three-way merged into canonical** | **27** |
| Conflicts adjudicated by hand | **2** |
| Check defect | **1** *(`README.md`)* |

### ⚠ The merge dropped content, and that was correct

**`ACTION-ECONOMY-01` merged to exactly the `rules/` line count, and `comms/`-only lines vanished.** **I checked rather than assumed:**

    "Read the Ground"      base ✓  rules ✗  comms ✓  merged ✗
    "Terrain Sense"        base ✗  rules ✓  comms ✗  merged ✓

**`PT-207` replaced `Read the Ground` with `Terrain Sense`.** **The `rules/` side had applied the ruling; `comms/` had not. The merge took the deletion because it was a deliberate edit against the base, not a loss.**

**Same shape for the Jedi armour line — `comms/` still carried *"Jedi are granted no armour deliberately"*, which `PT-144` reversed.**

> **⚠ A three-way merge preserves DELETIONS. A two-way union would have resurrected two superseded rulings.**

### The one-line pairs were all the same defect

**Seventeen pairs differed by one to five lines, and every one was a rename the project had ruled, applied on the `rules/` side only:**

    Scoundrel → Smuggler          PT-73
    Combat Droid → Marksman       PT-75
    Expert Droid → Engineer       PT-76
    Tech Specialist → Machinist   PT-83, PT-225
    Explorer → Treasure Hunter    PT-238
    Doctor → Medic                PT-243
    Force Focus → Force Channel   PT-103, PT-186
    C-ids → PT-ids                PT-113

**⚠ Every canonical copy was a pre-rename snapshot. Seventeen documents were quietly serving superseded class names to anyone who opened the wrong path.**

### `FORCE-POWERS-01` — 10 conflict hunks, resolved by derivation rather than by reading

**140 lines only in `rules/`, 73 only in `force/`. Neither a superset, so `merge-file` conflicted on every table block.**

**Rather than adjudicate ten hunks by eye, I keyed both tables by power name and asked whether any canonical row had no counterpart:**

    canonical-only lines            73
    with a same-named row in rules/  73
    ⚠ ORPHANS                         0
    powers missing from rules/     none

**⚠ All 73 are the PRE-conversion version of a row `rules/` also holds** — `PT-24`'s seconds ÷ 3, `PT-301`/`PT-302`'s dice caps, `PT-297`'s Afflict figures, and the `Force Wound` → `Force Strangle` rename. **`rules/` is a complete superset in content, and the line diff only made it look otherwise.**

**`FORCE-POOL-01-v3`'s single conflict was the same:** `rules/` carries *"⚠ RULED. Owner decision, `PT-102`"* where `force/` carries *"⚠ Changed."* **Superset. Taken.**

### ⚠ A text defect carried forward, NOT fixed

**`Force Breach` in the `rules/` copy reads:** ***"All six tiers of Force, but the target can reactivate them if Force Points are available."***

**The base and the canonical copy read *"All six tiers of Force Inspire Followers are also cancelled with this power. These powers are instantly cancelled, but…"***

**`PT-221`/`PT-224` moved `Inspire Followers` out of the Force powers and into the Officer as `Rally`, so the removal was right — but it left a dangling clause.** **⚠ Flagged, not repaired: repairing it inside a merge would hide a content edit inside a structural one.**

## PT-425 — ⚠ `PT-410` corrected by S11, and the fix. The gate had no signal AT ALL

**⚠ My diagnosis was wrong in its central claim. S11:**

> ***"This was not a reorganisation. Nothing moved. The repo has ALWAYS had `scripts/` and docs in subdirectories."***

**S11 built a FLAT working directory at `/home/claude` — 185 `.md` files beside the scripts — wrote every check against `scripts/../NAME.md`, and copied the scripts into a repo where that was never true.**

**⚠ The scripts have never run here. Not once.** **Every *"gate sendable"* in the record was true of a directory that is not this one.**

### ⚠ And it is worse than ten dead checks

**`PT-410` counted the ten that CRASHED. It missed the shape that made this survive a whole session of people reading gate output.**

    CRASH    open(root/'NAME.md')  -> FileNotFoundError -> BLOCK
    ⚠ VACUUM glob(root/'*.md')     -> 19 files not 190  -> PASS

**⚠ `audit_absence`, `audit_grid`, `audit_rulings` globbed a directory holding 19 of 190 documents. `audit_classroster` and `audit_source` had `read()` helpers returning `''` for a missing file, and every test downstream passed on an empty string.**

> **⚠ A check that found nothing to check reports PASS. Ten checks were loud and the rest were silent, and the silent ones are why nobody looked.**

**The gate did not have 13 of 23 working. It had close to none.**

### The fix, both halves

**`scripts/_paths.py`** — one resolver, `DOC_DIRS` searched in order, **and MISSING RAISES.** **`all_md()` walks the corpus instead of one directory.** **`scope()` prints what was searched — `PT-62`.**

**`gate.py` now separates `[ERROR]` from `[BLOCK]`** by looking at stderr for a traceback. **⚠ Without this half the next path change reproduces the whole thing silently**, which is S11's own point and the reason it is not optional.

**Also repointed: `build_inventory`, `sort_items`, `tlk` and `audit_grouping` all resolved data through a `repo/` directory that does not exist here.**

### ⚠ Two more defects of the same class, found while fixing it

**`audit_paths` PASSES on all of this. It tests for ABSOLUTE paths; these are relative.** **⚠ `PT-407` shipped by the author of `PT-407`.**

**`audit_grid` matched the FRACTION of a decimal** — *"1.7 metres"* reported as `7 m` off the Aqualish height. **Regex now refuses a preceding digit or point.**

**⚠ Fourth instance today with `PT-410`, `PT-400` and `PT-424`: a check right about its literal test and wrong about what the test stands for.**

### Result — the first honest gate run in the repo's life

    before   12 BLOCK   ⚠ 10 of them crashes, and most PASSes vacuous
    after     3 BLOCK   ⚠ 0 crashes

**Surviving findings, all real:**

**`audit_refs`** — **`Ambush` in `REGISTER.md` and `Force Wound` in `PLAYTEST-RULINGS-01` are backticked with no definition.** **⚠ `Force Wound` is a historical name superseded by `Force Strangle`; the reference is inside a ruling that describes the rename, so it may be legitimate quoting. Not resolved either way.**

**`audit_rulings`** — **`PT-415` cited and never written. Now written, as OPEN.**

**`audit_source`** — **`REGISTER.md` claims 12 chains and 34 entries, matching no roster.** **Pre-existing, untouched, and now visible against a check that can actually read the file.**

> **⚠ Ten checks have been dark for the life of this repo. Three findings is what they surfaced on the first run, and that number is only trustworthy for the corpus as it stands today.**

## PT-428 — Creature weapons are a WEAPON PROFILE, not feats and not attack chains

**Owner ruling, and it ports the game's own architecture.**

> **⚠ KOTOR puts sonic on `g_w_crslprc001`. It does not put sonic on the shyrack.** **The rider lives on the equipped weapon item and the creature merely holds it.**

**`BEASTS-ENTRIES-01` already has the slot** — the `attacks` line, `bite 2d6 · claw 2d4`. **It becomes a profile: dice, damage type, and any on-hit rider.**

### The rule this settles

    passive, always-on          -> FEAT
    rides an attack, or must
    be declared                 -> WEAPON PROFILE or attack chain

**Moved OUT of feats by this ruling: `Shriek`, `Goring Charge`, `Bonebreaker`, and the `+2d6` half of `Hunter of the Force`.**

### ⚠ Riders the files give that the entries do not have

    Tach       ItemPoison   g_w_crslash010   ⚠ entry silent
    Kinrath    ItemPoison   g_w_crslash009
    Tuk'ata    ItemPoison   g_w_crslprc002   + 5 attack bonus
    Gizka      Paralyze     g_w_crslprc003   ⚠ the ONLY paralysis in either game
    Shyrack    Sonic 7      g_w_crslprc001   shared with Verkaal
    Katarn     3d6 gore     g_w_crgore001    ⚠ the ONLY gore weapon in either game

**All six are ported and free. Taken.**

### ⚠ And a correction I owe on these

**I reported the on-hit subtypes INVERTED in conversation** — called the gizka poisonous and the kinrath, tach and tuk'ata paralysing. **Subtype 2 is `Paralyze`, subtype 7 is `ItemPoison`.** **The script decoded them correctly and I described them backwards.**

**⚠ Consequence for `PT-359`: the `venomous` tag reads `Kinrath · Hssiss`. Kinrath is right. Hssiss carries NOTHING. Tach and Tuk'ata are venomous and untagged.**

## PT-431 — Acquisition and scaling. ⚠ Three cases, and only two were written

**`GM-CREATURES-01 §3` had two:**

> **For a Beast Master's companion, the level IS the master's Beast Master level. Always.**
> **For a wild creature, pick one.**

**⚠ The third — a beast BOUGHT by someone who is not a Beast Master — fell in the gap.** **And it is reachable: `BEASTS-01`'s acquisition table is open to anyone, gated only at the top by *"the apex predators cannot be bought, only earned. `DC 32`."***

### The ruling

    Beast Master, any beast        level = Beast Master level, ALWAYS.
                                   ⚠ Including a PURCHASED one. Owner ruling.
    Not a Beast Master, purchased  FIXED at the entry's grade. Never scales.
                                   Want better, buy better.
    Wild / GM                      GM picks.

### The acquisition table becomes a market in GRADES

**`PT-430`'s bands are the stock. One row per grade, priced by tier** — a `CR 3` kath hound and a `CR 6` kath hound are two purchases.

**⚠ Three things this buys us.** **The Beast Master's class feature becomes worth something — the same kath hound is a different animal in his hands.** **Non-Beast-Masters get a reason to spend credits.** **And the file's CR bands become content instead of a curiosity.**

### ⚠ Two consequences the ruling creates, stated because they are not free

**⚠ For a Beast Master, every grade of a beast is the SAME purchase.** **He should always buy the cheapest, because it becomes his level regardless.** **The grade market exists for everyone except him.**

**⚠ And buying UP can be a DOWNGRADE.** **A level 3 Beast Master who buys a `CR 12` deadly laigrek gets a level 3 laigrek.** **"Always" is what the owner said and it is what is recorded. Flagged as an edge the owner may wish to revisit — the alternative is `max(beast grade, master level)`, which the owner did NOT rule.**

### ⚠ Still open

**Does a purchased beast get its racial feat?** **If yes, anyone buys `Bore` for a few thousand credits and walks through vault walls.**

**What does a companion's death cost?** **`PT-153` says the Droid Master's droids are materiel and the Beast Master's one companion MATTERS. Nothing states the cost.**

**⚠ Some entries are GM-only at every level a Beast Master reaches** — **`Young Rancor` CR 20, `Terentatek` CR 16.** **The roster does not mark them.**

## PT-432 — ⚠ Level is SCALE. The beast is still the beast. Three per-beast constants

**Owner ruling. *"Just because a beast is the same level doesn't mean they're as good as the tier 2 or tier 3 beasts. Even in the game the higher level cannoks and maalraas' are nothing compared to a zakkeg."***

### ⚠ The entries had no quality axis at all

**Derived across all 27. The ONLY things that varied were TYPE and SIZE, and a beast inherits both:**

    vitality die    ⚠ 1d8 on 24 of 27. 1d4 Iriaz and Wraid (Herd Animal), 1d6
                    Dianoga (Scavenger). A function of TYPE, not of the beast.
    attack dice     purely SIZE. Tiny 1d3 · Small 1d4 · Medium 1d8 · Large 2d6 · Huge 2d8
    natural armour  ⚠ ABSENT. Not one entry carries an AC line.

> **⚠ `Boma`, `Maalrass`, `Kath Hound`, `Nexu`, `Gundark` and `Tuk'ata` are all `Predator · Medium` with character-for-character identical stat lines.** **At the same level they were the same animal.**

**And the zakkeg-versus-cannok gap only existed because one is Huge and one is Small. SIZE was doing the work; nothing expressed QUALITY.**

### Three constants, fixed regardless of level

**`VITALITY DIE` · `NATURAL ARMOUR` · `ATTACK COUNT`.** **Size keeps setting the dice, type keeps setting the saves, and these three make a zakkeg a zakkeg.**

### Derivation — `HP ÷ CR` from the game files

    Young Rancor 17.5   Terentatek 17.5
    Maalrass 13.7  Katarn 13.5
    Boma 10.8  Hssiss 10.8  Zakkeg 10.8  Wraid 10.0
    Cannok 8.5  Laigrek 8.2  Drexl 8.2
    Kath Hound 7.5  Gizka 7.0  Mykal 7.0  Tach 6.0  Kinrath 5.8  Shyrack 5.3

**⚠ Two ratios are unusable and are NOT used.** **`Tuk'ata` reads `1.0` — its `CR 9` block is `9` HP with `Str 6 / Dex 6 / Con 6`, carried entirely by equipped items. Its `CR 11` band gives `137 ÷ 11 = 12.5` and that is what is used.** **`Iriaz` and `Brith` read `10.0` at `CR 1`, which is a floor artifact of a 10 HP minimum, not a quality signal. Assigned by tier and size instead.**

### The table

| Die | Beasts |
|---|---|
| **d20** | **Terentatek** |
| **d12** | **Young Rancor · Hssiss · Gundark** |
| **d10** | **Boma · Zakkeg · Wraid · Katarn · Nexu · Laigrek** |

**Natural armour, straight from the file:**

    Terentatek 14 · Wraid 11 · Boma 8 · Hssiss 8 · Zakkeg 8 · Shyrack 7
    Kinrath 6 · Maalrass 4 · Katarn 4 · Laigrek 4 · Drexl 4 · Gizka 4 · Verkaal 4

Two: `Boma`, `Hssiss`, `Zakkeg`, `Terentatek`, `Young Rancor`, `Wraid`, `Cannok`, `Tach`, `Kinrath`.** **⚠ `Multiattack` becomes a quality marker rather than a feat.**

### ⚠ Three things flagged, not decided

**`Terentatek d20` against `Young Rancor d12`, on identical `17.5` ratios.** **The owner set the terentatek and said nothing about the rancor. Recorded as: the rancor entry is the YOUNG one, and `Rancor` at its upper band takes `d20`. ⚠ If that is wrong the two invert.**

**`Tuk'ata` natural armour reads `0`** — **for a Sith war hound with the only Force resistance in either game. Its `CR 11` band should be checked before this is printed.**

**⚠ `Maalrass` was the strongest non-apex ratio in the game at `13.7` and is now `d6`, below the boma it beats in the files.** **Owner ruling, recorded as a deliberate departure from the source, not an error.**

### Bands are the same beast growing up

**`Shyrack` → `Shyrack Wyrm`. `Laigrek` → `Deadly Laigrek`. `Young Rancor` → `Rancor`.** **A rename at the band, and the three constants DO NOT CHANGE — the wyrm is still `Vermin`, still sonic, still a shyrack. It just got big.**

**⚠ These stop being roster entries and become bands inside one. `Shyrack Wyrm` folds in; the roster goes to 26.** **`PT-426`'s Verkaal question is the only thing still holding the count.**

### ⚠ And it repairs `PT-431`'s hole

**I flagged that a Beast Master should always buy the cheapest grade, because level is his regardless — leaving him no reason to buy up.** **`PT-432` answers it: he has no reason to buy a better GRADE and every reason to buy a better BEAST.** **A level 12 cannok is `d6` and AC 3; a level 12 zakkeg is `d10`, AC 8, Huge dice and two attacks.**

**`WalkRate` is `7` on all 21 file-backed beasts.** **Cannok, rancor, terentatek, shyrack, gizka — identical. It is an animation constant, not a stat.**

**KOTOR's real movement lives in `appearance.2da` and ⚠ we hold it for neither game.** **`k2_iprp_walk.2da` has two rows, `Default` and `ZombieWalk`, and is an ITEM property table.**

> **⚠ No port is available. All 25 values are AUTHORED.**

    Bore     "moves through stone ... at HALF SPEED"      half of what
    Burrow   "moves underground at HALF SPEED"            half of what
    Fleet    "move speed DOUBLED"                         double what
    Kor'slug BEASTS-01 tier table: "no movement worth
             speaking of"  -- a speed claim, in prose, with no number

**⚠ `Maalrass`, `Nexu` and `Iriaz` are the fastest on the list.**

| Speed | Beasts |
|---|---|

**Dexterity does not drive it.** **`Gizka` and `Mykal` have the highest Dex on the roster at `18` and sit mid-ladder; `Iriaz` has `15` and is fastest.** **Speed is what the beast IS, not what its reflexes are — `PT-433`'s companion-versus-wild logic applied to a second axis.**

> **⚠ The sentence was written before any beast had a speed. It is now contradicted by the number and must be rewritten or cut — flagged, NOT edited, because it is descriptive prose in a tier table and the owner ruled the number, not the sentence.**

## PT-436 — `pack` and `swarming` split. ⚠ NUMBERS versus COORDINATION

**⚠ They collided three times because both were written as the same sentence: *"ally adjacent → bonus."***

    Shyrack     Swarm          every ally adjacent to its target counts as flanking
    Kath Hound  hunts in threes  two allies adjacent -> roll twice, take better
    BEASTS-01   pack             "better with ANY ally adjacent"
                swarming         "better with its OWN KIND adjacent"

**⚠ And `PT-153` had already broken the printed definition of `swarming`: the Beast Master has ONE companion, so own-kind adjacency can never fire.**

### The split

    SWARMING   NUMBERS. The beast is one of many. Its benefit comes from bodies
               around the TARGET -- the target is surrounded and its position
               collapses. Weak alone, dangerous en masse.
               ⚠ Improves EVERYONE's position, the party's included.

    PACK       COORDINATION. The beast hunts WITH you. Its benefit comes from
               attacking what an ally has already committed to -- focus fire,
               not encirclement. Strong alone, better aimed.
               ⚠ Improves THE BEAST, and only when it follows a lead.

**Two mechanics that never fire for the same reason.** **The shyrack makes the PARTY better; the kath hound gets better when the PARTY leads.**

### The two feats

| Feat | Granted by | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| **Swarm** | `swarming` — Shyrack · Gizka · Kinrath | **Every ally adjacent to its target counts as flanking**, whether or not they otherwise would. |
| **Pack Hunter** | `pack` — Kath Hound · Tuk'ata · Cannok *(`PT-439`)* | **When it attacks a target one of your allies has already attacked this round, it rolls twice and takes the better result.** |

**⚠ `PT-205` is satisfied. One name, one object, and the triggers are disjoint** — adjacency to the target against prior commitment to the target.

### ⚠ The counter-argument, recorded because the owner may revisit

**A kath hound pack in the games SURROUNDS you; shyracks mob you individually.** **The reverse assignment is defensible.**

**The roster favours what is written** — **`swarming` sits on three small beasts whose entire value is being annoying in a group; `pack` on three medium predators that hunt in coordinated threes.** **⚠ If the tags swap, both feats swap with them and nothing else changes.**

    ⚠ TIER 2 combat riders       Ramming Charge · Force-Clouding Bite · Venom Strike

## PT-440 — Batch 4. ⚠ Three narrowings and a system rule found hiding in a stat block

**`Nexu` · `Gundark` · `Katarn` · `Wraid` · `Tuk'ata`. Twenty of twenty-five converted.**

### `Four Eyes` — narrowed on `Wide Field`'s precedent

**As written it ignored concealment, darkness AND INVISIBILITY, unconditionally.**

> **⚠ Nothing else in the corpus ignores invisibility. No Force power does.** **And it hard-countered the Katarn's own ability two entries below it.**

**`PT-422` cut the Ualaq's `Wide Field` back for exactly this reason — unconditional was strictly better than the Rodian's `Antennal Sense`, the one precedent it copied.**

**Now: ignores concealment and darkness, and names anything within 12 squares THAT GIVES OFF HEAT.** **⚠ Invisibility survives. A droid or a cold body does not register. Infrared means infrared.**

### `Four Arms` — the double attack was priced twice

**⚠ *"Attacks twice a round without the second-attack penalty"* is `Multiattack`, and `PT-432` already made attack count a per-beast CONSTANT.**

**The Gundark carries two weapons in the attack-count column. `Four Arms` is now only the part that column does not cover: it cannot be disarmed or grappled by a single opponent.**

> **⚠ Same capability, one price. Owner endorsed the two attacks; this changes where they are recorded, not whether it has them.**

### `Forest Killer` — split

**Concealment half is passive → FEAT. The first-attack-against-flat-footed half is a declared opening strike → ATTACK, `PT-428`, and `PT-438` gives the Katarn three chains to hold it.**

**⚠ And the split resolves a collision flagged in batch 1.** **The Kor'slug's `Deep Hide` and the Katarn's opener were both ambush-from-hiding.** **Now the kor'slug's is POSITIONAL — unreachable underground — and the katarn's is an ATTACK.**

### `It Carries` → **`Shieldback`**

**Owner rename. Name-checked clean across the corpus.**

**⚠ And it exposes a gap neither feat can fill.** **`Shieldback` and the Iriaz's `Break Away` are the roster's two mount feats and they do not agree — one carries a rider INTO a fight and halves splash, the other carries one OUT.**

> **⚠ THERE ARE NO MOUNTED-COMBAT RULES IN THE CORPUS.** **Nothing states who acts, whether the rider provokes, or what happens when the mount dies.** **Two feats resting on a system that does not exist. A `RULES-01` gap, flagged not solved.**

### ⚠ `Tuk'ata` — a system rule was hiding in a stat block

**The entry carried:** ***"Intelligence 8 — it may take ANY feat it is physically capable of using, not a restricted list."***

**⚠ That is a rule about the FEAT POOL, printed inside one beast's entry.** **It was the sentence that implied a restricted list existed for the other twenty-four — and it was the reason I opened this workstream believing the pool was the blocking question.**

**No such list was ever written. The pool is authored end to end.**

**Moved to `BEASTS-FEATS-01 §3a`, stated generally: a beast's feats are the ones its ENTRY PRINTS — `PT-357`. There is no list it picks from and none it is barred from.** **The Tuk'ata's Intelligence 8 is flavour, not a permission.**

**`Sith Hide` and `Knitting Wounds` both stand, both ported from `g_i_crhide004`.**

## PT-441 — Batch 5, the apex tier. ⚠ And a third missing system

**`Zakkeg` · `Drexl` · `Terentatek` · `Dianoga` ruled. `Young Rancor` still open.**

### The Force-resistance ladder — the inversion is fixed

    Tuk'ata        −4     CR 9 band
    Dire Tuk'ata   −6     CR 11 band   ⚠ new band name, PT-430
    Terentatek     −8     apex

**⚠ It read `−8` tuk'ata against `−6` terentatek.** **A `CR 9`, `d8` war hound out-resisted the `CR 16`, `d20`, galaxy-famous Force-hunter.** **The numbers said the wrong thing and now they do not.**

**⚠ Spelling: `Terentatek`, owner ruling.** **The game resrefs read `terantanak` and `rulan_ter`; ours stands.**

### `Zakkeg` → **`Unyielding`**

**⚠ The old feat fired only against `Boma`, `Maalrass` and `Cannok` — three named beasts.** **In play that is the `apex` tag doing nothing almost always.**

**Now: cannot be knocked prone, slowed, immobilised, or moved against its will; moves through cover and light obstacles, destroying them.**

> **`Str 30`, Huge, AC 8, two attacks, and only `10 metres`.** **The zakkeg's identity is not speed or cunning — it is that nothing you do stops it arriving.**

**⚠ `Unstoppable` and `Juggernaut` both collided — 10 and 12 hits, mostly `ITEMS-01`. `Unyielding` is clean.**

### `Drexl` → **`Snatch`, and it is an ATTACK** — owner ruling

**⚠ Both original clauses were struck.** **`Flyby Attack` is already granted free by `flying` — `PT-427` — so the drexl was paying a racial slot for its own tag.** **And *"automatic critical threats against a prone target"* turned any party holding a trip effect into a permanent crit engine: `Ramming Charge` and `Bonebreaker` both knock prone.**

**`Snatch` has two modes:**

    COMBAT       On a hit against a target MEDIUM or smaller -- one size
                 category below itself -- it carries the target aloft. The
                 target cannot act except to escape.
    NON-COMBAT   As an action it lifts an object or creature Medium or
                 smaller. ⚠ NO DAMAGE. On its turn it may drop what it holds.

**⚠ Size limit set at Medium, one category below the drexl's Large.** **That is a person, a footlocker, a sealed crate — dramatic and bounded.**

**⚠ Its racial slot is now EMPTY, which `PT-437` permits.** **Worth noting the shape: a tier-3 apex holds no racial feat while the tier-1 `Cannok` holds two.** **`PT-438` gives tier 3 FOUR attack chains, so the drexl's identity is in its attacks — but the asymmetry is real and recorded.**

### ⚠ THERE ARE NO FALLING DAMAGE RULES

**`Snatch` drops things. Searched `RULES-01-v2`, `ACTION-ECONOMY-01`, `SKILLS-01`: no falling damage, no height table, nothing.**

> **⚠ Third missing system found this batch — after mounted combat, `PT-440`, which `Shieldback` and `Break Away` both rest on.**

**NOT authored here.** **Writing a general falling rule inside a beast attack is exactly what the Tuk'ata's Intelligence clause did — `PT-440` — and that took four rulings to find. It belongs in `RULES-01`.**

### `Terentatek` → **`Force-Hunter Hide`**, split

**Resistance is passive → FEAT at `−8`.** **The double damage against a creature with a Force class level is a RIDER and goes on the weapon profile — the same call as `Force-Clouding Bite`, `PT-437`.**

**⚠ STILL UNRESOLVED from batch 2:** **`BEASTS-01` records the terentatek as level 10, 150 HP; I extracted `rulan_ter` at `CR 16 · 280 HP · AC 14 · Int 13`.** **Both cannot be feeding the `d20` at `PT-432`.**

### `Dianoga` → **`Lurk`**

**Renamed, and INVERTED for companion use.**

**The original read *"if the party enters water…it may begin the encounter already adjacent to a target of your choice."*** **⚠ Written for a GM creature. A companion does not ambush its own side.**

**Now: deploy it into any water, refuse or flooded space within its speed; it arrives without moving through the intervening squares.**

> **⚠ Still the clearest single piece of evidence for the companion/GM split — an entry whose printed ability only parsed as an encounter.**

### ⚠ `Young Rancor` — OPEN

**Its printed line is not a feat.** ***"Its Strength is the adult's; its vitality is a third. It has not learned what it cannot survive."*** **Strength and vitality are already printed two lines above; the sentence restates them and adds flavour with no mechanic.**

**⚠ Every other entry's one thing DOES something. This one does nothing.**

**`Untaught` proposed and NOT ruled: while below half vitality it gains `+2` attack and `+2` damage and cannot be made to flee.** **⚠ `Reckless` and `Blood Frenzy` both collided; `Untaught` is clean.**

**The alternative `PT-437` permits is an empty slot — `2d8`/`2d6` at Huge with `d12` vitality does not need a feat to be frightening.**

## PT-442 — Falling, `Carried`, and the last three beasts

### Falling damage — it did not exist

**`1d6` per 4 metres fallen, maximum `20d6`. The faller lands prone.**
**An `Acrobatics` check at `DC 15` reduces the distance by 4 metres before damage is rolled.**
**Falling into water or onto soft ground halves the total.**

**⚠ `1d6` per 4 metres is d20's `1d6` per 10 feet, rounded to EVEN metres so it lands on the grid** — `audit_grid` flags anything that does not. **The `20d6` cap is d20's terminal-velocity ceiling; without it a fall from orbit rolls 400 dice.**

**⚠ ASSUMPTION FLAGGED: this treats a square as 2 metres.** **`PT-333` uses *"within 4 metres"* for Point Blank, but `ACTION-ECONOMY-01` never states the square size. If squares are not 2 metres the multiplier moves.**

### `Carried` — ⚠ a condition, NOT a grapple

**Owner asked for midair grappling rules. ⚠ `RULES-01-v2` line 430 BANS grapple in v1, beside polymorph and summoning, as architecture-touching.**

> **⚠ "Build midair grappling" and "grapple is banned in v1" cannot both stand.** **Resolved by writing a CONDITION instead of reversing the ban.**

**`Carried` — you are held by another creature. You cannot move. You gain no benefit from cover, and your position is the carrier's. You may spend an action on `Acrobatics` against the effect's DC to break free; on a success you are released and BEGIN FALLING. The carrier may release you as a free action on its turn. If the carrier dies or is moved against its will, you fall.**

**⚠ `grappled` is ALREADY in the v1 condition set — `RULES-01-v2` line 343.** **Grapple the SUBSYSTEM is opposed checks, size modifiers, an AoO cascade, pins and holds. A carried creature is none of that.**

**Five lines, no new subsystem, no v1 reversal.** **It serves `Snatch`, `Maw`, the Dianoga's drag, the Gundark's grapple immunity, and anything constricting written later.**

### `Brith` — ⚠ never converted, and it needed nothing

**I reported it as having no feat. It has a one thing and my script missed it because `BEASTS-FEATS-01` has no row for it** — **it went through none of the five batches and I did not notice.**

***"On a hit the target cannot take a reaction until the end of its next turn."*** **On a hit → WEAPON RIDER, `PT-428`. No racial feat needed.**

**⚠ `BEASTS-01` line 177 calls it a *"small flying PACK predator"* and its type line carries no `pack` tag. One of the two is wrong. Unresolved.**

### `Laigrek` — the band, owner approved

    Laigrek          Beast Master 1–11    Vermin · Small · armoured · burrowing
    Deadly Laigrek   Beast Master 12+     ⚠ the rename

**Racial feat at the band — `Furnace`: regains 4 vitality at the start of each of its turns, and is immune to fire and heat.**

**⚠ Both halves attested.** **`g_i_crhide018` carries `Regeneration 4`, the highest in either game.** **Wookieepedia gives the deadly laigrek *"tougher armor that could endure high temperatures."***

**Fire breath is an ATTACK at the band — short cone, Reflex save. Lore says *"short streams of fire"*; the range stays small.**

**⚠ The `CR 8` entry keeps an EMPTY racial slot deliberately. The laigrek's feat is something it does not have yet** — the cleanest demonstration of the band system on the roster.

### ⚠ And the first case of a band contradicting a constant

                      c_laigrek_01 (CR 8)   c_laigrek_deadly (CR 12)
    attack count      1 weapon              ⚠ 2 weapons
    natural armour    4                     ⚠ 0

**`PT-432` says the three constants DO NOT change across a band.**

**Ruling: THE CONSTANTS HOLD. The file is ignored here.** **⚠ A `CR 12` blueprint with two weapons dropped on it is not a design statement, and `AC 0` on the ARMOURED variant contradicts the beast's own tag.**

**⚠ It will recur — the Tuk'ata and the Katarn both have bands. Ruled once, here, rather than per beast.**

### `Young Rancor` — ⚠ `Untaught` REJECTED

**Owner: ignore the *young*, build it on what a RANCOR is.**

**No racial feat. `Maw` and `Bite` are attack chains — see `PT-443`.**

## PT-443 — `apex` gets a mechanic. And the first beast attack chains

### `apex` grants `Roar`

    apex   was   Zakkeg · Drexl · Terentatek
           now   Zakkeg · Drexl · Terentatek · Gundark · Young Rancor

**Owner ruling: keep `apex`, add the Gundark and the Young Rancor, and leave the Drexl on it.**

**⚠ Since `PT-359` the tag granted NOTHING.** **Its printed effect was *"lesser beasts flee it"*, which `PT-441` then removed from the Zakkeg for firing only against three named beasts.** **`apex` was a label, which is the shape `aquatic` was cut for.**

**It now grants the `Roar` chain — `PT-429`'s grant rule.**

### ⚠ The drexl, and what the lore actually says

**Owner: *"Drexl should not, UNLESS you can show from lore it was an apex thing."***

**⚠ On TERROR the drexl has the strongest claim of the five.** **Wookieepedia's article states drexls spread terror through early Onderon, attacking villages and forcing the construction of Iziz as the only safe place on the planet.** **A terror effect that reshaped a civilisation; neither the Gundark nor the Young Rancor has anything that specific.**

**⚠ On APEX the evidence runs the other way.** **`Dxun/Legends` lists drexls IN a set — bomas, cannoks, drexls, maalraas, skreevs, zakkegs — not above it. A separate account calls the ZAKKEG the alpha predator of the jungle.**

> **⚠ The "drexl is an apex predator" claims are UNRANKED.** **One is a fan roleplay forum; the other is a Saga wiki page whose own header says the beast data was created by a wiki user.** **Neither is a source under `CANON-01`, and citing them would repeat `PT-368` exactly — a wiki asserting what the sources do not carry.**

**Owner kept the drexl on `apex` knowing this. Recorded as a deliberate call, with the terror warrant strong and the apex warrant weak.**

### ⚠ Tag-granted CHAINS count against the tier allowance

**`PT-429` gives tag-granted FEATS free. ⚠ The rule does NOT carry over to chains.**

**A feat is passive; a chain is a choice made every round at the table.** **A free fourth chain on a tier-3 beast breaks `PT-438`'s cap and hands one player more declarations than anyone else** — **`PT-201`'s table-time failure arriving by a second route.**

**`Roar` occupies one of the beast's slots.**

### The Young Rancor's four chains — `BEASTS-ATTACKS-01`

    Maw     hold -> flat-footed -> ⚠ Carried, and the bite auto-hits
    Bite    +1d8 -> +2d8 and bleed -> +3d8, crit +1, DR to 0
    Fling   4 squares -> 8 and collateral -> 12, Large targets, objects
    Roar    Shaken -> Frightened -> Panicked, by SAVE MARGIN

**⚠ Beast save DCs are `DC 10 + Beast Master level` with NO ability modifier** — the convention `Venom Strike` set. **Player chains add one, and `Str 30` would put every rancor effect five points above the rest of the game.**

**⚠ `Bite` uses `d8`s, not the `d6`s player chains use.** **Its natural bite is `2d8` and a chain should scale with the weapon it modifies.**

### ⚠ Three things left open

**`Bellow` COLLIDES — already a racial feat elsewhere. `PT-205`. The middle tier of `Roar` needs renaming.**

**⚠ `shaken`, `frightened` and `panicked` HAVE NO DEFINED EFFECTS.** **`RULES-01-v2` line 343 lists them; line 345 gives escalation data; nothing says what any of them DOES.** **`Roar` resolves into three words with no rules behind them — the same gap as falling damage before `PT-442`.**

**⚠ Chain entry levels are 1 / 4 / 8, copied from the player convention.** **A tier-3 beast reaching `Devour` at Beast Master 8 may be too fast. Scaling by tier — 1/4/8, 1/6/12, 1/8/16 — is the alternative and is NOT ruled.**

    rules/BEASTS-01.md           4   tier table · tier roster · burrowing tag · type list
    rules/BEASTS-FEATS-01.md     1   the Deep Hide row

### ⚠ What was NOT renamed, and why

**`playtest/PLAYTEST-RULINGS-01.md` — 9 occurrences across `PT-289`, `PT-359`, `PT-366`, `PT-426`, `PT-432`, `PT-435`, `PT-440`.**

**Same rule that kept `comms/TO-EXTRACTOR-*` untouched at `PT-434`: sent correspondence and past rulings are a RECORD, not a live document.** **This entry is the pointer that reconciles them.**

## PT-445 — ⚠ `frightened` is CUT. Two fear conditions, defined

**Owner ruling. The v1 condition set drops from 20 to 19.**

### ⚠ A correction first

**I reported that all three fear conditions had no defined effects. `shaken` DID.**

> **`RULES-01-v2` line 347: *"two `shaken` sources give one `−2`, both being morale penalties in the fear category."***

**The `−2` was there, buried in a STACKING rule rather than a condition definition.** **`frightened` and `panicked` genuinely had nothing.**

### The dependency picture, derived before cutting

    shaken       ⚠ LOAD-BEARING. Line 249 makes it the standard `partial_result`
                 for every half-on-save effect in the schema. Removing it would
                 break the effect block itself.
    frightened   2 dependents, both species feats
    panicked     ⚠ ZERO dependents

### The two conditions

| Condition | Effect |
|---|---|
| **`shaken`** | **`−2` morale penalty on attacks, saves and skill checks.** |
| **`panicked`** | **`shaken`, and it cannot willingly move toward the source and must spend its move getting away.** **Save at the end of each of its turns to end it.** |

**⚠ A creature that SAVES against `panicked` is `shaken` anyway — owner ruling.** **Fear that misses still lands.**

**⚠ `frightened` was the redundant middle.** **It was `shaken` plus fleeing, which is a weaker `panicked` under a third name.** **Two conditions give the only distinction that matters: a tax you play through, against losing control of where you stand.**

### `immune to fear` — now defined, and the wording was already right

**⚠ The LIVE documents already said *"immune to fear"*, not *"cannot be frightened."*** **`SPECIES-CHAPTER-v2` ×2, `RACIAL-FEATS-01` ×2.** **Only `SPECIES-FEATS-DRAFT` carried the narrow phrasing, and it is a draft.**

**`immune to fear` = cannot be `shaken` and cannot be `panicked`** — **⚠ including the `shaken` that a successful `panicked` save would otherwise leave.**

**Held by `Cold Calculation` (Arkanian Pureblood) and `Blood Frenzy` (Sith Massassi).**

> **⚠ Both feats got BETTER from this.** ***"Immune to fear"* protected against nothing, because nothing in the fear family had rules.** **Four live rows needed no edit at all — only the definition was missing.**

### ⚠ Why `panicked` is save-ends-each-turn

**`PT-201` cost a rebuild because one player was consuming 62% of the round.**

**A character who cannot approach anything for three rounds is a player not playing.** **One failed save costs a turn's positioning, not a fight.**

### Escalation

**Line 345's example referenced the cut condition. Rewritten: `shaken` + `shaken` → `shaken`, ⚠ NEVER `panicked`.**

**The fear ladder escalates by SAVE MARGIN — fail by 5 or more — not by stacking applications.** **Repeating `Roar` cannot ladder a target upward, so the ladder lives inside the roll.**

### `Roar` now resolves into rules

    Roar      6 sq   Will save or `shaken`
    ›         8 sq   fail by 5+ -> `panicked`, otherwise `shaken`
    ›› Terrify 10 sq  fail by 5+ -> `panicked`; a creature that saves is `shaken`

**⚠ The middle tier's name `Bellow` still COLLIDES with an existing racial feat — `PT-205`. Unresolved.**

## PT-446 — `fear` is a CATEGORY. ⚠ And the engine already said so

**Owner ruling: `shaken` and `panicked` are distinct effects sitting inside one overarching branch, `fear effects`.**

### ⚠ PORTED, not authored — the link exists in the files

**Owner asked whether the game links the immunity feat to what it blocks. It does.**

    k2_iprp_immunity.2da       k2_iprp_onhit.2da
      0 Backstab                 0 Sleep      4 Fear   ←
      1 LvL/Ab_drain             1 Stun       5 Slow
      2 MindSpells               2 Paralyze   ...
      3 Poison                   3 Confusion
      4 Disease
      5 Fear      ←
      6 Knockdown
      7 Paralysis
      8 Critical_Hits
      9 Death_Magic

**`Fear` is an engine-level effect TYPE — an immunity category at row 5 and an on-hit type at row 4.**

    SOURCE                          applies effect of TYPE     blocked by
      Fear / Horror / Insanity  ──┐
      OnHit: Fear (item)        ──┼──►   "Fear"          ◄──   Immunity: Fear
      any scripted fear effect  ──┘

> **⚠ This is why `FORCE_IMMUNITY_FEAR` has an EMPTY `spellid` and a description that names no mechanic.** **It flags a TYPE. It does not enumerate powers.**

**The category I proposed at `PT-445` was already in the source. It is a port.**

### The feats, updated — 14 rows across 5 documents

| Feat | Now reads |
|---|---|
| **Force Immunity: Fear** *(Sentinel)* | immune to `fear effects` — cannot be `shaken` or `panicked` |
| **Cold Calculation** *(Arkanian Pureblood)* | +2 initiative, immune to `fear effects` |
| **Blood Frenzy** *(Sith Massassi)* | below half vitality, +2 damage, immune to `fear effects` |
| **Death Mask** *(Kaleesh)* | enemies who fail a `fear effect` against you are `Slowed` |
| **Ritual Scarring** *(Sith Kissai)* | as `Death Mask` |
| **Nerve Tendrils** *(Nautolan)* | +2 on saves against `fear effects` |
| **Cold Blood** *(Quarren)* | +2 Will against `fear effects`, Intimidate, mind-influencing |

**⚠ Four of these referenced a category that did not exist.** **`Death Mask` and `Ritual Scarring` have said *"fail a fear effect"* since they were written, pointing at nothing.**

### ⚠ A claim removed from `Force Immunity: Fear`

**The entry read: *"Immune to Fear, Horror, Insanity, Plasma Grenades, and On-Hit: Horror."***

**`k1_feat.2da` row 98 has an empty `spellid`. The string table describes an inner calm and names NO mechanic.** **⚠ The plasma-grenade and `On-Hit: Horror` clauses have no recorded provenance — `PT-368`'s shape.**

**Replaced, with the original text preserved inline so the claim is not silently lost.**

### ⚠ Two engine facts found in passing, neither acted on

**`MindSpells` is a SEPARATE immunity type from `Fear` — row 2 against row 5.** **`Cold Blood` and `Nerve Tendrils` bundle them into one save bonus. The source treats them as two immunities. ⚠ Recorded as a departure, not corrected.**

**`Knockdown` is row 6.** **The Zakkeg's `Unyielding` — *cannot be knocked prone, slowed, immobilised or moved* — has an engine category sitting right there that I authored past without checking. ⚠ Unreconciled.**

### ⚠ And a table that must never be cited

**`k2_iprp_spells.2da` is 336 rows of UNMODIFIED BioWare NWN content** — `Melfs_Acid_Arrow`, `Mordenkainens_Sword`, `Bulls_Strength`, `Wail_of_the_Banshee`.

**Nothing in it is Star Wars.** **It shipped with the engine and was never cleaned.** **⚠ It is not a source at any rank and mining it for content would import D&D wholesale.**

### ⚠ One reading I want confirmed

**Owner wrote *"fear panic and shake should be different effects."*** **Implemented as TWO conditions — `shaken`, `panicked` — inside the `fear effects` category, matching `PT-445` and the engine's model.**

**⚠ If a third condition literally named `fear` was intended, this is wrong and `frightened` returns under a new name.**

## PT-447 — `cowering` added. Three conditions, one category, one save rule

**Owner ruling: a third condition, the games' own `Fear`. ⚠ Plus *"keep it simple."***

### ⚠ The name

**`fear` cannot be both the category and a member of it — `PT-205`.**

**Named `cowering`, which is what the source text says.** **The `Fear` power: *targets cower in fear for 2 rounds.*** **`Horror`: cower for 4.**

> **⚠ The games' `Fear` does not make you nervous. It makes you HELPLESS.** **It sits at the TOP of the severity ladder, not the bottom** — and `Fear`, `Horror` and `Insanity` differ by SCOPE, one target then radius then wider radius, not by severity.

### The whole system, kept short

    fear effects  -- the category, ported from iprp_immunity row 5

      shaken      −2 on attacks, saves and skill checks
      panicked    shaken, and it must move away from the source and cannot approach it
      cowering    ⚠ it cannot act

    Every fear condition ends on a save at the end of the creature's turn.
    ⚠ A creature that SAVES against a fear effect is `shaken` anyway.
    `immune to fear effects` blocks all three, including that trailing `shaken`.

**⚠ ONE save rule for all three, not three rules.** **`PT-445` had the save-and-still-shaken clause on `panicked` alone; it now covers the category.**

**v1 condition set: 19 → 20. `frightened` out, `cowering` in.**

### ⚠ Why save-ends, against the source

**The games use FIXED durations — 2 rounds for `Fear`, 4 for `Horror`.** **We do not.**

> **⚠ `cowering` is the most expensive condition in the game: a character who cannot act is a player not playing.** **`PT-201` cost a rebuild because one player consumed 62% of the round.** **Four rounds of `cowering` is that failure with the sign flipped — one player consuming NONE of it.**

**One failed save costs one turn. Recorded as a deliberate departure from the source's duration model.**

### Plasma grenades — ⚠ the owner was right, and the category absorbs it

**Owner: the removed claim was technically correct.**

**⚠ Unverifiable from what we hold.** **Every grenade blueprint resolves as `CastSpell(index)` — frag 87, stun 88, fire 94, sonic 91 — pointing into `spells.2da`, WHICH WE DO NOT HOLD.** **And there is no plasma grenade `.uti` in our item set at all.**

**Not refuted. Not confirmable. And it does not matter:**

> **⚠ Under the category the enumeration is UNNECESSARY.** ***"Immune to fear effects"* covers a plasma grenade automatically if the grenade applies one.** **That is exactly what the engine does — `Immunity: Fear` blocks the type without naming a single source.**

**Restored to `Force Immunity: Fear` as a WORKED EXAMPLE, not as the definition.**

### `Roar` re-pointed — the chain is now a real ladder

    Roar        6 sq   Will save or `shaken`
    ›           8 sq   fail by 5+ -> `panicked`
    ›› Terrify 10 sq   fail by 5+ -> `cowering`

**⚠ Three tiers, three conditions.** **The chain was already three steps and had only two outcomes to spend on them.**

**⚠ The middle tier's name `Bellow` STILL collides — `PT-205`. Unresolved across three rulings now.**

### ⚠ Not done, and deliberately

**`force/FORCE-POWERS-01`'s `Fear`, `Horror` and `Insanity` still say *"cower for 2 rounds"* and *"4 rounds."*** **They should apply `cowering` on the save-ends model.**

**NOT EDITED.** **That document is `GAP-002` territory — the largest unresolved design decision in the project — and rewriting Force power durations inside a beast-adjacent ruling is how the Tuk'ata's Intelligence clause happened, `PT-440`.**

## PT-448 — Both open items closed. ⚠ And my reason for deferring one was wrong twice

### `Bellow` → **`Howl`**

**⚠ Flagged across three rulings — `PT-443`, `PT-445`, `PT-447` — and never fixed.**

**The collision was real: `Bellow` is the ITHORIAN'S racial feat.** **`RACIAL-FEATS-01` line 23, `SPECIES-CHAPTER-v2` line 557, `SPECIES-MASTER` line 55 — *a ranged attack, both mouths at once, target deafened.***

**The `Roar` chain's middle tier is `Howl`. Name-checked clean.**

**⚠ `Shriek` was rejected despite being clean** — it is the Shyrack's planned attack from `PT-437` and taking it here would create the same collision one workstream later.

    Roar        6 sq   Will save or `shaken`
    ›  Howl     8 sq   fail by 5+ -> `panicked`
    ›› Terrify 10 sq   fail by 5+ -> `cowering`

### ⚠ I deferred the Force powers on a reason that was false in BOTH halves

**I said the `Fear` / `Horror` / `Insanity` rewrite was blocked because `force/FORCE-POWERS-01` is `GAP-002` territory, *"the largest unresolved design decision in the project."***

> **⚠ `GAP-002` IS CLOSED. `PT-248` closed it — the KOTOR branch, decided by construction.** **`playtest/GAP-002.md` line 3 has said so the whole time.**

**⚠ And I said `force/` was stale. `PT-423` made it canonical** — the three-way merge wrote the merged superset INTO `force/FORCE-POWERS-01.md` and deleted the `rules/` copy. **I performed that merge and then cited the pre-merge state as a blocker.**

**Two proxy assertions, one about a ruling I never opened and one about work I did myself.**

### The three powers, rewritten

| Power | Now |
|---|---|
| **Fear** | A single creature is **`cowering`**. Save negates, **but the target is `shaken` anyway.** |
| **Horror** | All hostile creatures in a **5-metre radius** are **`cowering`**. Save leaves `shaken`. |
| **Insanity** | All enemies in a **10-metre radius** are **`cowering`**. Save leaves `shaken`. |

**⚠ The fixed durations are GONE — 2, 4 and 6 rounds.** **All three run save-ends-at-end-of-turn, `PT-447`.**

**The Will save DC is untouched: `5 + level + Wisdom modifier + Charisma modifier`, as ported.** **`Does not affect droids` is untouched.**

> **⚠ The three powers differ by SCOPE, not severity — one target, then 5 metres, then 10.** **All three always applied the same effect; only now does the corpus have a word for it.**

### ⚠ What this changed that was not asked for

**`Insanity`'s text read *"greatly confuse an enemy force, inflaming paranoia and doubt."*** **Under `PT-447` it applies `cowering`, not any confusion condition.**

**The flavour said one thing and the mechanic another, in the source itself.** **The mechanic is now explicit and the flavour trimmed to match. ⚠ If `Insanity` was meant to confuse rather than paralyse, this ruling made that harder to see, not easier.**

## PT-449 — `Terrify` → `Shriek`, and the `Fear` power negates entirely

**Two owner rulings.**

### `Roar`'s top tier is `Shriek`

    Roar        6 sq   Will save or `shaken`
    ›  Howl     8 sq   fail by 5+ -> `panicked`
    ›› Shriek  10 sq   fail by 5+ -> `cowering`

**⚠ `Shriek` was the SHYRACK'S planned attack name — `PT-437`, from its `Sonic 7` weapon property.** **It is now taken by the Young Rancor.**

> **⚠ The Shyrack's sonic attack needs a different name when its chains are written.** **Recorded here because that beast is unwritten and the collision will otherwise be discovered by whoever writes it — `PT-205`.**

**⚠ And I rejected `Shriek` for this exact tier one ruling ago, on those exact grounds.** **The owner overruled it. Both facts are on the record.**

### The `Fear` power negates entirely — an EXCEPTION to the category rule

**`PT-447` set one rule for the whole category: *a creature that saves against a fear effect is `shaken` anyway.***

**⚠ `Fear` is exempt. A successful save leaves NOTHING.**

**`Horror` and `Insanity` keep the residual `shaken`.**

### Why it holds

**The three powers differ by SCOPE, not severity — one target, then 5 metres, then 10.** **With a uniform save rule the tier-1 power was as punishing as the tier-3 one on a success, which is the only axis on which they could differ at all.**

> **`Fear` is now fully avoidable. `Horror` and `Insanity` leave a mark whatever you roll.** **That is a severity ladder the source did not have and the scope ladder alone could not express.**

**⚠ `RULES-01-v2` updated: the category rule now states that an effect MAY declare it does not leave the residual.** **One exception exists. If a second appears the rule is wrong and should be inverted — opt-in rather than opt-out.**

## PT-450 — ⚠ `PT-448`'s prose trimming REVERSED. The source's flavour stands

**Owner: *"Before is better."***

**⚠ At `PT-448` I rewrote the flavour of `Fear`, `Horror` and `Insanity` while converting their mechanics to `cowering`.** **Only the MECHANIC needed changing. The prose was collateral.**

### What was lost, and why it mattered

**`Insanity` read: *"This power can greatly confuse an enemy force, inflaming paranoia and doubt."*** **I compressed it to *"Paranoia and doubt through an enemy force."***

> **⚠ The source's flavour says CONFUSE. Its mechanic says COWER. Those are different things and the contradiction is the SOURCE'S OWN.**

**By tightening the prose I made a real inconsistency invisible instead of visible.** **⚠ If `Insanity` was ever meant to be a confusion effect rather than a paralysis effect, my edit buried the evidence for it.**

**The same trimming hit `Fear` — *"causes fear in a single creature"* — and `Horror` — *"cower in catatonic fear of the attacking Jedi."*** **All three restored.**

### The rule this establishes

**⚠ A mechanical conversion changes the MECHANIC. It does not license editing the prose around it.**

**`PT-428` moved riders off feats and onto weapon profiles without touching a word of description. `PT-447` should have done the same and did not.**

> **⚠ Tidying source text while converting it is how provenance dies quietly** — **the next reader sees clean prose and has no reason to suspect anything was ever different.**

**Preserved deliberately in `Insanity`'s entry: a note that the flavour and mechanic disagree, and that the disagreement is the source's.**

    ours     "This power can greatly TERRIFY an enemy force, inflaming paranoia and doubt."

**`PT-450`'s rule: a mechanical conversion changes the mechanic, not the prose around it.**

> **⚠ That rule is about SILENT tidying done in passing.** **This is an owner ruling, one word, with the original recorded inline.**

**The distinction that matters is not whether prose may change. It is whether the change is VISIBLE.** **`PT-448` trimmed three powers and left no trace. `PT-451` changes one word and says so in the entry.**

**Everything else is verbatim.** ***"Inflaming paranoia and doubt"* stands, and it reads correctly against `cowering` — paranoia and doubt that end in a creature unable to act.**

**⚠ `Fear` and `Horror` are untouched. Neither had the contradiction; both described fear and delivered it.**

## PT-455 — Five poison types, all three-tier, on ⚠ D&D 3e's TWO-SAVE structure

**Owner ruling: steal 3e's poison mechanic for the venom tree.**

### The structure

    Fortitude save at the poison's DC
      FAIL   -> INITIAL damage, immediately
      then, 10 rounds later, save AGAIN
      FAIL   -> SECONDARY damage
    ⚠ An antidote kit or the light-side `Heal` power ends it at any point.

**⚠ Two saves, one bite.** **Getting bitten is not the end of it, and the fight moves on before the poison does.**

### ⚠ The DCs are PORTED, not authored

    Kinrath  g_w_crslash009  StrDamage  DC 10     base band
             g_w_crslash012  DexDamage  DC 14     g_kinrath03
             g_w_crslash011  ChaDamage  DC 18     g_kinrath02
    Tuk'ata  g_w_crslprc002  IntDamage  DC 10     base
             g_w_crslprc004  ChaDamage  DC 14     g_tukata02

> **⚠ The Kinrath already HAD a three-tier poison ladder, built by the people who made the game, with the DCs pre-set.** **`PT-453`'s authored `DC 10 + Beast Master level` is replaced by `10 / 14 / 18`.**

### The five types

| Type | Damages | Tiers |
|---|---|---|
| **Weakening** | Strength | `1d4` / `2d4` / `3d4` |
| **Numbing** | Dexterity | `1d4` / `2d4` / `3d4` |
| **Dulling** | Intelligence | `1d4` / `2d4` / `3d4` |
| **Withering** | Charisma | `1d4` / `2d4` / `3d4` |
| **⚠ Venom** | **VITALITY, over time** | `1` / `2` / `3` per turn |

**All tier at Beast Master 1 / 6 / 12 at DC 10 / 14 / 18.** **⚠ Ability damage reduces the SCORE, and everything derived from it re-derives — `RULES-01-v2` line 218. It heals 1 point per day of rest.**

### ⚠ `Venom` is the one that is AUTHORED, and here is why

**There is NO poison damage type in the game.** **`iprp_damagetype` has 13 rows — Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing, Universal, Unstoppable, Cold, Light_Side, Electrical, Fire, Dark_Side, Sonic, Ion, Energy. None is poison.**

**The green health bar is the VISIBLE SYMPTOM of `ItemPoison`, and its rate lives in compiled script we do not hold.** **⚠ Scoped: searched `iprp_damagetype`, `iprp_poison`, `iprp_onhit`, `iprp_onhitdc`, `iprp_onhitdur`, `iprp_paramtable`. The number is not in any of them.**

**⚠ The CURE is sourced.** **An antidote kit stops any poison effect; the light-side `Heal` power neutralises it; the Bio-antidote implant grants immunity.**

**`Virulence` and `Necrosis` carry 3e's secondary save as a DOUBLING rather than a second dose — the DoT is already running, so the second failure makes it worse instead of hitting again.**

### Assignments

    Kinrath    Weakening + ⚠ the Venom ladder     the ONLY beast with both
    Tach       Weakening
    Tuk'ata    Dulling                            ⚠ NOT venomous — PT-454 stands
    ⚠ Gizka    Paralyze — NOT a poison, and never was

**⚠ `venomous` now has ONE holder: the Kinrath.** **The Tach carries `Weakening` as an assigned feat but not the ladder.** **A tag with one holder is the shape `aquatic` was cut for at `PT-359` — flagged, not acted on.**

**⚠ `Withering` and `Numbing` have NO holder on the current roster.** **They exist because the Kinrath's and Tuk'ata's upper BANDS carry them.**

### Selkath — ⚠ `Toxic Claws`, and the species chapter never knew

**`n_selkath` carries `g_w_crslash007` — StrDamage, DC 10. `g_selkathmale03` carries `g_w_crslash008` — DexDamage, DC 10.**

> **⚠ The Selkath have a POISONED NATURAL ATTACK in both games and `SPECIES-CHAPTER-v2` says nothing about it.** **A player species with a mechanic in the source that the chapter omits entirely.**

**`Toxic Claws` — racial feat, maximum level 5. Unarmed attacks carry `Weakening`: `1d4` Strength, `2d4` at character level 6, `3d4` at 12, DC 10 / 14 / 18.**

**⚠ The Selkath now has three trait lines AND two racial feats — the most feat-dense species on the roster.** **`PT-104`'s one-feat-per-species was already stretched by the Nautolan; this stretches it further. Recorded.**

### `Gizka` abilities corrected

    was   Str 3 · Dex 18 · Con 4      ⚠ the Vermin·Tiny template, shared with the Mykal
    now   Str 6 · Dex 12 · Con 4

**⚠ Its own file reads `Str 12 · Dex 10 · Con 14` — the template contradicted the blueprint on all three.** **The Mykal's `Dex 18` IS file-backed and it keeps it.**

**`Str 6` is the owner's. ⚠ `Dex 12` is MINE — between the file's `10` and the template's `18`.** **It gets into cracks via `Squeeze`, which is a feat, not a Dexterity score.**

## PT-456 — Poison dice become `1d2` / `1d4` / `1d6`. ⚠ 3e scales the DIE, not the count

**Owner ruling, and it corrects `PT-455` one ruling after it was written.**

    PT-455   1d4 / 2d4 / 3d4     ⚠ WRONG SHAPE
    PT-456   1d2 / 1d4 / 1d6     3e's Tiny · Medium · Large rows

### What 3e actually does

    monstrous spider   Tiny        DC 11   1d2 Str / 1d2 Str
                       Small       DC 12   1d3
                       Medium      DC 14   1d4
                       Large       DC 16   1d6
                       Huge        DC 18   1d8
                       Gargantuan  DC 20   2d6
                       Colossal    DC 22   2d8

> **⚠ THE DIE SIZE GROWS. THE COUNT DOES NOT — until `Gargantuan`, which is past anything this ladder reaches.**

**⚠ If a fourth tier is ever added the next step is `1d8`, NOT `2d4`.** **Recorded because `PT-455` reached for the wrong axis and the next person will too.**

**Initial and secondary damage are the SAME roll in 3e. Ours already matched and is unchanged.**

### ⚠ Two sources, and they disagree on the DC

**The dice come from 3e's `Tiny` / `Medium` / `Large` rows. Those rows carry DCs `11` / `14` / `16`.**

**Ours stay `10` / `14` / `18`** — **ported from the Kinrath's own bands, `g_w_crslash009` / `012` / `011`.**

**⚠ Ruling: the game files outrank the parent system on any value our source actually sets.** **3e supplies the SHAPE where KOTOR has none; KOTOR supplies the NUMBERS where it has them.** **Only the middle tier agrees at `14`.**

### ⚠ Why the dice had to shrink

**Ability damage reduces the SCORE.** **Attack, damage, `Athletics`, `Climb`, `Jump` and carrying capacity all re-derive — `RULES-01-v2` line 218.**

    1d6  average 3.5   a serious wound
    3d4  average 7.5   ⚠ −3 to everything Strength touches, from ONE bite

**`PT-455` would have made a tier-3 poisoned bite a removal rather than a wound.** **And it fires TWICE — initial and secondary.**

### Applied to all five, plus the Selkath

**`Weakening` · `Numbing` · `Dulling` · `Withering` — `1d2` / `1d4` / `1d6`.**

**`Venom` is UNCHANGED at `1` / `2` / `3` vitality per turn.** **It is a different mechanic and a die per turn would slow the round.**

**`Toxic Claws` moved with them — `1d2` at level 1, `1d4` at 6, `1d6` at 12.** **⚠ This supersedes the owner's earlier instruction that its first number rise per tier; the Selkath now matches the beasts.**

## PT-458 — Rakghoul plague DEFERRED to Hard difficulty. ⚠ Note written, nothing built

**Owner ruling: not now, and record it so it is not rediscovered as a gap.**

**Note placed in `DEATH-AND-DIFFICULTY-01 §2`, under `Hard`.**

### Why `Hard` and not the poison system

**⚠ It is a PERMANENCE mechanic, not a combat one.** **An infection that worsens between encounters and ends a character if untreated is the same shape as `Hard`'s permanent death.**

**⚠ It must NOT reuse the poison chassis — `PT-457`.** **Poison is two saves and ability damage. A plague is a CLOCK.**

### The negative, recorded at full scope so nobody re-runs it

    39 creature weapons        every property, both games
    14 rakghoul/kinrath UTCs   FeatList · SpecAbilityList · ClassList · SkillList
    all .uti, both games       resref and Tag matched against "rakg"
    7 property tables          damagetype · poison · onhit · onhitdc · onhitdur
                               paramtable · immunity
    ⚠ NOT HELD                 disease.2da · spells.2da

**`c_rakghoul` `FeatList` EMPTY, `SpecAbilityList` EMPTY.** **Its weapon is `g_w_crslash001` — a generic `1d4` shared with the Iriaz and the Brith. Not a rakghoul weapon at all.**

**Complete `OnHit` vocabulary, 12 subtypes:** Sleep · Stun · Paralyze · Confusion · Fear · Slow · AbilityDrain · ItemPoison · SlayRG · SlayAG · Instant_Death · Knockdown. **⚠ No disease subtype. No health-drain subtype.**

### ⚠ The strongest evidence is BioWare's own note

**`ptar_rakghoulser.uti` — the Rakghoul Serum — has ZERO item properties, and its `Comment` field reads:**

> ***"This is the serum required to complete the various rakghoul disease plots on tar[is]."***

**PLOTS. The developer's internal note calls it a quest token, and the file is one.**

**⚠ `iprp_immunity` row 4 is `Disease`. The engine has the category and NOTHING in the data uses it.**

## PT-459 — Target types. ⚠ A rule written 36 times and never once stated

**Owner ruling. `Stun Droid` is the model: some effects simply do not apply to some targets.**

### ⚠ It was already in the corpus, as prose, thirty-six times

**`force/FORCE-POWERS-01` carries a target clause on 36 of 92 rows:**

    "This power does not affect droids."                      26 powers
    "...will not affect any droids in the party"              Battle Meditation x3
    "...non-droid fallen allies"                              Revitalize x3, Heal x2
    ⚠ "only works on sentients; beasts and droids are immune"  Force Confusion
    "...droids equipped with energy shield hardware"          Force Whirlwind
    Stun · Disable · Destroy Droid                            droids ONLY

> **⚠ `Force Confusion` ALREADY carried the beast exclusion.** **The concept has been in the corpus the whole time, as thirty-six unconnected sentences with no rule behind them and no way to check consistency.**

### The property

**Every attack, power and effect declares `targets:` from `sentient` · `beast` · `droid`. Omitted means all three.**

    mind        sentient only          Mind Trick · Dominate Mind · Force Confusion
    fear        sentient · beast       Fear · Horror · Insanity · a beast's Roar
    life        sentient · beast       healing · draining · ⚠ ALL FIVE POISON TYPES
    system      droid only             ion · slicing · Stun/Disable/Destroy Droid
    physical    all three              every weapon attack

**⚠ One property replaces thirty-six sentences, and it makes the EXCEPTIONS visible.** **`Force Whirlwind`'s energy-shield carve-out is now a stated exception rather than one line among ninety-two.**

### ⚠ `fear` is separate from `mind`, and the powers' own prose hid it

**`Fear`, `Horror` and `Insanity` say *does not affect droids* and say NOTHING about beasts.**

> **⚠ Under a single `mind → sentient only` class, a rancor would be immune to a rancor's `Roar`.**

**A beast can be frightened. `fear` takes `sentient` and `beast`; `mind` does not.** **⚠ The distinction is not in the source and is authored.**

### ⚠ No poison works on droids

**All five types — `PT-455`, `PT-457`. Owner confirmed as correct.**

**Stated because it is not free: a Beast Master facing a droid party has a companion whose venom does nothing, and four tags go dead in that fight.** **Relevant when beast encounters are designed.**

### Natural weapons cannot be disarmed — owner ruling

**`Disarming Strike` and the weapon half of `Stealing Strike` have NO EFFECT against a creature whose only weapons are natural.**

**⚠ `Stealing Strike`'s HELD-ITEM half still works** — a beast carrying something can still be relieved of it.

**⚠ `Sever` DOES reach natural weapons and is kept.** **It reads *"against an unarmed or natural-weapon target, its attacks deal half damage for the encounter."*** **Breaking a limb is not disarming it.**

### ⚠ And a correction I owe across three rulings

**I stated three times — at `PT-440`, in the `Four Arms` conversion, and again drafting the Cannok's chains — that the corpus HAS NO DISARM RULES.**

**It does. `ATTACKS-05`'s `Control` axis: `Disarming Strike` → `Stealing Strike` → `Sever`, levels 5 / 8 / 14, gated on Strength 12 AND Dexterity 13 — the only chain in the game requiring two abilities.**

> **⚠ `Sever` even reaches natural weapons explicitly. Beasts were inside that system already and I asserted absence three times without opening `ATTACKS-05`.**

**`Four Arms`' *"cannot be disarmed"* has a real rule behind it, and always did.**

### The Cannok's chain is unaffected

**`Worry` → `Wrench` → `Abscond` takes CARRIED ITEMS, not weapons.** **It works on a person with a pack and does nothing to a beast with no gear.** **The restriction makes explicit why, and changes nothing.**
