## PT-460 — `Roar` IS the fear ladder. Heal confirmed `life`. Disarm gated on a held object

**Three owner rulings.**

### `Roar` stops inventing outcomes and casts the powers

| Tier | Level | Power | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Roar** | 1 | **`Fear`** | one target within 6 squares |
| › **Howl** | 4 | **`Horror`** | 5-metre radius around a target within 8 squares |
| ›› **Dread** | 8 | **`Insanity`** | 10-metre radius around a target within 10 squares |

    Force power    DC 5 + level + Wisdom modifier + Charisma modifier
    ⚠ Roar chain   DC 12 + Beast Master level

**⚠ Slightly harder, and deliberately.** **A Jedi's DC rides TWO ability modifiers; `PT-455` set the beast convention as no ability modifier at all.** **`+12` flat against `+5` plus two modifiers puts a beast roughly two points ahead of a Jedi of the same level.**

**⚠ `Fear`'s exception carries across: a save against the first tier negates entirely, no residual `shaken` — `PT-449`.** **`Howl` and `Dread` leave the residual, as `Horror` and `Insanity` do.**

### ⚠ And the save-margin ladder is GONE

**`PT-443` escalated by failing a save by 5 or more.** **The powers do not work that way and now neither does this.**

> **The escalation is SCOPE — one target, then a 5-metre radius, then 10 — exactly as `Fear` → `Horror` → `Insanity` escalate.**

**⚠ Two rulings' worth of authored machinery removed.** **The chain now has NOTHING of its own except the DC.**

### `Heal` is `life` — confirmed, and it was already right

**Owner ruling. Audited every healing-family row in `force/FORCE-POWERS-01`:**

    Heal · Improved Heal · Master Heal              droid clause ✓
    Revitalize · Improved · Master Revitalize       droid clause ✓
    Drain Life                                      droid clause ✓

**⚠ Seven of seven already excluded droids.** **`PT-459`'s `life` class was correct and is now named explicitly in the table rather than implied by *"healing."***

### Disarm gated on a held object

**⚠ Reworded from `PT-459`.** **It read *"no effect against a creature whose only weapons are natural"* — which is nearly right and turns on the wrong thing.**

> **A disarm applies ONLY if the target is holding something that is not a natural weapon.** **No held object, no disarm.**

**⚠ The difference matters.** **The old wording asked what the creature IS; the new one asks what it is HOLDING.** **A beast carrying a satchel is disarmable of the satchel. A person who has dropped their blaster is not disarmable at all.**

**`Sever` is untouched and still reaches natural weapons — breaking a limb is not disarming it.**

## PT-461 — Force DC formulas audited. ⚠ Three variants are DELIBERATE; the transcriptions are not

**Owner approved `Roar`'s `DC 12 + Beast Master level` and confirmed the `Force Scream` and `Afflict`/`Plague` formulas as intentional.**

### The standard, and it is the GAME'S OWN TEXT

    5 + the attacking character's level + Wisdom modifier + Charisma modifier

**29 of 92 rows. ⚠ Transcribed from the in-game power descriptions — rank 1.**

### ⚠ What I could NOT verify

**Whether the game's DESCRIPTION matches the game's CODE.**

> **The DC lives in `spells.2da`, which is NOT in holdings** — the same wall as the grenades' `CastSpell` indices and `FORCE_IMMUNITY_FEAR`'s empty `spellid`.

**KOTOR descriptions are not reliably faithful to implementation.** **The formula is the game's STATED DC. It is not verified as the game's ACTUAL DC.** **Recorded so nobody later reports it as file-verified.**

### The three divergences — ⚠ DELIBERATE, owner confirmed

    Force Scream · Improved · Master     10 + level + Wis + Cha    five points higher
    Afflict · Plague                     5 + FORCE LEVELS + Wis + Cha
    Beast Trick                          5 + level, ⚠ no ability modifiers at all

**⚠ `Afflict` and `Plague` scale off FORCE levels, not character level.** **For a multiclassed character those are different numbers.** **Owner: deliberate. Closed.**

### ⚠ The one thing still worth fixing

**The standard formula is worded THREE ways across 29 rows:**

    18  "5 + the attacking character's level + the attacking character's Wisdom and Charisma..."
     8  "5 + the attacking character's level + attacking character's Wisdom and Charisma..."
     3  "5 + the attacker's level + attacker's Wisdom and Charisma modifiers"

**One formula, three transcriptions.** **⚠ Harmless to a reader and INVISIBLE to any check that greps for it** — a normalisation pass would let `audit_refs` or a successor verify DC consistency mechanically. **Not done. Flagged.**

### `Roar`'s DC, checked against a Jedi

    level  4    Jedi 5+4+3+3 = 15     Roar 12+4  = 16     +1
    level 10    Jedi 5+10+3+3 = 21    Roar 12+10 = 22     +1
    level 16    Jedi 5+16+3+3 = 27    Roar 12+16 = 28     +1

**Consistently one point ahead of a Jedi at `Wisdom +3 / Charisma +3`.**

> **⚠ Against a LOW-Wisdom Jedi the gap widens to `+7`; against a maxed `+5/+5` the beast falls `+3` behind.** **The beast is STABLE where the Jedi is VARIABLE, which is the right relationship — and it exists because `PT-455` ruled beasts use no ability modifier.**

**⚠ Matching the game exactly would read `5 + Beast Master level + Wis + Cha` — and beast Wisdom and Charisma are mostly 10 or lower, which would put every beast well BELOW a Jedi.** **The flat `+12` is the compensation.**

## PT-462 — `Beast Trick` → `Beast Control`. ⚠ And our `k2_dialog.tlk` appears to be MODDED

### The rename and the restrictions

**Owner ruling. Renamed across 7 live documents.** **⚠ `comms/REPLY-LIBRARIAN-05.md` was reverted — sent correspondence is a record, `PT-434`, `PT-444`.**

**`Beast Control`** — **`targets: beast`, `PT-459`.** **⚠ And the DC is CORRECTED.**

    our entry     DC 5 + the attacking character's level
    ⚠ the source  DC 5 + level + Wisdom modifier + Charisma modifier

> **⚠ `PT-461` recorded `Beast Trick`'s missing modifiers as a DELIBERATE variant and the owner confirmed it as intentional.** **It was a TRANSCRIPTION LOSS. The source has both modifiers.** **My question was framed as *is this deliberate* and the answer given was about `Force Scream` and `Afflict`, which ARE deliberate. This one was not, and I did not separate them.**

**`Beast Confusion`** — **prerequisites `Any Prestige Class` + `Beast Control`; the beast fights for you 10 rounds; ⚠ only ONE beast at a time; ⚠ only the MAIN CHARACTER may select it.**

**⚠ Its restriction is stated VERBATIM in the source: *"This power only works on beasts; sentients and droids are immune."*** **A third source instance of `PT-459`'s target-type property, after `Force Confusion` and the droid clauses.**

### ⚠⚠ PROVENANCE ALARM — the K2 string table carries content that is almost certainly a MOD

**Swept `k2_dialog.tlk` for power descriptions: 151 found against our 88 powers.**

**⚠ A contiguous block at strrefs `136376`–`136522` — roughly 70 powers — sits at the very TAIL of a 136,551-entry table and does not look like KOTOR 2:**

    Force Immortality · Doppelganger · Shatterpoint · Resonance
    Deep Resonance · Master Resonance · Force Incinerate · Force Bombard
    Spear of Midnight Black · Arrow of White Dawn · Leech Life Force
    Sith Alchemy: Create Life I / II · Sith Alchemy: Transform

**⚠ Prerequisites of *"Level 21"*, *"Level 24"*, *"Level 26"*, *"Level 30"* — and a *"Jedimaster"* typo.**

> **⚠ Appending new strrefs to the END of `dialog.tlk` is exactly how TSLPatcher installs a mod.**

**⚠ AND IT AFFECTS SOMETHING I ALREADY REPORTED.** **Last message I offered `Sith Alchemy: Create Life` — strref `136504` — as *"a fourth power in the family we don't have,"* citing its line that `Beast Control` makes a Sithspawn less likely to disobey.** **⚠ WITHDRAWN. That is almost certainly mod content and I presented it as rank-1 source.**

**⚠ Strref `136370` reads *"Poison, 4 pts every 3 sec"* — a poison damage-over-time.** **If that block is a mod, it is NOT evidence that vanilla KOTOR has poison DoT, and `PT-457`'s finding stands: the games have no health-drain poison.** **A DeadlyStream mod adding poison weapons to TSL surfaced in an earlier search, which fits.**

### ⚠ What this means going forward

**⚠ `k1_dialog.tlk` at 49,369 entries shows no comparable block and its `Beast Control` matches are ZERO — consistent with `POWER-COSTS-01`'s ruling that these powers are not in a KOTOR 1 package.**

### ⚠ And my name-pairing heuristic was unreliable

**I paired each description with the nearest short string above it. It returned `Change Card Value`, `tr_hssiss` and `[Fade to Black.]` as power names.**

## PT-463 — The mod block, batch 1. `Shutdown` ADOPTED · `Resonance`, `Force Hold`, `Sith Alchemy` REJECTED

**⚠ First, a data correction.** **The mod block uses TWO layouts and I reported the wrong one.**

    136375–136437   name / description ALTERNATING     ✓ pairs correctly
    ⚠ 136440–136452 names GROUPED, then descriptions    cannot be aligned
    136453–136522   alternating again                  ✓ pairs correctly

**⚠ `Force Hold` came back carrying `Force Strike`'s text because of this.** **Every name reported from the grouped section is suspect until re-derived; the rest of the block is sound.**

### ADOPTED — `Shutdown` → `Overload`

**Owner ruling: add it, with a way for the power to FAIL, and make `Overload` a high-level unlock whose failure falls back to shutting the item down.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **`Shutdown`** | T1, FP 6, DSP −1. One blaster or vibro-cell weapon within 10 metres. **Will save at the standard DC or the weapon is inert for 10 rounds.** |
| **`› Overload`** | T3, FP 20, DSP −2, **Character Level 15**. **Destroys** the weapon; `1d6` per two character levels within 2 squares, Reflex for half. |

**⚠ THE FAILURE MECHANISM — `+2` to the save per filled upgrade slot.** **A well-maintained cell is harder to bleed, and it ties the power to a system we already have rather than a flat percentage.**

**⚠ `Overload` takes a FURTHER `+4`, and on a successful save it does NOT fizzle — the weapon is inert for 10 rounds instead.** **Owner ruling. The bigger power degrades to the smaller one rather than wasting 20 Force points.**

**⚠ Lightsabers are immune** — the source says *blaster or vibration-cell*, and a lightsaber crystal is not a power cell being bled.

**⚠ `targets: sentient · droid` — `PT-459`. A beast holds nothing.**

### REJECTED — `Resonance` · `Deep Resonance` · `Master Resonance`

**Not Legends. Nothing lets a Jedi borrow a companion's attributes.** **⚠ Invented, and not Star Wars-shaped — it is MMO party synergy.**

> **⚠ And it is worse in OUR system than in K2.** **`RULES-01-v2` line 218 re-derives attack, damage, saves, skills, Defence, carrying capacity and vitality from an ability score.** **`Master Resonance` raising EVERY score to the party's best is a blanket buff to the whole sheet from one power.**

### REJECTED — `Force Hold`

**Era-appropriate in principle. ⚠ We already have it TWICE — `Force Stasis` and `Force Stasis Field`, both ported from the game proper.** **A duplicate under a third name, `PT-205`.**

### CUT — `Sith Alchemy: Create Life` I / II / `Transform`

**Owner ruling. ⚠ And it closes a retraction: at `PT-462` I withdrew my citation of `Create Life`'s *"Beast Control makes disobedience less likely"* line, which I had offered as a game power interaction. Mod content, now cut outright.**

### ⚠ Not everything in the block is invented

**`Deadly Sight` — strref `136517` — is a REAL Star Wars game power, from *Dark Forces II: Jedi Knight* and *Mysteries of the Sith*.**

**The block must be judged case by case. Dismissing it wholesale would have discarded attested material.**

## PT-464 — `Deadly Sight` ADOPTED. ⚠ Real Legends power, and the canon fixed the mod's mechanics

**Owner ruling: adopt with a fixed cost, and gate it behind `Force Sight`.**

    Deadly Sight   Dark · T3 · FP 24 · DSP −6
    Prerequisites  Sith Lord or Sith Assassin · Character Level 15 · ⚠ Force Sight

**Every creature in the user's line of sight within 10 metres takes `1d6` per two character levels, Fortitude for half.**

**⚠ ALLIES AND BYSTANDERS ARE INCLUDED. There is no way to exclude them.**

**⚠ `targets: sentient · beast` — `PT-459`. It burns flesh; droids are unaffected.**

### A — the era check, and it passes

**Wookieepedia: once an EXTREMELY RARE ability, even among the Sith; its usage exploded only in the last decades of the New Sith Wars.**

**⚠ The New Sith Wars ended around 1000 BBY — roughly three thousand years AFTER 3956 BBY.** **The spread is far downstream of us; the wording places the technique itself well before it.**

> **At our era it is a rare, ancient Sith technique — exactly the register for a prestige-gated dark-side power.** **The named practitioners — Sariss at 5 ABY — are the tail of its history, not its origin.**

**⚠ SOURCE CAUTION: the Saga Edition wiki entry is headed *"Homebrew Reference Book: Dark Forces Campaign Guide."*** **Homebrew, NOT citable — the same trap as the drexl's apex claim at `PT-443`.**

### B — ⚠ the canon supplied what the mod description omitted

**The mod text says only *"brings death and destruction to anyone seen by the caster"* and *"FP cost may vary."***

**Wookieepedia adds the two things that make it workable:**

**⚠ IT HITS ALLIES.** **The power injured everyone the user looked at, including allies and civilians, and it is unrecorded whether it could ever be refined.** **That is friendly fire IN CANON, and it is the single thing that makes the power balanceable — free area damage becomes a real decision.**

**The inefficiency is canon too** — tiring to sustain, and a heavy strain on the user's Force reserves. **The mod's variable cost was reaching for something real.**

### ⚠ Why the cost is FIXED and not variable

**`FORCE-POOL-01-v3` computes a pool against FIXED costs.** **A power that prices itself at cast time breaks the one assumption the pool system makes.**

**The canon inefficiency is expressed as a HIGH FLAT cost — `FP 24`, the second-highest on the roster — rather than a scaling one.** **⚠ Flavour lost, architecture kept. Recorded as a deliberate departure.**

### `Force Sight` as a prerequisite — owner ruling

**⚠ You cannot kill with a glare you cannot aim.**

**`Force Sight` is `Character Level 3`, Universal, and ⚠ NOTABLE — it cannot be bought at level-up by anyone but a Miraluka; everyone else must be TAUGHT it.**

> **⚠ That makes `Deadly Sight` conditional on a power with an unusual acquisition path, which narrows it further than the prestige gate alone.** **Consistent with *"extremely rare, even among the Sith."***

### ⚠ And the sequencing was right

**I nearly rejected this power for being from a 1997 game set in 5 ABY.** **The lookup showed the technique predates its famous users by three millennia.**

**A real power in the wrong millennium is still an anachronism — but so is rejecting an ancient technique because its famous practitioner is late.** **`PT-462`'s rule holds: judge the block case by case.**

## PT-465 — One dark tree becomes two. `Force Sleep` added. Three mod powers rejected

**Owner rulings.**

### ⚠ `Force Slow → Afflict → Plague` was ONE tree. It is now TWO

    was    Force Slow -> Afflict -> Plague
    now    Force Slow -> Force Mire -> Force Root          the SLOW tree
           Force Affliction -> Force Contagion -> Force Plague   the DISEASE tree

**⚠ Two mechanics were sharing a ladder.** **`Force Slow` is a movement and accuracy debuff; `Afflict` and `Plague` are ability-score poison.** **Nothing but the tree bound them.**

### The slow tree

| Tier | | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| **Force Slow** | T1, FP 6 | `−2` Defence, Reflex, attack. 10 rounds. Will negates. |
| › **Force Mire** | T2, FP 12 | Speed **halved**, no second move. `−4` Defence, Reflex, attack. |
| ›› **Force Root** | T3, FP 18 | **Cannot move at all.** `−6` Defence and Reflex. |

**⚠ `Force Root` is NOT paralysis — owner ruling.** **The target may still attack anything already within its reach, and is attacked normally.** **It is pinned, not helpless.**

### The disease tree

**`Afflict` → `Force Affliction`. `Plague` → `Force Plague`. ⚠ New middle tier `Force Contagion`, at four points from each physical attribute — between `Force Affliction`'s seven on one target and `Force Plague`'s twelve, and hitting a 2-square spread.**

**⚠ The rename is closer to the source: the game's own text reads *"Affliction causes a target to suffer as though poisoned."*** **We had shortened it to `Afflict`.**

**⚠ The NAME `Force Contagion` is taken from the mod block. The numbers are ours.** **The mod's version was `DC 100`, 20 damage and `−1` to ALL SIX abilities every 6 seconds — a no-save character-ender. Rejected as written, `PT-464`.**

**⚠ And its own text is a FIFTH source instance of `PT-459`: *"Creatures immune to poisons, like droids, are unaffected."***

### `Force Sleep` — added despite being a near-duplicate

**Owner ruling: NWN's `Sleep`, longer than `Force Stasis`, and breakable.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Force Sleep** | Light, T2, FP 14, DSP −3. Character Level 9, `Force Stun`. |
| | 5-metre radius. Cannot act; attacks against them treat them as `helpless`. **10 rounds** — ⚠ against `Force Stasis`'s four. |
| | **⚠ ANY DAMAGE WAKES THEM**, and an adjacent ally may spend an action to wake one. |

> **⚠ That is the whole trade and it is why the duplicate is permitted.** **`Force Stasis` is short and reliable. `Force Sleep` is long and fragile — it ends the moment anyone touches the sleeper, which makes it a power you cast to LEAVE a fight rather than to win one.**

### REJECTED — `Force Immortality` · `Force Bombard` · `Force Contagion` (as written)

**`Force Immortality`** — **⚠ the NAME is the blocker.** **Nothing in Legends by that name does this; it is a party heal-over-time wearing a grand title.** **And `DC 50 − caster level` is a formula shape that exists NOWHERE in our corpus — every DC we have counts UP from 5 or 10.**

**`Force Bombard`** — **`1d4` per caster level per bolt, multiple bolts. ⚠ Absurd at our scale.**

> **⚠ But its STRUCTURE is the one genuinely novel thing in the mod block — a SUSTAINED power that fires repeatedly and blocks other sustains.** **We have no sustained-power mechanic at all. Recorded as a note, not adopted.**

**`Force Contagion` as written** — **`DC 100` is not a saving throw, it is a sentence saying *no save*.**

### ⚠ Renames swept

**`Afflict` → `Force Affliction` and `Plague` → `Force Plague` across `FORCE-POWERS-01`, `POWER-COSTS-01` and `cost_tables.md`.** **⚠ `comms/` excluded — sent correspondence is a record, `PT-434`, `PT-444`, `PT-462`.**

## PT-467 — The fire tree ADOPTED and rebalanced. `Force Static Field` ADOPTED

### ⚠ `Force Incinerate` was the TOP of a tree, not a single power

**I assessed it alone at `PT-464` and recommended rejection. The mod block holds all three tiers:**

    Force Enflame     Universal · Level 8   damage = caster level
    Force Combustion  Dark · Level 12       damage = 2x caster level
    Force Incinerate  Dark · Level 26       lift + burn

**⚠ The two lower tiers are ALREADY at our scale.** **`Force Enflame`'s *damage equal to the caster's level* is exactly what `Stun Droid` does.** **Only the capstone was broken, and I judged the tree by it.**

### The rebalance

| | Source | Ours |
|---|---|---|
| **Force Enflame** | damage = level, Fort negates | **unchanged** |
| **Force Combustion** | damage = 2× level, Fort negates | **unchanged** |
| **Force Incinerate** | ⚠ Level 26 · `1.5×` level every 2 s for 12 s · **no save** | **Level 18** · **`1d6` per four Force levels, max `6d6`**, at the start of each of its turns for **4 rounds** |

**⚠ The original was `9 ×` caster level — `234` damage at level 26.** **Ours caps at `6d6` a round over four rounds, average `84`** — level with `Force Choke` and `Destroy Droid` at `25d6`, which are the corpus ceiling.

**Level 26 → 18.** **⚠ Our prestige powers sit at 12–15; 26 is a level-50 game's number.**

### ⚠ *"Cannot be resisted"* is KEPT, and made to mean something

**Every other power in the corpus has a save. This one says it has none.**

> **Resolved: the INITIAL effect always lands — the source's own words — and a Fortitude save at the start of each of the target's turns ENDS IT EARLY.**

**⚠ The power cannot be dodged; it can be endured and shortened.** **That preserves the source's claim and gives counterplay, instead of choosing one and discarding the other.**

**And it is lifted off the ground: ⚠ the target CANNOT MOVE while burning** — the same shape as `Force Root` at `PT-465`, arrived at independently by the source.

### ⚠ One clause DROPPED

**`Force Enflame`: *"the victim may also suffer a temporary bout of insanity."***

**We have no insanity condition. `PT-447`'s fear ladder — `shaken` · `panicked` · `cowering` — is the wrong home for it, and `Insanity` is a POWER, not a condition.** **Dropped rather than mapped onto something it does not mean.**

### `Force Static Field` — ⚠ it fills a real hole

**Our entire anti-droid line SWITCHES DROIDS OFF:**

    Stun Droid     T1   immobile 4 rounds + damage
    Disable Droid  T2   area shutdown
    Destroy Droid  T3   area shutdown + 25d6

> **⚠ A power that turns a droid AGAINST ITS ALLIES is a different thing entirely, and it is LIGHT SIDE.** **The light-side answer to a droid is to subvert it rather than destroy it — which is a better statement than a fourth way to shut one down.**

**Light, T2, FP 14. Every droid within 4 metres: Will save or `confused` for 4 rounds — on each of its turns it attacks the nearest creature, ally or enemy.**

**⚠ `targets: droid` ONLY. `PT-459` handles it natively and the source states it: *"completely harmless to organic lifeforms."***

**⚠ The source offered a RANDOM choice of three outcomes — confused, shorted out, or sensor-blinded.** **Nothing in the corpus rolls on a table for its effect. We take one, and confusion is the one worth having.**

**⚠ And the mechanic already exists:** **the Selkath's `Acute Hearing` ends in *"the Selkath attacks the nearest creature, ally or enemy."*** **Same wording, deliberately.**

## PT-468 — `Force Incinerate` made resistible. Batch 3 REJECTED ENTIRELY. ⚠ And the axis the mod block fails on

### `Force Incinerate` — a full negate added

**Owner ruling.** **A Fortitude save at `DC 5 + level + Wisdom + Charisma` now NEGATES the cast entirely.** **The per-turn save to end early stands.**

**⚠ The source says the power *cannot be resisted* and that a Fortitude save merely halves the duration.** **`PT-467` preserved that and it was wrong.**

> **⚠ NOTHING IN THE CORPUS LANDS WITHOUT A SAVE.** **Preserving a source claim that breaks a universal invariant is not fidelity, it is importing a defect.**

### `Force Static Field` — adopted

**Light, T2, FP 14, DSP −3. Character Level 9, `Stun Droid`. `targets: droid` only.**

### Batch 3 — ⚠ ALL SIX REJECTED

| Power | Reason |
|---|---|
| **Force Strike** | `1d8` per caster level, **no save**, plus prone, plus area knockback. ⚠ The prone-and-knockback is `Power Attack`'s tier-3 shape in `ATTACKS-05` at a fraction of the cost. |
| **Force Weaken** | ⚠ **Percentage-of-current-vitality damage exists NOWHERE in the corpus.** Every damage figure we have is dice or a flat number. Half of whatever remains scales identically against a rakghoul and a rancor. `−10` is outside every modifier band. |
| **Force Chain Lightning** | ⚠ Owner: **`Force Storm` is already basically that.** `Force Storm` — Dark, T3, FP 24 — hits all hostiles within 10 metres for `1d6` per Force level to 20, then per two, max `25d6`. **The arcing is flavour on an effect we already have.** |
| **Force Sap Will** | ⚠ **WORD-FOR-WORD IDENTICAL to `Force Sleep`.** Same duration, same `−10`, same *cannot be resisted, Will save halves*. **The mod shipped one description under two names.** Already adopted as `Force Sleep` — `PT-465`. |
| **Force Freeze** | ⚠ A FOURTH immobiliser. `Force Stasis` holds, `Force Root` stops movement, `Force Sleep` makes helpless. *The `Cold` damage TYPE is unused — `iprp_damagetype` row 5 — but that is a weapon-property question, not a power.* |
| **Force Grip** | ⚠ Real and famous, and **we already have it twice** — `Force Choke` and `Force Strangle`, both ported from the game proper. `PT-205`. *No initial save, damage until you die* is the harshest thing in the block. |

### ⚠ The axis the block fails on, and it is not the numbers

**FOUR of these six say *"cannot be resisted."*** **`Force Strike` · `Force Weaken` · `Force Sap Will` · `Force Grip`.** **Two more in earlier batches: `Force Contagion` at `DC 100`, and `Force Incinerate`.**

> **⚠ The mod's design instinct at high level is to REMOVE THE SAVING THROW.** **Ours is the opposite — the owner has now twice put a save back onto a power I had ported without one.**

**That is a better rejection criterion than damage.** **Numbers rescale; a power built on the premise that the target gets no roll cannot be rescaled into a system where every effect gets one.**

### ⚠ And a duplicate-detection lesson

**`Force Sap Will` and `Force Sleep` are the same text under two names.** **`Force Grip` duplicates `Force Choke`. `Force Hold` duplicated `Force Stasis`. `Force Chain Lightning` duplicates `Force Storm`.**

**Four of the ~14 powers assessed so far are duplicates of something already on the roster.** **⚠ Check the roster BEFORE the lore — it is cheaper and it has caught more.**

## PT-470 — `blinded` DEFINED. `Force Blindness` adopted. ⚠ And `audit_grid` cannot see hyphenated distances

### ⚠ `blinded` was in the condition set and meant nothing

**It has been in `RULES-01-v2` line 343 since the set was written, with no defined effect, and THREE species traits already depend on it:**

    Miraluka `Second Sight`      cannot be blinded
    `Nictitating Membrane`       immune to blinding by light, sand, smoke, spray
    Togruta `Spatial Awareness`  ⚠ when blinded, an Alertness check at DC 13

**Defined: you cannot see. You lose your Dexterity bonus to Defence and take a further `−2` Defence. Attacks against you are made as against a `flat-footed` target. Your own attacks take `−4`. Sight-based checks automatically fail.**

> **⚠ A blinded creature CAN still act and CAN still attack.** **The Togruta trait assumes it — a condition that stopped all action would make `Spatial Awareness` meaningless.**

**⚠ Same gap shape as the fear conditions before `PT-445`: a word in a list with dependents and no meaning.**

### `Force Blindness` — adopted, resistible

**Dark, T2, FP 14, DSP −3, Character Level 9.** **Every enemy within 4 metres: Will save or `blinded` for 4 rounds.**

**⚠ A successful save NEGATES — owner ruling.** *The source says the power cannot otherwise be resisted and that a save merely halves the duration.* **Ninth instance of the block's no-save instinct, ninth time it is overruled.**

**⚠ Level 23 → 9. And the source's *"blind, therefore cannot attack at all"* is DROPPED** — far stronger than `blinded` anywhere in our corpus.

**⚠ `targets: sentient · beast` — it clouds a mind, not a sensor.**

### REJECTED

**`Spirit Exodus`** — **⚠ a second combatant on the board. `PT-153`/`PT-201`.** **And Level 30 is our absolute cap; a power available at the last level is a footnote.**

**`Doppelganger`** — **same, at Level 16.**

**`Force Quake`** — **⚠ 20 metres of NO-SAVE prone.** **Larger than `Force Wave`'s 7 squares, which costs FP 22, deals damage, AND allows a save.**

**`Force Deception`** — **owner ruling.** **⚠ AND MY REASON WAS WRONG.** **I called it a duplicate of `Force Camouflage`, which actually reads *"use their Stealth skill without a Stealth Field Generator, until the character deactivates it."*** **That is STEALTH ENABLEMENT, not invisibility. The light-bending is genuinely different and I did not check before claiming.**

### ⚠ A CHECK DEFECT — `audit_grid` is blind to hyphenated distances

**My `Force Blindness` at *"within 5 metres"* was caught immediately. ⚠ `Horror` and `Force Sleep` both read *"5-metre radius"* and are NOT caught.**

**`audit_grid`'s pattern is `(\d+)\s*(?:metres|metre|m)\b` — `\s*` matches whitespace, and `5-metre` has a HYPHEN.**

> **⚠ `5 metres` is checked. `5-metre` is invisible. And 5 metres is 2.5 squares — OFF GRID.**

**⚠ NOT FIXED, deliberately.** **`Horror`'s 5 metres is the GAME'S number, ported.** **Widening the regex would flag ported values as defects, and whether the grid rule binds ported radii is a ruling, not a regex change.**

**Fourth `audit_grid`-class defect after `PT-410`, `PT-400`, `PT-424` and `PT-425`'s decimal-fraction bug: a check right about its literal test and wrong about its scope.**

## PT-471 — `Dark Healing` adopted. `Drain Life` capped. ⚠ And the heal line audited against the files

**Bundled deliberately. All four items are the same question — what a heal is worth — and splitting them would leave `Drain Life` and `Dark Healing` priced against each other in two different rulings.**

### `Dark Healing` — adopted at the agreed numbers

**Dark, T3, FP 24, DSP −6. Sith Marauder, Sith Assassin or Sith Lord. `targets: self`.**

**Heals `1d8` per Force level, maximum `15d8`.** **`−2` Strength and `−4` Constitution for 10 rounds.** **⚠ Stacks; neither score falls below 3; cannot be cast at Constitution 3.**

**⚠ The source says *"completely restores the vitality of the caster."*** **Rejected as too cheap — a full heal makes the Constitution cost INVISIBLE, because you are topped up anyway.** **At `15d8` you feel the ceiling drop.**

> **⚠ The cost needs NO new rule.** **`RULES-01-v2` line 218: vitality per level carries the Constitution modifier.** **`−4` Con is `−2` to the modifier, so at Force level 15 the caster loses 30 points of MAXIMUM vitality for the duration.** **Heal 67, lose 30 of ceiling — and the second casting nets far less.**

### ⚠ The hole it fills is NARROWER than I first claimed

**I said *"a Sith alone and bleeding has nothing."* Wrong. `ALIGNMENT-01` has the multipliers, ported from `forceadjust.2da`:**

    Deep Dark        0–14    Dark 0.50x   ⚠ Light 1.75x
    Committed Dark  15–28    Dark 0.75x   ⚠ Light 1.50x

**A Deep Dark Sith casting `Heal` at FP 8 pays 14. `Master Heal` at FP 24 costs him 42.** **It is not closed to him — it is priced at nearly double.**

**⚠ The REAL gap: `Drain Life` is `life`-class and `PT-459` excludes droids.** **A Sith fighting droids has no self-heal at all.** **That is `Dark Healing`'s niche and it should be stated as such.**

### `Drain Life` — capped at `20d4`, owner ruling

    K1 strref 1215   "1-4 per level, TO A MAXIMUM OF 10 LEVELS (10-40 points)"   ⚠ explicit cap
    K2 strref 1215   "1-4 per level"                                            ⚠ cap REMOVED
    was              25d4   avg 62   max 100
    now              20d4   avg 50   max  80

**⚠ Ours matched NEITHER game.** **`PT-301`'s general curve — per level to 20, then per two, cap 25 — was applied over a value the entry itself specifies.**

> **⚠ A general conversion rule beat a specific stated number. That is the wrong precedence and it should not have happened.**

**⚠ The two games disagree and both are rank 1.** **Owner ruling: keep our shape, lower the cap to 20. Neither game's figure is adopted, and that is deliberate.**

### ⚠ `Master Heal` needs nothing — I misread it

**I estimated it at ~20 and suggested it could be more.**

    Heal           L6    5 vitality  + Cha + Wis + level
    Improved Heal  L12   15 vitality + Cha + Wis + level
    Master Heal    L18   15 vitality + Cha + Wis + ⚠ TWICE level

**⚠ The tier difference is the SCALING, not the base.** **At level 18 with `+3/+3`: `Improved` gives 39, `Master` gives 57.** **Our entry already has it right. I read the flat 15 and ignored the multiplier.**

### ⚠ Two unrecorded departures found in passing, NOT fixed

**`Heal`'s base.** **Source: *"heals 5 vitality points."* Ours: **`1d8`**.** **A flat value converted to a die with no ruling. Average 4.5 against 5 — cosmetic, but it is an undocumented change to a rank-1 number.**

**`Improved Heal`'s base.** **⚠ K1 says 10, K2 says 15. Ours took K2's without recording the choice.** **Same K1/K2 split as `Drain Life`, resolved silently in the other direction.**

**Both flagged. Neither ruled — they want the same treatment `Drain Life` just got, and that is a heal-line pass rather than two one-line edits.**

## PT-472 — The drain pair separated. ⚠ The source never separated them

    Drain Life   T1 · FP 10 · DSP −1 · one target       ⚠ 25d4 -> 20d4 -> 15d4
    Death Field  T2 · FP 20 · DSP −4 · 10-metre radius  ⚠ 25d4 -> 20d4

**Owner ruling across two rulings. Final: `15d4` and `20d4`.**

### ⚠ The source gives them the SAME damage line

    K1 1215  Drain Life   "1-4 per level, to a maximum of 10 levels (10-40 points)"
    K1 1211  Death Field  "1-4 per level, to a maximum of 10 levels (10-40 points)"
    K2 1215  Drain Life   "1-4 per level"                  ⚠ cap removed
    K2 1211  Death Field  "1-4 per level"                  ⚠ cap removed

> **⚠ IDENTICAL. In both games. The source prices the upgrade entirely in SCOPE — one target becomes a 10-metre radius — and not at all in power.**

**Ours now prices it in BOTH. A deliberate departure, recorded here so it is not read as a transcription slip.**

### ⚠ And the FP step was never really buying the radius

**`Death Field` heals *"the equivalent of the most damage dealt to any single enemy."***

**Against six enemies it rolls its damage six times and heals the BEST result.** **⚠ That is a max-of-N heal, statistically well above a single roll even at identical dice — before counting the damage spread across six targets.**

    against ONE enemy   ⚠ strictly worse than Drain Life, for double the FP
    against a crowd     the strongest healing in the game

**The FP 10 → 20 step is pricing the MAX-OF-N, not the radius.** **Stated because the damage split now makes it look as though the step buys dice, and it does not.**

### ⚠ Both figures are now ours

**`15d4` — average 37, max 60.**
**`20d4` — average 50, max 80.**

**Neither matches K1's stated `10d4 (10-40 points)` nor K2's uncapped line.** **`PT-471` recorded that `PT-301`'s general curve had overridden a specific stated value; the fix was to lower the cap rather than adopt either game's figure.**

**⚠ That means the drain pair is now entirely authored on numbers and ported only on shape.** **Marked as such.**

## PT-474 — Seven feats adopted from the mod block. Nineteen rejected. ⚠ And a correction on percentages

### ADOPTED — 7

| Feat | Owner | Change from source |
|---|---|---|
| **Payday** → `Good Hunting` → `Everything Has A Price` | **Pirate** | ⚠ rewritten from a party-slot economy into a per-body credit drop |
| **Momentum** → `Gathering Pace` → `Killing Pace` | any | ⚠ renamed from `Killer Instinct`; **stacking CAPPED** |
| **Dark Rage** | Force-sensitive, Str 12 | unchanged |
| **Sadism** → **Sated** | Force-sensitive | ⚠ `Sweet Release` renamed; condition list restated |
| **Constancy** → **Respite** | Force-sensitive | unchanged |
| **Anti-Shield Protocol** | **Marksman** | ⚠ `HK-47` prerequisite retargeted |
| **Auto-Shield Protocol** | **Engineer** | ⚠ `Expert Droid` prerequisite renamed — `PT-76` |

### ⚠ `Momentum`'s cap is the whole fix

**The source: *"this bonus stacks with itself in the case of multiple kills."*** **No limit.** **A room of weak enemies hands you an unbounded attack bonus.**

**Capped at the tier value — `+1` / `+2` / `+3`.** **It rewards FINISHING without rewarding FARMING.**

### ⚠ `Dark Rage` inverts the Force stat model, deliberately

**Every Force save DC in the corpus runs on Wisdom and Charisma.** **`Dark Rage` adds STRENGTH to damage.**

> **⚠ A Sith Marauder now out-DAMAGES a Consular with the same power, and the Consular still LANDS it more often. The DC is untouched.**

**Recorded as a class-distinction change. ⚠ If it is wrong, the feat is the thing to cut — not the DCs.**

### ⚠ `Sadism` and `Constancy` are the first alignment-scaled EFFECTS

**`ALIGNMENT-01` scales the COST of a power by band — 0.50x to 1.75x. ⚠ NOTHING scaled an EFFECT.**

**These two are mirrored: `Sadism` is half as effective for a light-side character, `Constancy` half for a dark-side one.** **Cruelty works for the dark; patience for the light.**

**⚠ *"Half as effective"* ruled: halve the numeric result, round down.** **`+50%` becomes `+25%`; `1d8` becomes `1d4`.**

**⚠ And `Sadism`'s condition list is OURS.** **The source says *"Stun, Paralysis or Fear."*** **`PT-445` cut `frightened` and `PT-447` split fear into three, so the list is restated as `stunned` · `paralysed` · `shaken` · `panicked` · `cowering`.**

### ⚠ CORRECTION — I said percentage mechanics exist nowhere

**I rejected `Shield Boost` partly on *"energy shields are flat point values; percentage modifiers exist nowhere."***

**Wrong. `ITEMS-03` and `ITEMS-05` are full of them:**

    Energy Shielding Mark I–IV     DamageImmunity (Energy) 10 / 15 / 20 / 30%
    Thermal Shield Generator       DamageImmunity (Fire) 75%
    Multishield Generator          DamageImmunity (Electrical) 50%

**⚠ Shields in this corpus ARE percentage damage immunity.** **Which is why both protocol feats port cleanly — and it means `Shield Boost` was rejected on a false premise.** **The owner rejected it anyway; the reason recorded was bad.**

### REJECTED — 19, and the reasons cluster

**⚠ PARTY ARCHITECTURE — 5.** **`Designated Medic` · `Second Wind` · `Stimpack Treatment` · `Last Stand` · `Mysterious Benefactor`.** **All written for KOTOR's THREE-slot active party — *"while a character with this feat is in your active party, both other party members…"*, *"while both of your companions are incapacitated."*** **We have no fixed party size.**

**⚠ DEPENDS ON WHAT WE CANNOT SEE — 3.** **`Flashbang` · `Extra Kick` · `Shrapnel Burst`.** **Every grenade in `ITEMS-01` resolves via `CastSpell` into `spells.2da`, WHICH WE DO NOT HOLD — `PT-463`.** **We cannot modify a save DC we cannot read.**

**⚠ PERCENTAGE SHIELD STACK — 3.** **`Shield Boost` ×3.** **See the correction above: the stated reason was wrong.**

**⚠ ALREADY REJECTED AS POWERS — 3.** **`Resonance` ×3 appear in the feat block TOO. The mod ships them twice.** **`PT-463`.**

**⚠ COMBO SYSTEM — 3.** **`Whirling Blade` · `Thunderous Blade` · `Heartstopper`.** **A combo COUNTER with break conditions — *hit with a sword 4 times in a row, unbroken by any other damage source*.** **Nothing tracks consecutive same-weapon hits, and `ATTACKS-05`'s `Flurry`, `Dual Strike` and `Critical Strike` occupy that space by DECLARATION rather than ACCUMULATION.**

**⚠ SKILL CONVERSION — 1.** **`Applied Knowledge` maps skill ranks onto combat modifiers by lookup.** **`SKILLS-01` merged and restructured the skill list; the mapping would not survive translation.**

### ⚠ The mod block is now fully assessed

**32 powers, 26 feats. ⚠ Adopted: 8 powers, 7 feats. Rejected: 24 powers, 19 feats.**

## PT-475 — The shield feats split by chassis role. A droid `Shield Boost` tree. ⚠ And percentages go on the agenda

### The chassis split

    Anti-Shield Protocol   ⚠ Assassin · Battle      the COMBAT chassis STRIP shields
    Auto-Shield Protocol   ⚠ Astromech · Remote     the SUPPORT chassis RAISE them
    Shield Boost           ⚠ Astromech · Remote     authored, three tiers

**Owner ruling. ⚠ `PT-474` had put them on the Marksman and the Engineer — CLASSES. These are CHASSIS feats and belong on the chassis.**

> **⚠ `DROID-SKILLS-01 §2.3` already draws exactly this line.** **The support chassis get `Treat Injury` on organics; the combat chassis keep the exclusion.** **The shield split mirrors it without being told to.**

**⚠ And HK-47 is the Assassin chassis' own exemplar** — the source's named prerequisite lands on the right chassis by accident.

### `Shield Boost` — authored for droids

| Tier | Level | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| **Shield Boost** | 1 | **`+10` points absorbed before the generator fails.** |
| › **Reinforced Emitters** | 4 | **`+20`**, and one free reactivation per encounter. |
| ›› **Overcharge** | 8 | **`+30`**, and **no damage from the first attack each round** the shield would have absorbed. |

**⚠ FLAT POINTS. The source reads `+20% / +40% / +60%`.**

**⚠ `PT-474` rejected the source `Shield Boost` on the stated ground that *"percentage modifiers exist nowhere"* — which was FALSE and I corrected it in the same ruling.** **The real objection is that percentages are bad AT A TABLE, not that they are absent.** **This tree is the corrected version.**

### `Payday`'s capstone renamed

**`Everything Has A Price` → `Clean Sweep`.** **Two words, owner ruling.**

### ⚠ AGENDA — replace the percentage mechanics

**Added to `AGENDA-CURRENT` as its own block.**

    ITEMS-03   Energy Shielding Mark I–IV   10 / 15 / 20 / 30%
    ITEMS-05   Thermal Shield Generator     75% Fire
    ITEMS-05   Multishield Generator        50% Electrical
    powers     Force Choke                  "2/3rds of the attacker's level"

> **⚠ A percentage makes the player know a total, compute a fraction, and round. Flat points, dice and fixed steps do not.**

**⚠ NOT a find-and-replace.** **Several are PORTED values and changing them is a departure that must be recorded per item.** **Scoped as a pass over `ITEMS-03`, `ITEMS-05` and `PROPERTY-VOCAB-01`'s damage-immunity vocabulary.**

**⚠ Three mod-block rejections leaned on this — `Shield Boost`, `Force Weaken`'s *"50% of current vitality"*, and `Last Stand`'s *"5% of maximum VP"*.** **Once the replacement exists, `Force Weaken` and `Last Stand` may be worth reopening.**

## PT-477 — `Last Stand` adopted as a three-tier chain. `Force Weaken` rejected again

### `Force Weaken` — REJECTED, and the percentage was never the real problem

**Reopened at `PT-475`'s note that three rejections leaned on percentages.**

**⚠ Three objections survive the percentage fix:**

**`−10` to Defence, saves AND deflection** — **outside every band we use. Our largest single modifier is `Force Armor`'s `+6`.**

**⚠ *"Cannot be resisted"*** — **the block's signature defect, overruled eight times already.**

**⚠ And converting *"50% of current vitality"* to dice REMOVES THE ONLY THING THAT MADE IT DISTINCT.** **A percentage-of-current power scales identically against a rakghoul and a rancor; that was its identity.** **As dice it is `Force Choke` with a debuff attached, and we have `Force Choke`.**

> **⚠ Reopening was still correct.** **`Last Stand` survived the same test and this did not — which is the point of testing both.**

### `Last Stand` — three tiers, owner ruling

| Tier | Level | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| **Last Stand** | 1 | **`1d4` + Con** vitality at the start of each of your turns while last conscious |
| › **Improved Last Stand** | 4 | **`2d4` + Con**, and **`+4`** on saves against `fear effects` |
| ›› **Master Last Stand** | 8 | **`3d4` + Con**, and **you cannot be reduced below 1 vitality by a single attack** |

### ⚠ *Party* is defined, because the source's definition does not survive

**The source: *"while both of your COMPANIONS are incapacitated."*** **KOTOR's three-slot party, hard-coded into a feat.**

**Ruled: *party* means every allied character under player or GM control — players, companions, ⚠ a Beast Master's beast, ⚠ a Droid Master's droids.** **You are the last when all of them are at 0 vitality or below, or otherwise out of the fight.**

> **⚠ That has a consequence worth stating: a Beast Master or Droid Master is HARDER to trigger this on, because their companions are additional bodies that must all fall first.** **Correct, and the reason to say so is that it will look like a bug at a table.**

**⚠ And it is strongest in a SMALL party and weakest in a LARGE one — the inverse of most feats.** **Deliberate. A solo survivor is the point.**

### ⚠ `Master Last Stand`'s floor is not immunity

**One attack cannot drop you below 1. Repeated attacks still kill you.** **Stated because *"cannot be reduced below 1"* reads as invulnerability at a glance.**

### ⚠ And the fear clause is the second alignment-free effect scaling

**`Improved Last Stand` gives `+4` on saves against `fear effects` — you are past being afraid.**

**⚠ Written as `−2` in the first draft of this ruling. A PENALTY, where the flavour is resistance. Caught before it settled.**

**⚠ It uses `PT-459`'s category rather than naming conditions**, which is what that property was written for. **First feat outside the Force list to use it.**

## PT-478 — `Last Stand`'s regeneration lowered. ⚠ It was far outside the corpus

    was    1d8 / 2d8 / 3d8     avg 4.5 / 9.0 / 13.5
    now    1d4 / 1d6 / 1d8     avg 2.5 / 3.5 /  4.5

**Owner ruling. ⚠ And the comparison shows how far out it was:**

    Regeneration 1              beasts        1 flat per turn
    Regeneration 2              beasts        2 flat per turn    ⚠ the corpus HIGH
    Regenerate Vitality Points  feat          0.5 every 6 seconds
    ⚠ Last Stand, as drafted    1d8 / 2d8 / 3d8

> **⚠ `Master Last Stand` at `3d8` averaged 13.5 a turn — nearly SEVEN TIMES the highest sustained regeneration in the game, and roughly a `2d8` beast's entire vitality die every round.**

**At `1d4` / `1d6` / `1d8` the top tier equals a `Regeneration 2` beast at twice the rate, which is a defensible ceiling for a capstone that only fires when everyone else is down.**

### ⚠ The ladder grows the DIE, not the count

**`PT-456` ruled that for poison, taking 3e's monstrous-spider curve: `1d2` → `1d4` → `1d6`, die size growing, count fixed.**

**⚠ This is the first time that rule has been applied OUTSIDE the poison system.** **`1d8` → `2d8` → `3d8` was the count-scaling shape `PT-456` explicitly ruled against, and I wrote it anyway five rulings later.**

**Recorded because it will recur: `ATTACKS-05`'s player chains DO use count-scaling — `1d6` / `2d6` / `3d6` — and that inconsistency is still unruled.** **Two ladders, two shapes, and nothing says which governs a new feat.**

## PT-479 — `Last Stand` final: `1d4` / `2d4` / `3d4` + Constitution modifier

    PT-477 draft   1d8 / 2d8 / 3d8              avg  4.5 /  9.0 / 13.5
    PT-478         1d4 / 1d6 / 1d8              avg  2.5 /  3.5 /  4.5
    ⚠ PT-479       1d4 / 2d4 / 3d4 + Con mod    avg  2.5 /  5.0 /  7.5  before Con

**Owner ruling.**

### ⚠ The Constitution modifier is what makes it a survivor's feat

**It scales with the stat that already governs vitality — `RULES-01-v2` line 218.**

> **A tough character holds out longer; a fragile one gains little.** **⚠ At Constitution 8 the modifier is `−1` and the first tier can regain NOTHING on a roll of 1.**

**That is correct and should not be smoothed.** **A feat about refusing to fall should reward the constitution to keep standing.**

### ⚠ Count-scaling, and it settles which convention governs

**`PT-478` recorded that I had broken `PT-456`'s die-scaling rule and flagged the inconsistency: poison grows the DIE, `ATTACKS-05`'s chains grow the COUNT at `1d6`/`2d6`/`3d6`.**

**⚠ The owner's ruling resolves it for this case: `Last Stand` is a three-tier FEAT CHAIN and follows the CHAIN convention.**

    poison ladders    grow the DIE      PT-456   1d2 / 1d4 / 1d6
    feat and attack   grow the COUNT    PT-479   1d4 / 2d4 / 3d4

> **⚠ Two conventions, and now a stated basis for choosing between them: what KIND of ladder it is, not which was written most recently.**

**⚠ This is a general rule arrived at through one feat, and it governs the ~60 beast chains still to write.** **Worth confirming as such rather than leaving it implicit in a `Last Stand` ruling.**

## PT-480 — ⚠ Senses WITHDRAWN as feats. Two type grants. `Echolocation` and `Skittish`

### ⚠ `PT-453` broke an existing ruling and I wrote it myself

**`SPECIES-CHAPTER-v2` line 41:** ***"How a species communicates is not a feat. Scent, radio, lekku, signal fires, hive consensus — all of it belongs in the species prose, where a player reads it, rather than on the mechanical block."***

**⚠ `PT-453` created `Scent`, `Tremorsense` and `Darkvision` as FEATS. Withdrawn.**

**They are now a `senses` line in the entry, beside `speed` and `vitality`. They cost nothing and count for nothing.**

> **⚠ AND IT FIXES THE DISTRIBUTION PROBLEM THE REFERENCE TABLE EXPOSED.** **Removing three sense feats hits the tag-heavy beasts hardest — `Kinrath` 7 → 5, `Laigrek` 6 → 5, `Tuk'ata` 6 → 4 — and barely moves the sparse ones.** **The imbalance was largely an artefact of my own rules violation.**

### Two TYPE grants — types now do what tags do

**`Scavenger` grants `Forage` and `Sniff Out`.** **⚠ `PT-453` left them hand-assigned because the type had ONE holder; `PT-454` gave it four — exactly the beasts they were written for.** **Types already grant saves and a vitality die; this is not a new mechanism.**

**`Herd Animal` grants `Bearer` — it can be ridden and a rider acts normally from its back.** **⚠ Both Herd Animals already carried a mount racial and NOTHING CONNECTED THEM.**

### `Shyrack` → **`Echolocation`**, and it is ported

**Wookieepedia: *eyeless beasts*, *ungainly and slow-moving with no eyes*.**

> **⚠ THE SHYRACK IS NOT DARK-ADAPTED. IT IS BLIND.** **`PT-453` gave it `Darkvision`, which is wrong for a creature with no eyes. Removed.**

**⚠ Three times per DAY it maps everything within 12 squares through darkness, smoke and total concealment — including creatures Hidden from the party.**

**⚠ While `deafened` it is blind: total concealment against everything, and it cannot use this at all.** **A weakness nothing else on the roster has.**

**⚠ A note is owed to `Nictitating Membrane`** — immunity to blinding by light, sand, smoke and spray does NOTHING for a creature that has no eyes. **Not yet added.**

### `Iriaz` → **`Skittish`**

**It notices first. At intervals the GM judges, and BEFORE the party perceives anything, it makes an `Alertness` check and alerts you to danger.**

**⚠ It will not willingly move toward a creature it knows to be a predator.** **The cost: you cannot scout with it.**

**⚠ FOR THE APP: this must run in the BACKGROUND.** **The check fires on a GM interval, not on a player declaration, and the player should learn of the result rather than be asked for the roll.** **Owner instruction, recorded here because it is an APP-ARCHITECTURE requirement disguised as a feat.**

**⚠ Do not overdo the interval.** **A warning that fires constantly stops being a warning.**

**`Break Away` is retired as a racial — it is now the `Herd Animal` grant `Bearer`'s territory.**

### ⚠ THE IRIAZ ATTACK LINE IS WRONG — flagged, NOT corrected

**Our entry: `bite 1d4 · claw 1d3`. ⚠ A grazing herbivore with CLAWS.**

**Wookieepedia: *"while not normally aggressive, they could attack if provoked, CHARGING WITH THEIR HORNS."*** **Saga: *"charging with their huge, majestic horns."***

> **⚠ It should be `gore`. The `PT-356` per-type template was applied without anyone reading the creature — the same defect as the Gizka's `Dex 18` at `PT-455`.**

**⚠ AND IT BLOCKS THE OWNER'S CHAIN REQUEST.** **Two tier-1 chains were asked for on `bite` and `claw`. If the attack line is corrected they should bind to `gore` and a second weapon — `hoof` or `trample` — and writing bite/claw chains now would be writing chains for weapons it does not have.**

**NOT CORRECTED. It needs a ruling on what a Herd Animal's natural weapons are, which touches the Wraid too.**

### ⚠ And the iriaz was CUT from KOTOR

**Wookieepedia: *intended to appear in KOTOR but cut. Dialogue from the "Murdered Settler" quest suggests they were meant to be present.*** **Rickard Lusoff claims he was hunting iriaz; Bolook insists there are iriaz all around.**

**⚠ That explains `c_iriaz.utc`'s all-10 placeholder abilities.** **Our iriaz is built almost entirely from a cut creature's leftovers.**

## PT-481 — `Echolocation` is three per DAY. ⚠ "Long rest" is not a thing in this game

**Owner asked for per long rest. ⚠ The corpus does not have one.**

**`force/REST-AND-MEDITATION-01` line 12:** ***"RCR has no long rest and no short rest. Neither term is defined; no unit of rest exists as a game object."***

**That document resolves both into MEDITATION and states the equivalence outright:**

    "Short rest"   one hour of meditation      75% of lost ceiling, max two per day
    "Long rest"    eight hours of meditation   the true maximum in full
    ⚠ "the two-per-day cap ... was two per long rest, and A LONG REST WAS A DAY"

**And the existing corpus already uses `per day` everywhere it means this:**

    Emergency Reboot        once per day
    Master Emergency Reboot twice per day
    Rakata Rage             once per day
    Wookiee Rage            once per day

**⚠ Ruled as `three times per day`.** **The owner's intent is preserved exactly; the vocabulary is the corpus's own.**

> **⚠ `REST-AND-MEDITATION-01` records that `FORCE-POOL-01 v2` used BOTH undefined terms anyway.** **Writing *"per long rest"* into a beast feat would have been the third document to do it, in a project that already noticed and fixed the problem once.**

**Three per day, on a `1d4`-ish encounter rate, is roughly one per fight and not always.** **⚠ That is the intended shape: a shyrack finds the hidden thing SOMETIMES, and the party cannot lean on it.**

    force/ALIGNMENT-01-v2.md    2 lines   ⚠ the meditation alignment shift

    now    "during EIGHT HOURS of uninterrupted work"
           "One such period produces one crafting session — and no more than ONE PER DAY"

## PT-483 — `audit_beasts.py` — check 24. ⚠ It found three real defects on its first run

**Written because `PT-482` caught the Gizka's withdrawn `It Breeds` by ACCIDENT, during a search for something else.**

### ⚠ Why nothing existing could catch it

**`audit_refs` asks whether a backticked name RESOLVES.** **Both names resolved — `It Breeds` was a real feat once and `Gnaw` is a real feat now.** **⚠ RESOLUTION IS NOT AGREEMENT.**

**`audit_duplicates` compares whole FILES. `audit_names` asks whether a name denotes one object.** **⚠ Neither compares two documents' accounts of the SAME beast.**

### What it checks — four questions per beast

    ROSTER    in BEASTS-ENTRIES-01 and BEASTS-FEATS-01 alike
    TAGS      entry's tag line matches BEASTS-01's tag table, BOTH WAYS
    SENSES    a `senses` line exists at all -- PT-482 requires one
    ATTACKS   a natural-weapon line exists
    ⚠ RACIAL  ADVISORY — the entry's prose against the feat's name

**⚠ The racial test is ADVISORY and that is deliberate.** **An entry DESCRIBES and a feat NAMES; *"Eats machinery"* against `Scrap-Eater` is style, not a defect.** **It is LISTED rather than blocked, because the Gizka's withdrawn feat looked exactly like style and was not.**

### ⚠ Three real defects on the first run

**`Shyrack`** — **its entry's one-thing was *"Never alone"*, which is the `swarming` TAG GRANT, not a racial.** **`PT-480` gave it `Echolocation` and the entry was never updated.** **Corrected, and the entry now states explicitly that `Swarm` comes from the tag and is not its racial.**

**`Maalrass`** — **its entry carried ONLY the `PT-368` source flag.** **⚠ It had no printed ability at all — the same hole `PT-437` found and filled in `BEASTS-FEATS-01`, and the ENTRY was never given the fix.** **`Jungle Stalker` and `Scorched Hide` written in; the source note rewritten to say what IS attested rather than only what is not.**

**`Tach`** — **its entry carries `venomous`; `BEASTS-01`'s tag table did not list it.** **⚠ `PT-453` added the tag to the entry and `PT-454`'s rewrite of the table dropped it.** **Table corrected: `Kinrath · Tach`, with the `Weakening` ladder on both and `Wasting` on the Kinrath alone.**

### ⚠ Registered as BLOCKING

**`gate.py` check 24. 25 entries, 24 feat rows, 7 tags. PASSES.**

> **⚠ Two of the three defects were rulings applied to ONE document and not the other.** **That is not a beast problem — it is what happens whenever a decision touches two files, and this check only covers beasts.**

## PT-484 — Herd Animal weapons are per-beast. The Iriaz gores. ⚠ And six beasts break `PT-432`'s size rule

### ⚠ `Herd Animal` does NOT dictate a weapon set

**Owner ruling: *"different herd animals are going to have different things at their disposal."***

**And the roster proves it. `BEASTS-01`: the Wraid is a *"heavy REPTILIAN herd beast."*** **⚠ No hooves, no horns.**

> **⚠ The TYPE says what a beast IS. The ANATOMY says what it fights with.** **`Bearer` is a type grant because every Herd Animal can be ridden; weapons are not, because a reptile and a grazer share nothing but a diet.**

### `Iriaz` — `gore 1d6 · hoof 1d4`

    was    bite 1d4 · claw 1d3      ⚠ a grazing herbivore with CLAWS
    now    gore 1d6 · hoof 1d4

**Wookieepedia: *"while not normally aggressive, they could attack if provoked, CHARGING WITH THEIR HORNS."*** **Saga: *"charging with their huge, majestic horns."***

**⚠ The `PT-356` per-type template was applied without reading the creature — the third instance, after the Gizka's `Dex 18` and the Iriaz's own all-10 abilities.**

**⚠ The Wraid is NOT changed.** **A reptile with a bite and claws is plausible; nothing in the sources contradicts it.**

### ⚠ SIX BEASTS BREAK `PT-432`'s SIZE RULE

**`PT-432`: *"attack dice — purely SIZE. Tiny 1d3 · Small 1d4 · Medium 1d8 · Large 2d6 · Huge 2d8."***

    Iriaz           Medium   expected 1d8/1d6   ⚠ has 1d6/1d4  (as corrected)
    Duracrete Slug  Medium   expected 1d8/1d6   ⚠ has 1d6/1d4
    Kinrath         Medium   expected 1d8/1d6   ⚠ has 1d6/1d4
    Wraid           Large    expected 2d6/2d4   ⚠ has 1d6/1d4
    Dianoga         Large    expected 2d6/2d4   ⚠ has 1d8/1d4
    Brith           Small    expected 1d4/1d3   ⚠ has 1d6/1d4 — ABOVE its size

> **⚠ `PT-432` stated size-sets-dice as a RULE after observing the MAJORITY. Six beasts were already exceptions and nobody checked.**

**⚠ NOT NORMALISED.** **Changing six beasts' damage is a balance ruling, not a script run** — **and the Wraid's `1d6` at Large may be deliberate: a `d4`-vitality Herd Animal that is not meant to fight.**

**Flagged as its own decision.**

### The two chains

**`Lower Horns` → `Run Down` → `Stampede`** — **gore, POSITION axis, `PT-333`.** **Damage bought with movement; `+1d6` / `+2d6` / `+3d6`, prone at tier 2, passing THROUGH a creature at tier 3.**

**`Trample` → `Batter` → `Crush Underfoot`** — **hoof, CONTROL axis.** **`+1d4` / `+2d4` / `+3d4`, against prone targets first, then pushing, then double damage on the prone.**

**⚠ The pair does not duplicate: the gore chain PUTS THEM DOWN, the hoof chain KEEPS THEM DOWN.**

### ⚠ And the chains make `Skittish` cost something

**`Skittish` — `PT-480` — says it will not willingly move toward a known predator.**

> **⚠ Both chains require movement to matter. The beast that must charge 2 squares is the beast that refuses to move toward the dangerous thing.** **The Beast Master has to order it in, and that is the price of the early warning.**

**Recorded because the interaction was not designed — it fell out of two rulings written four apart.**

## PT-484 — ⚠ NATURAL WEAPONS ARE PER-BEAST, NOT PER-TYPE. Iriaz corrected and chained

**Owner ruling: *"herd animals are distinct enough that the type should not determine the attack type — the beast itself should."***

**⚠ Ruled generally. A beast's natural weapons come from ITS ANATOMY. Type sets saves and the vitality die; SIZE sets the dice; the WEAPONS are the creature's own.**

### `Iriaz` — `gore` and `hoof`

    was    bite 1d4 · claw 1d3     ⚠ a grazing herbivore with claws
    now    gore 1d6 · hoof 1d4

**Wookieepedia: *"while not normally aggressive, they could attack if provoked, CHARGING WITH THEIR HORNS."*** **Saga: *"charging with their huge, majestic horns."***

**⚠ The `PT-356` per-type template was applied without reading the creature — the same defect as the Gizka's `Dex 18` at `PT-455`.**

### Its two chains — `BEASTS-ATTACKS-01`

    Lower Horns → Run Down → Stampede      gore · POSITION axis
    Trample → Batter → Crush Underfoot     hoof · CONTROL axis

**⚠ `POSITION` is the right axis, `PT-333`: damage bought with movement.** **The same shape as the Boma's `Ramming Charge` — a charge that has not charged is not a charge.**

**⚠ And it makes `Skittish` cost something real.** **The Iriaz will not willingly approach a known predator — so the beast that must move 2 squares to matter is the beast that refuses to move toward the dangerous thing.** **The Beast Master has to order it in.**

### `Wraid` — ⚠ `bite · claw` is CORRECT, and the lore confirms it

**Wookieepedia: *very powerful front legs, large claws at the end of their feet, sharp teeth, and two small back legs.*** **A knuckle-walker with all its power in the forelimbs.**

**⚠ NO CHANGE. The owner's *"massive mouths and giant arms"* is the source verbatim.**

### ⚠⚠ BUT THE WRAID IS A PREDATOR IN EVERY SOURCE, AND WE HAVE IT AS A HERD ANIMAL

**Wookieepedia and two others: *"large PREDATORY reptilian animals."*** **`swtor` codex: *"hunting dangerous predators is a tradition on Tatooine, and stalking the deadly wraid is often a test."***

## PT-485 — The Iriaz's chains named

    Bull Rush → Run Down → Stampede     gore · POSITION
    Stomp → Batter → Trample            hoof · CONTROL

**Owner ruling. ⚠ `Trample` MOVES to the capstone — it was the tier-1 name and is now tier 3.**

**⚠ That reads better than my draft.** **`Stomp` is a small deliberate act on something already down; `Trample` is the whole animal going over you.** **My `Trample → Batter → Crush Underfoot` started at the biggest word and had nowhere to go.**

**⚠ `Bull Rush` is d20's own term for this manoeuvre**, which cuts both ways: instantly readable to anyone who has played, and generic. **The readability wins on a chain that must be understood at a glance.**

**`Rush`, `Drive`, `Flatten`, `Impale`, `Pin`** — 1 to 2 hits each, too close to collide.

## PT-486 — ⚠ The weapon decides the AXIS, not the die. The damage grid. The Wraid retyped

### The rule — owner ruling, option B

**A beast's natural weapon does not change how hard it hits. It changes WHAT IT CAN DO.**

    bite    Power · Control        one mouth — it commits, and it holds
    claw    Velocity · Precision   two of them, and they open things
    gore    Position ONLY          ⚠ a gore that has not moved is not a gore
    hoof    Control ONLY           knocks down, keeps down
    tail    Spread ONLY            one sweep, everything adjacent
    sonic   Spread · Control       ⚠ no attack roll — an area and a save

> **⚠ A gore beast and a bite beast of the same tier and size hit for the SAME DIE.** **The gore beast can only earn its damage by moving; the bite beast can hold you where you are.**

**⚠ AND IT WAS ALREADY TRUE BEFORE IT WAS A RULE.** **The Iriaz's `Bull Rush` is gore on POSITION and `Stomp` is hoof on CONTROL — both chosen by instinct at `PT-484`.**

### ⚠ The option that was rejected, and why

**Option A gave each weapon a DIE STEP — `gore +1`, `claw −1`, and so on.**

> **⚠ It breaks the tier ladder.** **A tier-1 Iriaz's gore would become `1d8` — the same die as a tier-2 Boma's bite.** **A herd animal out-hitting a predator one tier up, because it has horns.**

### The damage grid

|  | Tiny | Small | Medium | Large | Huge |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **tier 1** | `1d3` | `1d4` | `1d6` | `1d6` | `1d8` |
| **tier 2** | `1d4` | `1d6` | `1d8` | `1d10` | `1d12` |
| **tier 3** | `1d6` | `1d8` | `1d10` | `1d12` | `2d8` |

**⚠ This SUPERSEDES `PT-432`'s *"size sets the dice."*** **Tier and size together set them.**

**⚠ 17 of 25 already matched. Eight changed:**

    Cannok      1d8 -> 1d6    −1.0    Kinrath     1d6 -> 1d8    +1.0
    Hssiss      2d6 -> 1d10   −1.5    Dianoga     1d8 -> 1d10   +1.0
    Katarn      2d6 -> 1d10   −1.5    ⚠ Wraid     1d6 -> 1d10   +2.0
    Drexl       2d6 -> 1d12   −0.5    Terentatek  2d6 -> 1d12   −0.5

**⚠ The Wraid was the clear defect: `Large`, `Str 17`, carrying SMALL-tier dice — and its game file `g_w_crslash004` gives it `2d12`.**

### ⚠ Two flat spots, both recorded

**Tier 1 `Medium` and `Large` are both `1d6`.** **It never fires — tier 1 has no Large beast — but a Large beast added at tier 1 would gain nothing from its size.**

**Huge/tier 3 jumps `1d12 → 2d8`, `+2.5` average where every other step is `+1`.** **Kept because the Rancor and Zakkeg already sit there and should not drop.**

### ⚠ And the grid ignores Strength, deliberately

**The Kinrath at `Str 8` rises to `1d8`; the Boma at `Str 15` also sits at `1d8`.** **Strength already adds to damage — `RULES-01-v2` line 218 — so the die is size and tier alone.** **Stated because a `Str 8` Medium hitting as hard as a `Str 15` Medium looks wrong until you remember the modifier.**

### `Wraid` retyped — `Predator · Large · armoured · pack`

**Every source: *large PREDATORY reptilian animals* · *stalking the deadly wraid is a test to separate the amateurs from the experts* · *pack organisms by nature, often found in clusters between 2 and 6*.**

**⚠ `Herd Animal` now has ONE holder — the Iriaz.** **The shape `aquatic` was cut for at `PT-359`, and `Scavenger` was in before `PT-454` gave it four.** **Flagged.**

**⚠ AND `Shieldback` IS AUTHORED.** **Nothing in any source says a wraid is ridden. It is HUNTED — skull plates sold at Anchorhead, wraidskin made into chestguards.** **Kept, marked.**

## PT-487 — ⚠ `1 / 4 / 8` is a DEFAULT, not a rule. The Cannok's chains written

### ⚠ `PT-438` recorded a convention that does not exist

**It says beast chains gate at Beast Master levels `1 / 4 / 8`. ⚠ I derived that from `Flurry` without reading the rest of `ATTACKS-05`.**

**The player roster gates by WHAT A CHAIN DOES:**

    Flurry · Dual Strike · Cleave · Critical Strike
    Power Attack · Quick Attack · Sweep Attack        1 / 4 / 8    ⚠ seven DAMAGE chains
    Guarding Stance · Parry                           1 / 6 / 12   control and reaction
    Disarming Strike                                  5 / 8 / 14   ⚠ PERMANENT LOSS

> **⚠ Seven of ten at `1/4/8`. The three exceptions are exactly the ones that do something other than damage.**

**Ruled: a damage chain opens at 1 and climbs at 4 and 8. A chain that removes a turn, or ends in permanent loss, climbs SLOWER.**

**⚠ This governs the ~60 beast chains still unwritten. `PT-438`'s `1/4/8` should not be applied to all of them.**

### The Cannok — two chains

    Worry → Wrench → Abscond    bite · CONTROL     ⚠ 1 / 4 / 12
    Rake → Flense → Shred       claw · VELOCITY       1 / 4 / 8

**⚠ Both axes are legal under `PT-486` — bite takes `Power · Control`, claw takes `Velocity · Precision`.** **I chose them at the Cannok's first draft, before the rule existed, and they happen to comply.**

### ⚠ `Abscond` gated at 12, owner ruling

**It DESTROYS an item permanently, and the Cannok is a TIER 1 beast available immediately.**

**`Sever`, its player equivalent, sits at level 14 behind `Strength 12` AND `Dexterity 13` — the only chain in the game requiring two abilities.**

**⚠ `12` rather than `14` because a beast's level is the MASTER'S BEAST MASTER LEVEL, not a character level.** **A Beast Master at 12 in their own class is deep into the build; a level-14 CHARACTER might be a 6th-level Beast Master multiclassing.**

> **⚠ The gate is on the DESTRUCTION, not the theft.** **`Worry` at level 1 is the Cannok's identity — `PT-239` set the same precedent for `Plunder`, which unlocks at class level 1 BECAUSE it requires dropping someone first.**

### ⚠ And the earlier draft of `Worry` was a different chain

**The version shown at the Cannok's first design used `+1d4 / +2d4 / +3d4` bonus damage. ⚠ That was a POSITION chain.**

**This is the CONTROL version: opposed rolls, no bonus damage at all.** **A `Str 10` scavenger was never going to win on damage. It wins by taking your things.**

### `Rake` is `Flurry`, halved

**Same penalties, same tiers, ⚠ TWO attacks instead of three.** **A beast has two forelimbs and no weapon.**

**⚠ Its dice fell at `PT-486`: the Cannok moved from `bite 1d8 · claw 1d6` to `1d6` / `1d4`.** **The chain states no dice, so nothing in it needed editing — but `Rake` now throws two `1d4`s.**

### Three retyped to Medium — owner ruling

    Laigrek   Small -> Medium    bite 1d4/1d3 -> 1d6/1d4
    Shyrack   Small -> Medium    bite 1d4/1d3 -> 1d6/1d4

**⚠ `Mykal` at `Str 3` is now MEDIUM.** **The weakest Strength on the roster on a Medium frame.** **Flagged: `Str 3` was set when it was Tiny, and nothing has revisited it.**

### ⚠ The K'lor'slug is the first beast whose SIZE and TIER change

| Band | BM level | Size | Tier | attacks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **K'lor'slug** | 1–5 | Small | 1 | `1d4` / `1d3` |
| **Grown K'lor'slug** | 6–11 | Medium | 1 | `1d6` / `1d4` |
| **Great K'lor'slug** | 12–19 | **Large** | **2** | `1d10` / `1d8` |
| **Elder K'lor'slug** | 20+ | **Huge** | **3** | `2d8` / `2d6` |

**Dice read straight off `PT-486`'s grid at each band's tier AND size.** **⚠ Both climb together, which is why Medium → Large jumps `1d6 → 1d10`.**

### ⚠ `Squeeze` stops working, and that is the cost

**A Large or Huge slug cannot move through a space one size smaller than itself in any useful sense.** **Retained on the Small and Medium bands only.**

**It trades access for weight — which is the only thing keeping the growth from being pure upside.**

### ⚠⚠ AND IT BREAKS THE ACQUISITION TABLE

**`PT-431`: a Beast Master's beast levels with him. A purchased beast is fixed at its grade.**

**`BEASTS-01`'s acquisition table prices by TIER, and the apex beasts are gated at `DC 32` — *"cannot be bought, only earned."***

> **⚠ A Beast Master buys a K'lor'slug at TIER 1 PRICE and eventually holds a TIER 3 CREATURE.** **It is the only beast that crosses a tier gate the acquisition table exists to enforce.**

**⚠ NOT RESOLVED. Three ways out, none applied:**

**① Price it as tier 2 or 3 from the start** — expensive early, honest.
**② Cap the growth at Large** — it never reaches the apex tier and the gate holds.
**③ Accept it and mark the K'lor'slug as the deliberate exception** — a beast whose whole identity is that it outgrows what you paid for.

**⚠ Option ③ is the most interesting and the most exploitable.** **The owner should rule before any acquisition work is done.**

## PT-489 — The growth surcharge. `Mykal` at `Str 12`

### `Mykal` — `Str 3` → `Str 12`, owner ruling

**⚠ `Str 3` was set when it was `Tiny`. `PT-488` made it `Medium` and nothing revisited the number.**

**At `Str 12` its damage modifier goes `−4` to `+1`** — **a five-point swing on every attack**, which matters more than the die change did.

### The growth surcharge — ⚠ TRIPLE PRICE, same DC

**A beast whose SIZE and TIER change with its master's level is bought at its CURRENT band's DC and at TRIPLE its current band's price.**

    tier 1 band    DC 15    ⚠  5,000–14,000     (was 2,000–5,000)
    tier 2 band    DC 24    ⚠ 50,000–140,000    (was 20,000–50,000)
    ⚠ owner trimmed 1,000 off tier 1 and 10,000 off tier 2 from the first draft
    tier 3 band    DC 32    ⚠ not for sale, as any tier 3

**⚠ ONE HOLDER: the `K'lor'slug`.**

> **⚠ You are not buying the beast in front of you. You are buying every beast it becomes.** **A tier-1 K'lor'slug at 6,000 credits is dearer than a Boma is worth.**

### ⚠ The PRICE carries the surcharge and the DC does not — deliberately

**Bonding a young slug IS bonding a young slug. The difficulty is real and present, and raising the DC would punish the wrong thing.**

**⚠ A SELLER who knows what it becomes charges for what it becomes.** **That is a market fact, not a difficulty.**

**⚠ And it preserves `BEASTS-01`'s own principle — *"tier is not a level gate. It is a difficulty and a price, and either one opens it."*** **The growth surcharge moves ONE of the two, which is what that sentence permits.**

### ⚠ The tier-3 band is STILL not for sale, and that is what saves the gate

**Nobody sells an Elder K'lor'slug.** **You grow one, or you do not have one.**

> **⚠ `DC 32`'s gate holds for everything except a master who raised it from the start** — which is the gimmick, and it costs twenty levels of commitment rather than credits.

**⚠ A rich party can still buy a `Great K'lor'slug` at tier 2 for 60,000–150,000 — more than the most expensive item in KOTOR 2 at 32,000, and more than a Boma.** **That is the ceiling money reaches, and it stops one band short of the apex.**

### ⚠ Priced against the corpus, per `BEASTS-01`'s own method

    794 priced blueprints   median 1,600 · 90th percentile 23,600 · most expensive 32,000
    tier 1 growth beast     ⚠ 6,000–15,000 — between the 90th percentile and the median
    tier 2 growth beast     ⚠ 60,000–150,000 — nearly five times the most expensive item in the game

**⚠ The tier-2 figure is deliberately absurd.** **It is the price of skipping twelve levels of raising one, and it should read as a bad deal.**

## PT-490 — ⚠ A FEAT MAY ADD AN ACTION. The tier-1 racials split three ways

### ⚠ The test is not *passive or declared*. It is *does it have three steps*

**`PT-428` ruled: passive is a feat, declared is a chain or a rider.** **Applied to tier 1, six of seven racials are declared actions and would all become chains.**

> **⚠ THAT WOULD BE PADDING.** **`Bore` is complete in one line — *it moves through stone, permacrete and durasteel at half speed, carrying nothing*. There is no natural tier 2.** **I sketched *"thicker walls, then carry something through"* and it existed to fill a shape, not because the beast needed it.**

**Ruled: a racial becomes a CHAIN only if it has three genuine steps. Otherwise it stays a FEAT.**

### ⚠ A feat may add an action — owner ruling

**`ACTION-ECONOMY-01` has five budgets: `Move` · `Action` · `Bonus` · `Gear` · `Reaction`, plus one free interaction.**

**A passive feat may add a NAMED ENTRY to one of them.** **⚠ It is still a feat: nothing is chosen at level-up and nothing escalates. It means the creature can do a thing on its turn that nothing else can.**

    Scrap-Eater      Action   destroy one unattended object of its size or smaller
    Dextrous Hands   Action   fetch, carry, or work one simple mechanism
    Bore             Move     movement may pass through stone at half speed
    Deep Hide        Move     may end its move underground, unreachable
    ⚠ Beneath Notice  none    purely passive — adds nothing to any budget

> **⚠ This is a general mechanism, not a beast one.** **It gives the corpus a third thing a feat can be, between *a passive modifier* and *a chain*.**

### The split — three ways, not two

    ⚠ CHAIN   Echolocation      range, uses per day, and detail all escalate
    ⚠ RIDER   Gnaw              it modifies a bite — PT-428's weapon-profile slot
    FEAT      Scrap-Eater · Dextrous Hands · Bore · Deep Hide · Beneath Notice

**⚠ `Scrap-Eater` was proposed as a chain and the owner ruled it a feat that adds an action.** **Correct: *destroy one object* has no second step that is not arbitrary.**

### `Echolocation` — the chain, and the check makes it interesting

    Echolocation   1    Action, 3/day.  Alertness vs Stealth, or DC 15 for an object
                        SUCCESS: everything within 12 squares, INCLUDING what is Hidden
                        ⚠ FAILURE: still maps everything that is NOT hidden
    Read the Echo  6    5/day, 16 squares — a success names WHAT KIND of thing it found
    Pierce        12    7/day, 20 squares — maps through walls, doors and closed ground

**⚠ A FAILED check is never wasted.** **The beast always learns the room; the check decides whether it also finds what is hiding in it.**

**⚠ Gated `1 / 6 / 12` — `PT-487`. A utility chain climbs like `Guarding Stance`, not like `Flurry`.**

**⚠ AND IT IS THE ONLY CHAIN ON THE ROSTER THAT IS NOT AN ATTACK.** **`PT-438` counted chains as attack trees; this is the first that resolves nothing against a Defence.**

### ⚠ The Shyrack's racial slot is now EMPTY

**`Echolocation` left the feat column for the chain document.** **The Shyrack holds `Swarm` and `Flyby Attack` from its tags, sonic on its weapon, and NO racial.**

**⚠ Second beast in that state, after the Laigrek.** **Both are next.**

## PT-493 — `scythe` added. ⚠ The natural-weapon vocabulary is OPEN

### The rule, stated generally — owner ruling

> **⚠ A beast's attack TYPES come from the beast.** **Not from its type, not from its size, and not from a template.**

**`PT-484` ruled this for the Iriaz and treated it as a one-off correction. It is the general case.**

### `Laigrek` — `scythe`, not `claw`

    PT-356 template   bite 1d6 · claw 1d4      ⚠ neither word is in any source
    PT-492            claw 1d6 · claw 1d4      the bite removed
    ⚠ PT-493          scythe 1d6 · scythe 1d4

**Wookieepedia: *six SCYTHE-SHAPED legs* · *the inner surfaces of its KNIFE-LIKE LOWER LIMBS bearing JAGGED EDGES*.**

**⚠ *Claw* was the template's word for anything that is not a bite. The source's word is scythe.** **A jagged blade is not a claw, and calling it one loses the only distinctive thing about how this creature kills.**

**⚠ Name-checked: the only three `scythe` hits in the corpus are my own QUOTATIONS of this source, in the two rulings above. Clean.**

### `scythe` takes **Precision · Power**

| Weapon | Axes | Why |
|---|---|---|
| bite | Power · Control | one mouth — it commits, and it holds |
| claw | Velocity · Precision | two of them, and they open things |
| **⚠ scythe** | **Precision · Power** | **a bladed limb. It cuts deep, and it commits.** |
| gore | Position | a gore that has not moved is not a gore |
| hoof | Control | knocks down, keeps down |
| tail | Spread | one sweep, everything adjacent |
| sonic | Spread · Control | no attack roll — an area and a save |

**⚠ Deliberately NOT the same as `claw`.** **A claw is fast and shallow — `Velocity · Precision`. A scythe is heavy and sharp — `Precision · Power`.** **They share `Precision` because both cut; they differ on whether the limb is quick or committed.**

**⚠ And it fits the beast: `Str 14`, two strikes, `armoured`.** **A Laigrek is not fast. It is armoured and it swings blades.**

### ⚠ The vocabulary is OPEN, and that is the point

**A new weapon type needs ONE thing to join the table: an axis assignment.**

> **⚠ `PT-486` fixed six types and read as a closed list. It is not.** **The list is whatever the roster's anatomies require, and it will grow as beasts are read properly.**

**⚠ Candidates already visible in the sources and NOT yet acted on:** **the Laigrek's *small horns on its back end* and *thorn-like mounds along its sides*; the Nexu's quills; the Dianoga's tentacles.**

### ⚠ Third template defect in three beasts

    Gizka      Dex 18   ⚠ its file says 10          PT-455
    Iriaz      claws    ⚠ it charges with horns     PT-484
    Laigrek    bite     ⚠ it has no jaws            PT-492/493

**`PT-356` derived every attack line from RCR's per-type tables without reading a single creature.** **Every beast read carefully since has been wrong.**

**⚠ Twenty-two have not been read carefully.**
