## PT-540 — The basic attacks named. ⚠ An attack must not share a name with its weapon

    bite       Bite        ⚠ kept — no better verb exists
    claw       Swipe
    gore       Toss        a horned animal does not stab; it HOOKS AND THROWS
    hoof       Buck        ⚠ kicking BACKWARD — which is the rider verbatim
    sting      Sting       ⚠ kept
    tail       Tail Whip
    tentacle   Wrap        it GRIPS rather than crushes — `PT-515`
    sonic      Screech

### ⚠ The reason is mechanical, not aesthetic

    Bite  233 hits    Claw  184    Gore  93    Sting  35

**Those counts are the WEAPON names. ⚠ An attack called `Claw` is UNRESOLVABLE by `audit_refs` — it cannot tell *"the claw weapon"* from *"the `Claw` attack"* — and neither can a reader.**

**⚠ `Bite` and `Sting` are KEPT anyway, owner ruling.** **No better verb exists for either, and the ambiguity is worth less than a bad name.**

### ⚠ `Buck` — I am reversing myself deliberately

**`PT-485` REJECTED `Buck` for the Iriaz's charge chain: *"wrong behaviour entirely. That is a mount throwing a rider."***

> **⚠ As a BASIC HOOF ATTACK it is the opposite case — literal and exact.** **A backward kick IS a buck, and `PT-539`'s rider reads *"may be made against a creature BEHIND the beast without turning."***

**Same word, different job. Recorded so this reads as a reversal rather than a forgotten ruling.**

### `Toss` earns its rider

**`PT-539` gave `gore` *"`+2` damage if the beast moved at least 2 squares first."*** **⚠ `Toss` says why: a horned animal does not stab. It gets under the thing and throws it, and that needs momentum.**

**⚠ `Bite · Swipe · Screech` — the Shyrack, the first three-weapon tier-1 beast.**

## PT-541 — Nexu, Wraid, Gundark, Tuk'ata. ⚠ A fourth `bite · Control` variant, and a chain gated by a BAND

### `Nexu` — and the source describes `Take Down` exactly

    Rake → Flense → Shred            claw · VELOCITY
    Open → Lay Bare → Unmake         claw · PRECISION
    Take Down → Bear Under → Throatlock   bite · CONTROL, the AMBUSH variant

***"It would CLIMB TOWARDS ITS VICTIM, STRIKE, then return to the ground quickly, waiting to see if its enemy would strike back."***

**⚠ That is the Maalraas's ambush chain, performed by a different animal.** **`Climber` and `Four Eyes` are how it arranges the approach — it comes from above, in the dark, seeing heat.**

**⚠ `It tires` is the COST — `PT-516`.** **A nexu that has not finished the fight in three rounds is losing it.**

### `Wraid` — ⚠ `Overbear`, the FOURTH `bite · Control` variant

    Overbear   1   +1d6, and if an ALLY is adjacent the target falls prone
    Bear In    4   +2d6, and the wraid may move into the square it occupied
    Beset      8   +3d6, and a prone target adjacent to BOTH cannot stand

**⚠ CONDITION: an ALLY must be adjacent. Alone, the wraid has the damage and NONE of the rest.**

**⚠ The four variants are genuinely four different things:**

    Worry      Cannok     it takes your THINGS
    Latch On   Boma       it holds you and EATS
    Take Down  Maalraas   it puts you DOWN, from where you were not looking
    ⚠ Overbear Wraid      it needs a FRIEND

***"Pack organisms by nature, often found in clusters anywhere between 2 and 6"* — `PT-484`.**

### `Gundark` — ⚠ A CHAIN GATED BY A BAND

    Young Gundark   1–11   strikes 1   ⚠ NOT `paired`   `Maul` · `Rake`
    ⚠ Gundark       12+    strikes 2   ⚠ `paired`       + `Twin Strike`, gated 12/16/20

> **⚠ IT CANNOT HOLD `Twin Strike` BEFORE THE BAND.** **A young gundark has TWO arms and ONE strike; the chain requires two weapons arriving together and it has nothing to pair.**

    Pounce → Upend → Skewer      gore · POSITION, the AMBUSH variant
    Rake → Flense → Shred        claw · VELOCITY
    Open → Lay Bare → Unmake     claw · PRECISION

**⚠ `gore` opens ONE axis and `claw` opens TWO — exactly three.** **Fourth beast whose set was DETERMINED rather than chosen, after the Katarn, Kinrath and Laigrek.**

**⚠ `Pounce` is right because it is a TOMB GUARDIAN** — it waits in the dark and is on you before you know the corridor is occupied. **`Darkvision` is how it arranges that.**

## PT-544 — `Bloodscent` CUT to a feat. `Unfeeling` is the Terentatek's fourth chain

### ⚠ Detection has no natural escalation

**`PT-543` wrote `Bloodscent` as a three-tier chain: 100 metres, then a kilometre, then a day-old trail.**

> **⚠ THAT WAS THREE NUMBERS PRETENDING TO BE A DESIGN.** **A beast either knows where you are or it does not.** **Owner ruling: it is a FEAT.**

**`Bloodscent` — it knows the direction and rough distance of every FORCE-SENSITIVE creature within 1 kilometre, through walls, darkness and concealment, and follows a trail up to a day old across any terrain, INCLUDING WATER.**

**⚠ FORCE-SENSITIVE, not *"with a Force class level"* — owner ruling.** **It feeds on Force-sensitive BLOOD, and that is a property of the PERSON rather than of their training.**

**⚠ It sits close to `PT-480`'s senses rule — *"how a species perceives is not a feat."*** **Recorded as a FEAT because it does more than perceive: it TRACKS, across water, a day later. Flagged rather than argued.**

### ⚠ AND IT MAKES `Unnerve` INCONSISTENT

**The Hssiss's chain — `PT-538` — reads *"a creature with a FORCE CLASS LEVEL."*** **`Bloodscent` now reads FORCE-SENSITIVE.**

> **⚠ Two effects keying on the same idea, using two different tests, three rulings apart.** **NOT RECONCILED — and the difference is real: a Force-sensitive with no Force class levels is findable by one and immune to the other.**

### `Unfeeling` — ⚠ the only DEFENSIVE chain on the roster

    Unfeeling            1   ⚠ as a REACTION, once per encounter, it ignores one
                             Force power targeting it ENTIRELY — no save, no effect
    Dead to It           6   twice per encounter, ⚠ and an AREA power does not
                             touch it either
    Nothing Reaches It  12   three times, area as above, ⚠ and a Force-user who
                             targets it must make a Will save or LOSE THE POINTS SPENT

**⚠ CONDITION: it works only on FORCE POWERS. A lightsaber, a blaster and a fist all reach it normally.**

**PORTED, and `PT-520` already recorded that our `−8` is a SOFTENING:** ***"A terentatek's hide was highly resistant — IN SOME CASES EVEN IMMUNE"*, and Jedi hunting them *"had to rely on their WEAPONRY SKILLS ALONE."***

> **⚠ `Force-Hunter Hide` is the constant `−8`. This chain is the *"in some cases even immune"* half — and it is the reason the Great Hunt sent Jedi with SWORDS.**

**⚠ EVERY OTHER CHAIN DOES SOMETHING TO A TARGET. THIS ONE REFUSES TO HAVE SOMETHING DONE.**

**⚠ And it spends no Force Points, which is now deliberate rather than an oversight: a terentatek does not USE the Force. It is a hole where the Force does not work.**

## PT-545 — `Turn Aside → Shed → Consume`. ⚠ A Fortitude save, a cost, and the first pool that refills

**Owner rulings: rename it, make it cost Force Points, and attach a DC it usually makes.**

    Turn Aside   1   FP 4 · reaction · once per encounter · ⚠ Fortitude DC 10
                     On a success the power is negated ENTIRELY.
                     ⚠ On a failure the FP 4 is still spent.
    Shed         6   FP 4 · twice · and AREA powers are included
    Consume     12   FP 4 · three times · ⚠ on a success it TAKES the Force
                     Points the caster spent, up to its own maximum

### ⚠ FORTITUDE, because the resistance is a HIDE

***"A terentatek's HIDE was highly resistant — in some cases even immune — to the effects of the Force."***

**⚠ It saves with the BODY. Its Fortitude is `Strong` and its Will is `Weak` — it should roll the one it is good at.**

    BM 1    +2   ⚠ about 65%
    BM 12   +8   ⚠ about 95%

> **⚠ `DC 10` on a strong ladder is EASY AND NEVER CERTAIN.** **It shrugs off almost everything and occasionally does not — which is what *"in some cases even immune"* describes.** **Not a wall. A hide that usually holds.**

**⚠ A FAILURE STILL COSTS THE `FP 4`.** **It cannot spam the reaction, and a bad roll wastes the resource.**

### ⚠ `Consume` is the first thing that REFILLS a beast pool

**`PT-506` flagged that beast pools have NO REGENERATION RULE — `REST-AND-MEDITATION-01` restores a pool through MEDITATION, and a beast does not meditate.**

**⚠ `Consume` is the first answer, and a narrow one: the terentatek refills ONLY by eating what a Force-user spent.** **`FP 4` from `24` is six uses a day, against per-encounter caps of one, two and three.**

### ⚠ AND IT CORRECTS `PT-544`, WHICH I ARGUED MYSELF INTO

**I wrote that the chain spends nothing because *"a terentatek does not USE the Force — it is a hole where the Force does not work."***

> **⚠ That reads well and LEFT `24 FP` DOING NOTHING.** **`PT-506` and `PT-538` had both flagged the unused pool and I wrote a sentence that made the flag sound like a design.**

**A hole that COSTS something to maintain is the better idea. Owner's.**

### Names

**`Deny Force` was considered and set aside — two words, and *"Force"* in a beast chain name reads like a POWER rather than a HIDE.** **Every other beast chain is what the ANIMAL DOES.**

**⚠ `Turn Aside → Shed → Consume`: refuse, reject, FEED.** **`Shed` is the one that earns it — a hide sheds things, which is the physical reading the Fortitude save wants.**

    Drive Off    12   as above, and on a win by 10 or more: pushed 4 and PRONE

## PT-547 — Four open items closed. ⚠ And `Meat-Fed` cut

### ⚠ 1 · A BEAST'S FEATS COME WITH THE BEAST. THE CHAINS ARE GATED

**`PT-431` left open whether a PURCHASED beast gets its racial feat, and `BEASTS-FEATS-01` named the risk: *"if it does, anyone buys `Bore` and walks through walls."***

> **⚠ RULED: racial feats, tag grants and senses ALWAYS come with the beast. They are what the animal IS.** **A duracrete slug that could not bore would not be a duracrete slug.**

**⚠ THE EXPLOIT DIES ON THE GATE, NOT ON THE PURCHASE.**

    Bore the FEAT     the slug's movement passes through EARTH
    Bore the CHAIN    ⚠ PT-532, gated 4 / 10 / 16 — stone at 10, durasteel at 16

**⚠ A level-1 character can buy a duracrete slug. He gets a slow, blind, indifferent animal that can push through soil.** **He does not get a key to a blast door until he is a 16th-level Beast Master.**

**⚠ Same everywhere: `Nimble Fingers` opens a LATCH at 1 and a console at 6; `Underfoot` gnaws a bulkhead at 12; `Echolocation` reaches through walls at 12.** **The feats are free and small; the chains are gated and large.**

### ⚠ 2 · FORCE-SENSITIVITY is the test, everywhere

**`PT-538` wrote `Unnerve` as *"a creature with a FORCE CLASS LEVEL."*** **`PT-544` wrote `Bloodscent` as *"FORCE-SENSITIVE."*** **Three rulings apart, and I flagged it rather than fixed it.**

**⚠ UNIFIED ON FORCE-SENSITIVE.** **A hssiss influences what a terentatek can smell, and both key on what the PERSON IS rather than on what they have trained.**

**⚠ A Force-sensitive with no class levels was findable by one and immune to the other. No longer.**

### ⚠ 3 · Beast Force pools regenerate by SLEEPING

**`PT-506` flagged that beast pools have NO recovery: `REST-AND-MEDITATION-01` restores a pool through MEDITATION and a beast does not meditate.**

> **⚠ IT DOES NOT NEED TO. A beast recovers its ENTIRE pool after eight hours of REST — the same eight hours a character spends meditating. The beast sleeps through it.**

**⚠ A beast's pool is `8 × tier` and FIXED. It does not grow with skill, it is not spent on choices, and there is no reason to make it recover slowly.**

**⚠ `Consume` — `PT-545` — remains the only IN-COMBAT refill and is still worth having.** **A terentatek that has spent its pool by round three does not get it back by sleeping later.**

### ⚠ 4 · `Roar → Howl → Dread` regated `1 / 6 / 12`

**It casts `Fear`, `Horror` and `Insanity`, and `PT-447` makes all three apply `cowering` — ⚠ A CONDITION THAT REMOVES A TURN.**

> **⚠ `PT-487`'s own test names this case: *"a chain that removes a turn, or ends in permanent loss, climbs slower."*** **`Guarding Stance` and `Parry` are `1 / 6 / 12` for exactly that reason.**

**⚠ `Roar` was written at `PT-443`, BEFORE the test existed, and nothing re-read it afterwards.** **Same shape as `PT-530`: `PT-119` named the third save rung and nobody re-read the class documents against the new vocabulary.**

**Holders: Zakkeg · Drexl *(adult)* · Terentatek · Gundark · Rancor — every `apex` beast.**

### `Meat-Fed → Reddened → Red Ruin` — CUT, owner ruling

**⚠ It made a beast better at fighting and worse at obeying, and it required FEEDING A HERBIVORE MEAT between fights.**

**The lore is real — *"fed meat… turned their leathery skin crimson and made the reeks much more aggressive"* — but it describes ARENA REEKS.** **⚠ A Beast Master carrying corpses to keep a mount angry is not the game.**

**⚠ The Reek's fourth chain is OPEN again.**

## PT-550 — The Reek moves to TIER 2. ⚠ Its "missing fourth chain" was a tiering error

### ⚠ Why a rhinoceros was in tier 3

**Tier 3 is `DC 32`, NOT FOR SALE, and its other four members all hunt and eat people — Zakkeg, Drexl, Terentatek, Rancor.**

**⚠ The Reek is a HERBIVORE THAT GETS RIDDEN.** **`BEASTS-OBEDIENCE-01` already called it *"the easiest apex-tier beast to handle"*, and its `DC 23` was the LOWEST in the band by two points.**

    Reek        23   ⚠ lowest in tier 3
    Drexl       25 · Zakkeg 26 · Terentatek 27 · Rancor 28

**⚠ MOVED. It sits at the TOP of tier 2, tied with the Nexu at `DC 23` — the heaviest thing in the band.** **Owner ruling: *"a high up tier 2, naturally."***

### ⚠ AND THE FOURTH CHAIN PROBLEM DISSOLVES

**`PT-547` cut `Meat-Fed` and left the slot open. `PT-548` considered a herd chain and refused to write one.** **I spent three rulings looking for a fourth chain.**

> **⚠ AT TIER 2 IT IS OWED THREE, AND IT HAS THREE:** **`Bull Rush` · `Stomp` · `Lock Horns`.**

**⚠ `PT-531` called it *"the MOST WEAPON-STARVED beast on the roster"* — two axes against four chains.** **IT ONLY WAS BECAUSE THE TIER WAS WRONG.** **The starvation was a TIERING error wearing a design problem's clothes, and I wrote a whole rule — `PT-531`'s utility-chain fallback — partly to solve it.**

**⚠ The rule survives and is right for the Duracrete Slug and the Terentatek. The Reek was never its real case.**

**Dice fall `1d12 / 1d10` → `1d10 / 1d8`. ⚠ Still the heaviest hitter in tier 2 at `Str 22`.**

### ⚠ AND THE TIER 3 HEADER WAS LOST FOR THE SECOND TIME

**`PT-500` deleted it by cutting the Dianoga, whose entry sat directly above it. `PT-502` restored it.**

> **⚠ MOVING THE REEK OUT OF TIER 3 TOOK IT AGAIN — the header sat inside the block I moved.**

**⚠ A block operation by heading boundary takes the section header with it, and NOTHING CHECKS DOCUMENT STRUCTURE.** **`audit_beasts` reads entries and feat rows; it does not know sections exist.**

**Twice in fifty rulings, same cause, both caught by eye.**

## PT-551 — `audit_chains.py`, check 26. ⚠ It found two real gaps on its first run

**Written because *"24 of 24 chained"* was MY CLAIM, tracked by eye — and the eye has failed twice this session.**

    PT-541  the Gundark's `strikes` line was BLANK. It read "by band" with no
            value, and every derivation silently returned nothing for it.
    PT-550  ⚠ the `# Tier 3` header was lost TWICE — by PT-500's cut and again
            by the Reek's move — because a block operation by heading boundary
            takes the header with it.

### ⚠ IT CHECKS DOCUMENT STRUCTURE, WHICH NOTHING ELSE DOES

**The three tier headers must exist, in order.** **⚠ That is the `PT-550` defect, and `PT-550` could only record it because nothing could check it.**

**A beast's TIER is read from the section it sits under, not asserted anywhere.**

### ⚠ Two real gaps, both mine

    Shyrack      tier 1, 2 due — ⚠ only `Echolocation`
    Young Boma   tier 2, 3 due — its own heading said "not yet written"

**⚠ `PT-539` gave the Shyrack its `sonic` weapon and `PT-543` never gave it the chain.** **`Keening → Rupture → Shatter` written — sonic · SPREAD.**

> **⚠ IT HITS FRIEND AND FOE ALIKE AND IT DEAFENS ITS OWN ALLIES.** **And a `deafened` shyrack is BLIND — `PT-480` — so an ally who deafens it back has taken `Echolocation` and everything else away from it.** **The only beast that can disable itself.**

**The Boma's `Maul` and `Rake` written; `Latch On` already arrived at its band.**

### ⚠ AND THE DOCUMENT RECORDS CHAINS TWO WAYS

**A checker that read only one form reported the other as missing.**

    (a) a `## Beast — ...` section with `### ` chain headings
    (b) a row in an ASSIGNMENT TABLE — `PT-532`'s five tier-1 beasts

> **⚠ THAT INCONSISTENCY IS THE FINDING.** **Five beasts have their chains in a table and nineteen have sections, and nothing said so until a parser tried to count them.**

**Both forms are now read.**

### ⚠ Two parser defects fixed in the SCRIPT, not the documents

**A `###` heading counts only if it NAMES a chain in backticks.** **Prose headings — *"### ⚠ Why FORTITUDE, and why `DC 10`"* — were being counted as chains, which gave the Terentatek SEVEN.**

**⚠ A growth beast's heading names BOTH bands — *"## Young Boma → Boma"* — so the leading band is the entry key.** **Without that split the Boma read as having no chains at all when it had four.**

### Registered as gate check 26, blocking

    tier 1   12 beasts · 2 due each
    tier 2    8 beasts · 3 due each
    tier 3    4 beasts · 4 due each
    ⚠ every beast holds the chains its tier requires

**⚠ Over-counts are reported as ADVISORIES, not failures.** **A chain named inside explanatory prose inflates the count, and I would rather over-report than miss a gap.**

## PT-552 — `Survival` added. ⚠ And the Beast Master had NO APTITUDE BLOCK

### ⚠ I argued against this and was half right

**`PT-551` closed with: *"a beast doesn't track by TRAINING. It tracks because it has a NOSE."*** **That is TRUE AND IT ONLY COVERS BEASTS.**

> **⚠ A CHARACTER HAD NO WAY TO TRACK, FORAGE, READ WEATHER OR SHELTER AT ALL.** **`Scavenging` is `Wis` but it is about finding usable JUNK, not wilderness.**

**Both readings were true and I checked one. Owner ruling: add it.**

**`Survival` · `Wis` · aptitude-eligible. Tracking, foraging, shelter, terrain and weather.**

**⚠ AND IT DOES NOT OVERRIDE A SENSE.** **A creature with `Scent`, `Tremorsense`, `Acute Hearing`, `Echolocation` or `Bloodscent` does NOT roll it for anything that sense answers — it simply knows.** **The senses stay superior, which is what `PT-480` intended.**

### ⚠ NO SPECIES CONVERSIONS, and that is the finding

**Four species carry survival-adjacent traits. ⚠ NONE should become a `+2 Survival`.**

    Kaleesh      Hunter's Scent     detect by smell — 20 m upwind, 6 down
    Bith         Heightened Smell   identify an individual by scent, ⚠ a WISDOM check
    Nikto, Pale  Weather Sense      ⚠ "you KNOW what the weather will do"
    Zabrak       Highland Bred      no difficult-terrain penalty, +2 Athletics on climbs

> **⚠ `Weather Sense` gives the ANSWER WITHOUT A ROLL. A `+2 Survival` would make it a check you might FAIL — a downgrade dressed as integration.**

**⚠ The scent traits are SENSES, and the Bith's rolls a WISDOM check rather than a skill check — deliberately.** **`Highland Bred` is terrain-specific and already pairs with `Athletics`.**

**They were built to BYPASS ROLLS, and `Survival` arriving does not change that.**

### Five classes gain the aptitude

    Scout            11 → ⚠ 12
    Soldier           6 → ⚠ 7
    Bounty Hunter     8 → ⚠ 9
    Treasure Hunter  10 → ⚠ 11

### ⚠⚠ AND THE BEAST MASTER HAD NO APTITUDE BLOCK AT ALL

**`SKILLS-01 §11` lists SIXTEEN classes. ⚠ THE BEAST MASTER IS NOT AMONG THEM.**

> **⚠ The class whose entire feature is a living companion had NO SKILL LIST.** **`Beast Handling` is its obedience skill — `PT-510` — and the class that rolls it was not recorded as having aptitude in it.**

**Written: `Beast Master — 9`. `Alertness · Athletics · Beast Handling · Medicine · Scavenging · Stealth · Survival · Swim · Acrobatics`.**

**⚠ Found only because `Survival` needed adding to it.** **Nothing checks that every class on `CLASS-ROSTER-01` has an aptitude block, and the roster and `SKILLS-01` have disagreed silently for the length of the project.**

## PT-555 — Beasts get six ability scores, a skill menu, and aptitudes. ⚠ `Fly` is a new skill

**`rules/BEASTS-SKILLS-01.md`. Before this NO beast had a skill, a rank, an aptitude, or an `Int` score.**

### ⚠ Sixteen of twenty-four had mental scores in the FILES and none reached an entry

    Tuk'ata      Int 8  Wis 6  Cha 9    ⚠ confirms "unusually intelligent"
    Drexl        Int 8  Wis 8  Cha 8
    Terentatek   Int 3  Wis 10 Cha 10   ⚠ low Int, high Wis/Cha — a Force hunter
    Maalraas     Int 5  Wis 5  Cha 12   ⚠ the highest Cha on the roster
    ⚠ Iriaz      Int 10 Wis 10 Cha 10   ⚠ THE PLACEHOLDER FLAGGED AT PT-484
    ⚠ six beasts Int 3  Wis 3  Cha 6    a FILE DEFAULT

**⚠ Every entry carried `Str · Dex · Con` and stopped.** **`Alertness` is `Wis`, `Intimidate` is `Cha`, `Survival` is `Wis` — none of them could be rolled.**

**⚠ File values taken where real. Eight authored, and the Iriaz's placeholder replaced:** **`Wis 12` — it notices first, and `Skittish` is its whole identity.** **Nexu `Wis 10` for four eyes and infrared; Katarn and Reek `Wis 8`; Kath Hound `Cha 8` for *"docile, clever, and it wants to please."***

**⚠ Owner floor: minimum 3 in every ability. The Gizka's `Cha 3` was the only score that touched it.**

### ⚠ The CHARACTER skill-point formula does not work on beasts

**It is *base + Int modifier*, and `Int 3` is a `−4` MODIFIER.** **Every beast lands on zero or below.**

> **⚠ `2 + ⌊(Int − 3) ÷ 2⌋` per level, minimum 2 — it reads off `Int` WITHOUT the modifier's steep curve.**

    Int 3–4 → 2 points · Int 5 → 3 · Int 8 → ⚠ 4

**A tuk'ata gets TWICE a cannok's points, which is what its lore-confirmed `Int 8` should mean, and no beast becomes a skill monkey.**

**⚠ `SKILLS-01 §11.1` governs cost and cap UNCHANGED — and every rule the owner named ALREADY EXISTED: `1` point with aptitude and `2` without; cap is level + 3 with, half without.** **At level 1 that is `4` and `2`. Nothing had to be authored.**

### The menu — ten skills, fifteen closed

**⚠ TEN are `Int`-based and beast `Int` runs 3 to 8.** **A beast cannot be trained in a body of knowledge.** **`Persuade` and `Streetwise` need language; `Medicine` and `Mysticism` are knowledge wearing a `Wis` key; `Beast Handling` is the MASTER'S skill — `PT-510`.**

**⚠ `Intimidate` is restricted to `apex` or Large-or-bigger, and `Sleight of Hand` to the TACH ALONE — the only beast with hands.**

### ⚠ `Fly` — a new skill, and it needed two homes

**Added to `SKILLS-01`'s own table, not only the beast document. ⚠ If a player species ever flies it will want the same entry.**

**⚠ AND THE CHECKS IMMEDIATELY DEMANDED MORE:**

    audit_skillfeats   >> covered by no feat: ['Fly']
    audit_classskills  >> class skill for nobody: ['Fly']

**`Fly` added to `Nimble` — `Acrobatics · Swim · Fly`, the body-control trio — and to the `Scout`, now 13.** **26 skills, all covered, all a class skill somewhere.**

### ⚠ A SENSE OUTRANKS A SKILL

**A beast with `Scent`, `Tremorsense`, `Darkvision`, `Acute Hearing`, `Echolocation`, `Blind` or `Bloodscent` does NOT roll `Survival` or `Alertness` for anything that sense answers.**

**⚠ The skill covers what the sense does NOT — reading weather, choosing ground, foraging where nothing is buried.** **Which is why `Alertness` still matters to the Iriaz, and why the Katarn's `Scent` makes its `Survival` ranks a formality on ground crossed within the day.**

## PT-556 — The beast level table. ⚠ `Fly` is BEAST ONLY, and full attack is the ladder

### ⚠ `Fly` does not appear on a character's skill list at all

**Owner ruling. `PT-555` put it in `SKILLS-01`'s table, gave it to `Nimble`, and added it to the Scout. ⚠ ALL THREE REVERTED.**

**⚠ It is a NEW SHAPE.** **The droid precedent — `DROID-SKILLS-01` — is *"everyone has it except droids."*** **This is *"only beasts have it"*, and even among beasts only the `flying` tag opens it.**

> **⚠ BOTH SKILL CHECKS ASSUMED EVERY SKILL IS A CHARACTER SKILL, AND THE ASSUMPTION WAS NEVER STATED.** **`audit_skillfeats` demands a feat cover it; `audit_classskills` demands some class hold it. A beast-only skill can satisfy neither.**

**Both taught to exempt beast-only skills. ⚠ 25 skills covered, 25 a class skill somewhere, and `Fly` outside both sets by design.**

### Full attack — `cls_atk_1`, `+1` per level

**Owner constraint: *"beasts should all be enabled to obtain their full attack trees, so it should be based off what a beast has available to them."***

> **⚠ A BEAST IS ITS ATTACKS.** **No class features, no equipment, no Force powers, no skill tricks.** **Everything a character gets from gear, feats and powers, a beast gets from HITTING THINGS — the reduced ladder would take away the only thing it contributes.**

**⚠ `cls_atk_2` reaches `+21` at level 28. A Rancor missing with `2d8` tusks is not a rancor.**

### ⚠ Ability increases at 6 / 12 / 18 / 24 / 30 — FIXED, not chosen

**Five against a character's seven. ⚠ A beast does not TRAIN. It GROWS.**

**⚠ AND THEY LAND ON THE GROWTH BANDS** — K'lor'slug 6 and 12, Boma and Kath Hound 12, Nexu/Gundark/Drexl 16, Rancor 28. **A beast improving on the same beats it transforms on reads as ONE event rather than two.**

    Str   Cannok · Young Boma · Wraid · Zakkeg · Rancor · Gundark
    Dex   Tach · Gizka · Mykal · Nexu · Shyrack · Laigrek
    Con   Duracrete Slug · K'lor'slug · Kinrath
    Wis   ⚠ Iriaz · Katarn · Kath Hound · Reek — they NOTICE FIRST
    Cha   ⚠ Maalraas · Hssiss · Tuk'ata · Terentatek · Drexl — `Force-touched`
          and `apex`. Their Force pool and `Roar` DCs read off presence.

**⚠ At 30 that is `+5` in one score. A Terentatek ends at `Cha 15`; a Rancor at `Str 35`.**

### ⚠ The only choice in the whole table is where SKILL POINTS go

**Everything else is automatic — attack bonus, vitality, saves, ability increases, chain tiers, band changes.**

**⚠ Left to the beast, points go to its FIRST-LISTED aptitude until capped, then the second.** **A cannok left alone becomes very good at scavenging and nothing else, which is what a cannok would do.**

### ⚠ `NaturalAC` STILL HAS NOT REACHED A SINGLE ENTRY

**`PT-432` named FOUR per-beast constants: vitality die, natural armour, attack count, and the ability block.**

> **⚠ `strikes` reached the entries at `PT-492`, sixty rulings late. `natural armour` has not reached them at all.** **A BEAST HAS NO DEFENCE VALUE, and a level table that adds to Defence has nothing to add to.**

**⚠ And nothing states what happens when a beast DIES — `PT-153` recorded that no cost was ever set.**

## PT-557 — Defence, tiered. ⚠ `PT-432`'s fourth constant finally reaches the entries

**⚠ `PT-432` named FOUR per-beast constants. `strikes` arrived at `PT-492`, sixty rulings late. `natural armour` had NEVER ARRIVED AT ALL — a beast had no Defence value.**

### ⚠ The file values do not port

    Rancor      17   Huge, CR 20
    Wraid       11   ⚠ CR 5 — higher than the Terentatek at CR 10
    ⚠ Laigrek    0   OUR ARMOURED BEAST, with `Layered Armour`
    Iriaz        0   CR 1

> **⚠ THE LAIGREK AT ZERO IS THE TELL.** **It carries `armoured` AND `Layered Armour` — *"a layered and armored exoskeleton"* — and its file says no natural armour at all.**

**⚠ These are KOTOR's AC numbers on KOTOR's scale. `PT-497` already frames them as the WILD creature.** **DERIVED instead, the way `PT-486` derived dice and `PT-119` derived saves.**

### The rule

> **`10` + natural armour + `Dexterity` modifier + size modifier.**

    SIZE   Tiny 0 · Small 1 · Medium 2 · Large 4 · Huge 6 · Colossal 8
    TIER   ⚠ tier 1 +0 · tier 2 +2 · tier 3 +4
    TAG    armoured +2

**⚠ THE SIZE MODIFIER RUNS THE OTHER WAY — `Tiny +2` down to `Colossal −4`.** **A bigger target is easier to HIT and harder to HURT, and the two partly cancel.**

### ⚠ TIER was added because size alone inverted the roster

**My first pass gave a tier-1 Laigrek `17` and a tier-3 Rancor `14`.** **Owner: *"AC should be tiered to avoid that issue."***

    tier 1   13 – 17    Gizka 13 · ⚠ Laigrek and Duracrete Slug 17, both armoured
    tier 2   16 – 18    ⚠ Wraid 18, armoured
    tier 3   18 – 20    ⚠ Zakkeg 20, armoured Huge

**⚠ The only overlaps are ARMOURED beasts, which is the tag doing its job.** **An armoured tier-1 matching an unarmoured tier-2 is the point of carrying the tag.**

**⚠ AND IT DOES NOT REPLACE `armoured`'s DAMAGE REDUCTION — `PT-527`.** **`DR 5`, `DR 10` at Large or bigger, is what gets THROUGH the hide. Defence is whether you connect at all.**

## PT-558 — Beasts and droid companions DIE on Normal. ⚠ A droid can be rebuilt and a beast cannot

**Owner ruling. ⚠ It AMENDS `DEATH-AND-DIFFICULTY-01 §2`, which said the opposite.**

    was     "a henchman, A BEAST COMPANION, or a droid is not [dead] — it is
             out for the encounter and recovers"
    now     ⚠ a player, a BEAST COMPANION and a DROID COMPANION all die at −10.
             A HENCHMAN gets up.

    EASY    ⚠ it does not die unless the WHOLE PARTY dies — unchanged
    NORMAL  ⚠ permanent
    HARD    ⚠ permanent

> **⚠ THE TWO COMPANION CLASSES WERE THE ONLY ONES PLAYING WITHOUT A STAKE AT THE DEFAULT DIFFICULTY.**

### ⚠ The droid rebuilds. The beast does not.

**`DEATH-AND-DIFFICULTY-01 §5` already said a Droid Master's droids are *"built, commanded, permanent until destroyed, and REPLACEABLE."*** **A destroyed droid companion is REPAIRED AND REBUILT TO NEW — the Droid Master loses TIME AND PARTS.**

**A Beast Master ACQUIRES ANOTHER — `BEASTS-01`'s bond DC and price, PAID AGAIN.**

> **⚠ THE REPLACEMENT IS A NEW ANIMAL AT THE MASTER'S CURRENT LEVEL.** **It does not keep the dead beast's NAME or its SKILL RANKS — ⚠ THE ONLY TWO THINGS A BEAST MASTER EVER CHOSE, `PT-556`.**

**⚠ Everything else is fixed by species, so a replacement is MECHANICALLY IDENTICAL and is not the same creature.** **That is the whole of the loss and it is deliberate.**

### ⚠ It makes `PT-151`'s constraint mechanical

**`PT-151`: *"either a devastating loss or a shrug, and both are bad."***

**`§5` answered it in PROSE — *"the Beast Master has one companion and it matters. The Droid Master has several and they are materiel."***

> **⚠ NOW IT IS A RULE. The droid is the shrug and the beast is the loss.**

**⚠ A Beast Master pays the acquisition price twice. A Droid Master pays for parts.**

### ⚠ Two things this makes load-bearing

**A beast's DEATH THRESHOLD is unstated.** **`DEATH-AND-DIFFICULTY-01 §6` already flagged it — *"`−10` assumes a character sheet; a beast may not have one at the same scale"* — and it was a curiosity while beasts could not die.** **⚠ A beast has `Defence` and a vitality die and NO WOUND TRACK.**

**⚠ And what rebuilding a droid COSTS is unstated.** **`§5` and `§2` both say replaceable and neither says the price** — which is now the difference between the two classes and cannot stay blank.

## PT-559 — ⚠ ONE POOL. `wound points` are removed from the game

**Owner ruling. `rules/PROPOSAL-VITALITY-01.md` written first; 84 references across 23 documents, 49 of them mechanical.**

### The system

    ⚠ ONE POOL — vitality. It grows every level. Damage comes off it.
    ⚠ At 0 and below a character is DYING and keeps taking damage into the
      negative. THE KILLING BLOW'S EXCESS CARRIES THROUGH.
    ⚠ DEAD at −Constitution.

    0                    Disabled — no actions, still a legal target
    −1 to −(Con − 1)     Dying — loses 1 per round, `Medicine` stabilises
    −Constitution        Dead

**⚠ AND THE WHOLE NEGATIVE BAND IS GATED ON DIFFICULTY.**

    EASY     ⚠ NEGATIVES DO NOT EXIST. At 0 a character is DOWN — up when an
             ally helps, or at 1 vitality when combat ends. No dying, no
             bleed-out, no threshold. Damage below 0 is not tracked at all.
    NORMAL   negatives apply. Players, beasts and droid companions die.
             ⚠ Henchmen use the Easy rule.
    HARD     negatives apply to everyone, henchmen included.

### ⚠ Why two pools were not earning their complexity

**Saga Edition has two pools because CRITICAL HITS BYPASS VITALITY AND STRIKE WOUNDS DIRECTLY. That is what makes wounds tense.**

> **⚠ WE NEVER HAD THAT RULE.** **Nothing in the corpus makes a critical bypass vitality; ours multiply damage like d20's.** **The second pool was a smaller vitality pool that did not grow, and we paid two-pool complexity for one-pool behaviour.**

### ⚠ Overflow now counts

**The old system threw the killing blow's excess away.** **A hit taking you from 3 vitality to 0 did EXACTLY THE SAME as one taking you from 3 to −40.**

### The two feat chains — ⚠ DOUBLED

    Tenacity → Improved → Master          +1/+2/+3 wounds  →  ⚠ +2/+4/+6 threshold
    Hardened Chassis → Improved → Master   +1/+2/+3        →  ⚠ +2/+4/+6

**⚠ A wound point was a whole point of the pool that mattered. A death-threshold point only counts in the final moments.** **At `+1/+2/+3` these feats would be near-worthless.**

**⚠ Both capstones survive INTACT.** **`Master Tenacity`'s *"Constitution damage is halved — Con drain shrinks wound capacity directly"* still works: `Con` drain now shrinks the THRESHOLD, and halving it protects the same thing.**

### ⚠⚠ THE MEDIC'S CLASS IDENTITY WAS BUILT ON THE TWO POOLS, AND I DID NOT FLAG IT IN THE PROPOSAL

**`CLASSES-STANDARD-PHB`: *"### Wounds, not vitality"*, and *"YOU CAN HEAL WOUNDS, WHICH NOTHING ELSE IN THE GAME CAN."***

> **⚠ THAT DISTINCTION DISAPPEARED THE MOMENT THE SECOND POOL DID.**

**Rebuilt on the new system's own asymmetry:**

    Field Surgery   1   1d8 vitality to an adjacent character ⚠ AT OR BELOW 0
    Stabilise       4   2d8, ⚠ and they stop DYING, and are no longer Disabled
    Back Up         8   3d8, as above, and once per encounter at 4 metres

**⚠ *"You can bring back someone who is already DYING, which nothing else in the game can."*** **A medpac restores vitality to someone still standing; nothing else touches a character past 0.**

**⚠ The section heading is now *"Below zero, not above it."*** **The class kept its shape and changed its axis.**

### ⚠ AND A DEFECT WAS FOUND WHILE SCOPING

**`ATTACKS-04`'s `Lethal Shot` and `Execute` read *"Wound threshold rises to 20%"* and *"to 25%."***

> **⚠ `wound threshold` WAS USED TWICE AND DEFINED NOWHERE.** **No base value, no rule, no other reference in the corpus.** **AND IT WAS A PERCENTAGE MECHANIC — `PT-475`'s agenda item.**

**Rewritten as a real mechanic: the target's DEATH THRESHOLD NARROWS by 2, then 4 — it dies at `−(Con − 2)` and `−(Con − 4)`.** **⚠ `Execute` also kills outright a target already at 0 or below if the hit would reach its threshold, which is what a feat called `Execute` should do.**

**⚠ `PT-475`'s percentage list is one shorter.**

### What was converted

    49 mechanical · 35 prose · 23 documents
    ⚠ FEATS-LIBRARY-01 and feats_core.json BOTH — PT-552 found them forked once
    ⚠ BEASTS-01 and GM-CREATURES-01 — the size-scaled wound tables, CUT
    ⚠ PT-558's beast threshold question, CLOSED: a beast dies at −Constitution
      like everything else. Gizka −4. Rancor −25.

## PT-560 — Mounted combat. ⚠ A mounted pair is ONE TURN

**`rules/MOUNTED-COMBAT-01.md`. Flagged missing since `PT-440`; `mountable` and four beasts depended on it.**

### ⚠ ONE TURN, and it is the whole design

> **The rider and mount share a single turn on the rider's initiative. The MOUNT contributes MOVEMENT; the RIDER contributes the ACTION.**

    Move       ⚠ the MOUNT'S speed. The rider spends no Move.
    Action     the rider's
    Bonus      ⚠ the mount makes ONE basic attack
    Gear       the rider's
    Reaction   ⚠ ONE pool between them. Not one each.

**⚠ `BEASTS-PLAYER-01`: *"that is a second character sheet, and the Beast Master is one player."*** **`PT-201` cost the project a REBUILD for exactly this, and `PT-510` was written to avoid it.**

**⚠ The mount's CHAINS are unavailable while ridden — unless the RIDER declares one as their own Action, in which case there is no Bonus attack that round.**

### ⚠ Why the mount gets ONE attack, and why it must

    UNMOUNTED   its own turn, its Action, its chains, `strikes`-many attacks
    ⚠ MOUNTED   it gives up ALL of that

> **⚠ A BEAST MASTER WHO MOUNTS THEIR OWN BEAST IS TRADING AWAY MOST OF ITS OUTPUT.** **With nothing back, NOBODY EVER RIDES, and `mountable` is a tag on four beasts that does nothing.**

**⚠ ONE basic attack. No chain, no `strikes` count, no rider effects beyond the weapon's own.** **One extra attack roll is not a second character sheet — that is the line `PT-201` crossed and this does not.**

**Mounting is LESS BEAST OUTPUT and MORE REACH AND SAFETY.**

### Ground — height is real

**A rider on a mount one size larger than a creature has `+1` Defence against it, and it has `−1` to hit the rider.**

**⚠ Dislodged when the mount hits 0 or takes a critical: `Beast Handling` `DC 15`, or fall prone and take `1d6`.**

### ⚠ Air — three altitude bands and nothing else

    GROUND   0        everything normal
    ⚠ LOW    2 sq     no melee either direction; ranged works
    ⚠ HIGH   6+ sq    NO MELEE AT ALL. Ranged only, `−2` both ways.

**⚠ A FLIER COMMITS. It may not reverse direction in a round — one turn of up to 90 degrees, at any point in its move.**

> **⚠ THAT IS THE WHOLE OF AIR MANOEUVRE AND IT IS DELIBERATELY THIN.** **A facing-and-turn-radius system is a SECOND GAME, and this is a beast rule.**

**⚠ `Flyby Attack` — free from `flying`, `PT-427` — IS the air-combat loop and it already existed.** **The mount moves, the rider attacks, the mount keeps moving, nothing provokes.**

**⚠ Falling: `1d6` per 2 squares. From HIGH that is `3d6` minimum, `DC 20` to halve it, and the rider lands prone regardless.**

### ⚠ Water is a SITUATION, not a companion

**Owner ruling: *"the water is purely for those who run into a situation where they are in water mounted combat."***

**⚠ NO BEAST ON THE ROSTER IS A WATER MOUNT — `PT-359` cut `aquatic` for having one holder.** **Written thin and honest: surface counts as difficult terrain for footing; submerged, the rider holds breath for `Constitution` rounds then checks at a rising DC or begins DYING — `PT-559`.**

**⚠ Blasters do not fire underwater. Thrown weapons travel ONE SQUARE.**

**⚠ Dislodged underwater, the rider does not fall — they simply stop moving, at whatever depth they were.**

### ⚠ Three things left open

**⚠ `Shieldback` and `Break Away` are AUTHORED — `PT-525`. Only the Drexl's `Beast Rider` is ported.** **Two of four mount feats rest on nothing but our own reasoning.**

**⚠ NOTHING STATES WHETHER A NON-BEAST-MASTER MAY RIDE.** **`mountable` is a beast tag and `Beast Handling` is the Beast Master's skill — but a Beast Rider of Onderon was not a Beast Master, and neither was Darth Bane on a drexl.**

**⚠ AND A MOUNT THAT DIES ON `Normal` DIES PERMANENTLY — `PT-558`.** **A Beast Master who loses a mount mid-flight loses the beast AND takes `3d6`.**

## PT-561 — Mounted combat, filled in. ⚠ The Bonus attack is the WEAPON'S, and anyone may ride

### ⚠ The Bonus attack carries the weapon's own rider — owner ruling

**`PT-539` gave every natural weapon a rider that is *"what DISTINGUISHES the limb."*** **Mounted, they all apply:**

    Toss        ⚠ +2 damage if the mount moved 2 squares
    Buck        ⚠ may strike a creature BEHIND the pair, without turning
    Sting       delivers the `venomous` ladder
    Tail Whip   any ADJACENT creature, not only one it faces
    Wrap        the target is −2 to move away
    Screech     ⚠ NO attack roll — 2 squares, Fortitude or `deafened`

> **⚠ A REEK CARRYING A RIDER `Toss`ES AT `+2` ALMOST EVERY ROUND.** **The mount's movement IS the pair's movement, and a reek that stood still is not being ridden anywhere.**

### ⚠ ANYONE MAY RIDE — the open item from `PT-560`, closed

**`mountable` is a property of the BEAST, not a privilege of the class.** ***The Beast Riders of Onderon were not Beast Masters, and neither was Darth Bane on a drexl.***

**⚠ What a non-Beast-Master lacks is `Beast Handling` APTITUDE — so every mounted check costs DOUBLE and caps at HALF, `SKILLS-01 §11.1`.** **They can ride. They are worse at staying on.**

**⚠ Mounting is a MOVE; dismounting is a FREE INTERACTION.** **It is harder to get onto a moving animal than off one.**

### ⚠ The pair are TWO CREATURES SHARING A SPACE

**An attacker chooses which. ⚠ THE MOUNT DOES NOT SOAK DAMAGE FOR THE RIDER** — only `Shieldback` does that, and only for the Wraid.

**The mount grants the rider `+2` Defence as COVER against ground attackers while it is Large or bigger.** **⚠ An AREA effect hits BOTH, each rolling its own save.**

**⚠ THE RIDER MAY NOT BE FLANKED BY GROUND CREATURES on a Large-or-bigger mount. The mount can.**

### ⚠ Obedience still governs, and `Three Riders` becomes literal

**A mount that will not do a thing will not do it with you on its back.**

**⚠ `PT-522` gave the Drexl `DC 25`, or `20` if THREE HANDLERS act together.** **Mounted, *"three riders"* means three people ON THE DREXL — which is exactly what the source describes.**

**⚠ A refusal does not throw the rider.** **The mount does not do the thing, and the rider has spent their Action.**

### Passengers

    Large 1 rider · Huge 2 · Colossal 3

**⚠ ONLY THE FIRST CONTROLS IT.** **Passengers act on their own initiative with their own Action and Gear and ⚠ NO MOVE — the mount's movement is not theirs to spend. A passenger who wants to move gets off.**

**⚠ Passengers do NOT add to the Reaction pool. It stays ONE for the whole pair.**

### ⚠ Force powers from the saddle — no penalty

> **⚠ A JEDI ON A DREXL IS A THING THE SETTING HAS, and a check to stay on while casting would make it a thing nobody does.**

### Charging

**`+1d6` on the rider's melee attack after 2 squares in a straight line, **and** the mount's `Toss` gets its own `+2` on top.** **⚠ The PAIR takes `−2` Defence until the rider's next turn — a charge commits both of them.**

## PT-562 — Two weapons from the saddle. ⚠ And FOUR Force powers do nothing mounted

### ⚠ Melee and ranged, both — owner ruling

**A rider keeps a melee weapon in hand and a ranged weapon slung, and switches freely between rounds.** **⚠ Neither switch costs the Gear action it would cost on foot — a saddle is where you keep the other one.**

> **⚠ ONLY THE MELEE ATTACK TAKES THE MOUNT'S BENEFITS.** **The charge bonus, the height, the `+1d6` after two squares in a line — all melee.**

**⚠ A ranged attack from the saddle gets NOTHING from the mount and still pays the `−2` if the mount moved more than half its speed.** **A blaster does not care that you are on a reek.**

**⚠ THAT IS THE TRADE: MELEE IS BETTER MOUNTED AND RANGED IS WORSE.**

### ⚠ Every Force power read. FOUR fail, all for one reason

> **⚠ THE RIDER HAS NO MOVEMENT OF THEIR OWN TO ENHANCE.** **`MOUNTED-COMBAT-01 §1`: the MOUNT'S speed is the pair's, and the rider spends no Move.**

    Burst of Speed        ⚠ "movement speed is doubled" — there is nothing to double
    Knight Speed          ⚠ as above
    Master Speed          ⚠ as above. ITS EXTRA ATTACK AND DEFENCE GO WITH IT —
                          the power is ONE effect, not three.
    Force Enlightenment   ⚠ "the best of the Jedi's SPEED, Armor and Valor powers
                          are granted." The Speed component fails, and the WHOLE
                          power is unavailable rather than partially applying.

**⚠ THE CASTER MAY STILL CAST THEM AND THE FORCE POINTS ARE SPENT EITHER WAY.** **They simply do nothing until the caster dismounts.**

**⚠ A DISMOUNTED CASTER WITH AN ACTIVE SPEED POWER KEEPS IT — the duration runs; only the EFFECT is suspended while mounted.**

### ✓ And three that work, with consequences worth stating

**⚠ `Force Camouflage` cloaks the RIDER ONLY.** **A `Large` mount underneath a hidden rider is not hidden, and the pair is trivially spotted.**

**⚠ `Battle Meditation` and the `Heal` line treat the MOUNT AS A PARTY MEMBER** — it is healed, and it gains the attack and damage bonuses. **A Beast Master with `Improved Battle Meditation` is buffing two creatures with one power.**

**⚠ `Force Wave`, `Force Push` and the area powers include the MOUNT IN THE RADIUS.** **A rider who centres one on themselves THROWS THEIR OWN MOUNT.**

**⚠ `Throw Lightsaber` is RANGED — no mount benefit, and it pays the movement penalty.**

### ⚠ Why `Master Speed` fails wholly rather than partially

**It grants doubled movement, an extra attack, and `+Defence` in one power.**

> **⚠ Splitting it would mean every power needs a mounted clause naming which half survives.** **`PT-562` rules whole-power: if the movement component is the reason the power exists, the power does not function.**

**⚠ Same for `Force Enlightenment`, which is explicitly a bundle of three.**

## PT-563 — `Ride Down`, and the rider's own area powers spare the mount

### `Ride Down` — ⚠ a MOUNT-ONLY basic attack, no tiers

**Owner ruling: a trample, as a BASIC ATTACK based on the mount's stats. ⚠ `Trample` is taken — the Iriaz's `Stomp` chain capstone, `PT-485`.**

> **The mount moves THROUGH a creature's square instead of around it.**

    REQUIRES   ⚠ the mount is at least ONE SIZE LARGER than the target, and has
               moved at least 2 squares before entering its square
    SAVE       Reflex, DC 10 + the MOUNT'S Strength modifier + the RIDER'S Beast
               Master level — ⚠ or HALF the rider's level if not a Beast Master
    FAILURE    ⚠ the mount's PRIMARY natural weapon die + its Strength modifier,
               and PRONE
    SUCCESS    half damage, no prone
    ⚠ EITHER   the mount CONTINUES ITS MOVE. It does not stop, and the square is
               not difficult terrain.

**⚠ ONCE PER ROUND, first creature only. A MOUNT DOES NOT MOW DOWN A LINE.**

    Reek     Str 22 · Toss 1d10   ⚠ 1d10+6, DC 16 + level
    Wraid    Str 17 · Bite 1d10   1d10+3, DC 13 + level
    Iriaz    Str 14 · Gore 1d6    1d6+2, DC 12 + level
    Drexl    Str 20 · Bite 2d8    ⚠ 2d8+5 — and it does this FLYING, at LOW altitude

**⚠ IT USES THE MOUNT'S OWN NUMBERS AND NOTHING ELSE**, except the rider's level in the save DC — **because a trained rider AIMS THE ANIMAL, and that is the only thing the rider contributes.**

**⚠ A non-Beast-Master uses HALF their level**, the same shape as `SKILLS-01 §11.1`'s no-aptitude halving.

**⚠ It does NOT stack with a charge.** **`Ride Down` IS the movement; §8's `+1d6` charge bonus requires a melee ATTACK and this is the MOUNT'S.**

**⚠ AND IT DOES NOT WORK AT `HIGH` ALTITUDE. There is nothing up there to ride down.**

### ⚠ The rider's own area powers do NOT hit the mount — owner ruling

**`PT-562` had `Force Wave` throwing the caster's own mount. ⚠ REVERSED.**

> **⚠ The rider and mount are ONE TURN and ONE unit for this purpose.** **A Jedi who throws their own mount off a cliff is a comedy the rules should not REQUIRE, and `Force Wave` is the single most likely power to be cast from a saddle.**

**⚠ THE EXEMPTION IS THE RIDER'S OWN CASTING, NOT A GENERAL IMMUNITY.** **An area power cast by SOMEONE ELSE still hits both, each rolling its own save — §5.**

**⚠ MOUNTED COMBAT IS COMPLETE. Agenda slot 2 closes.**

## PT-564 — ⚠ Writing the mounted rules made THREE OF FOUR mount feats say nothing

**Owner: *"I'm okay with authored as long as it's balanced."*** **⚠ The problem turned out not to be sourcing. It was REDUNDANCY.**

### ⚠ Each feat, checked against the rules that now exist

    Broad Back    "a rider may act NORMALLY from its back"
                  ⚠ §1 GRANTS THAT TO EVERY MOUNT.
                  "and it may Ramming Charge with a rider aboard"
                  ⚠ §3 LETS THE RIDER DECLARE ANY CHAIN.
                  → ⚠ THE WHOLE FEAT SAID NOTHING THE GENERAL RULE DOES NOT

    Beast Rider   "a rider may act normally" — same redundancy.
                  ⚠ Only "it FLIES with a rider aboard" was real.

    Shieldback    "the rider takes HALF DAMAGE from any attack that would hit both"
                  ⚠ §5 SAYS ATTACKS CHOOSE A TARGET. They do not hit both.
                  → ⚠ IT ANSWERED A QUESTION THE RULES DO NOT ASK

    Break Away    ⚠ REAL, and covered nowhere else. The only one that worked.

> **⚠ THREE FEATS WERE WRITTEN BEFORE THE SYSTEM THEY SIT IN.** **`PT-525` authored them when mounted combat did not exist, so they described the BASICS of riding — and `PT-560` then made the basics universal.**

### Rewritten — each now grants something the rules do not

| Feat | ⚠ Now |
|---|---|
| **Break Away** *(Iriaz)* | ⚠ **Once per encounter, a REACTION: full speed away from everything threatening it, provoking from none.** The rider comes with it. **⚠ It draws on the pair's SINGLE reaction pool.** |
| **Shieldback** *(Wraid)* | ⚠ **TOTAL COVER for the rider against anything the wraid is between them and**, and `+4` on the rider's Reflex saves from that side. **⚠ Balanced by DIRECTION — the wraid must be between them, and facing is chosen on mounting or as a free interaction.** |
| **Broad Back** *(Reek)* | ⚠ **One rider MORE than its size allows** — §7 — **and passengers ignore the `−2` movement penalty on ranged attacks.** |
| **Beast Rider** *(Drexl)* | ⚠ **It flies with a rider**, and ⚠ **changes ALTITUDE BAND FOR FREE** — §9 charges half speed to everything else. |

**⚠ `Break Away` is the only one whose meaning did not change.** ***"Prey. It notices first and it leaves first."***

**⚠ `Beast Rider` keeps the only PORTED clause and loses the redundant one.**

### ⚠ The general lesson, and it has happened before

**`PT-511`: a file marked DERIVED with no generator rots.** **⚠ This is the mirror: a FEAT written before its SYSTEM describes the system, and then the system arrives and the feat is describing the floor.**

**⚠ Nothing checks whether a feat grants anything a general rule does not.** **These four were caught because `PT-560` was written LAST WEEK; a feat written before a rule five hundred rulings ago would not be.**

## PT-565 — `Beast Rider` becomes a BEAST MASTER class feat. The Drexl's is `Wingborne`

**Owner ruling. ⚠ The name was on the wrong creature: the Beast Riders of Onderon were the PEOPLE.**

### `Beast Rider` — Beast Master 5

> **⚠ The mid-tier of a ten-level prestige class.**

    ⚠ +4 on EVERY `Beast Handling` check made while riding — obedience,
      mounting a beast not their own, and the dislodge check
    ⚠ never dislodged by a CRITICAL HIT. Only the mount reaching 0 does it,
      and then at DC 10 rather than 15.
    ⚠ mounts or dismounts as a FREE INTERACTION rather than a Move

**⚠ IT IS WHAT MAKES A BEAST MASTER BETTER AT RIDING THAN ANYONE ELSE.**

**`MOUNTED-COMBAT-01 §4` already said ANYONE may ride, and that a non-Beast-Master merely lacks `Beast Handling` APTITUDE.** **⚠ That separated a Beast Master from a passenger. THIS separates a Beast Master who took the feat from one who did not.**

**⚠ NOT A CHAIN. One feat, no tiers — `PT-490`'s test: it does not have three genuine steps.**

### `Wingborne` — the Drexl's, renamed and narrowed

    ⚠ it FLIES with a rider aboard, and changes ALTITUDE BAND FOR FREE

**`MOUNTED-COMBAT-01 §9` charges half a mount's speed to change band. ⚠ The Drexl pays nothing, which is the whole of what an air mount should be better at.**

**⚠ `Three Riders` still governs controlling it — `PT-522`.**

### ⚠ AND THE BEAST MASTER HAS NO CLASS TABLE

**`rules/` holds `CLASS-TABLES-BASE`, `-JEDI` and `-DROID`. ⚠ THERE IS NO PRESTIGE TABLE FILE AT ALL.**

> **⚠ SECOND STRUCTURAL GAP FOUND ON THIS CLASS IN TWELVE RULINGS.** **`PT-552` found it had no APTITUDE BLOCK; this finds it has no LEVEL TABLE — and neither do the other twenty-nine prestige classes.**

**⚠ `Beast Rider` is placed at LEVEL 5 on the assumption of a ten-level prestige class. THAT ASSUMPTION IS NOT WRITTEN ANYWHERE and must be confirmed when the prestige tables are built.**

**⚠ It belongs with `PT-554`'s queued prestige review — which was already scoped as *"does the requirement test the COMPETENCE, or only the ROUTE?"* and now also has to ask whether the classes have TABLES at all.**

## PT-566 — The Droid Master. ⚠ A droid NEVER refuses, NEVER levels, and has NO chains

**`rules/DROID-MASTER-01.md`. Owner ruling on shape.**

### ⚠ The owner's constraint governs the whole design

> ***"Droid as a playable species already exists, and it would just make it more complicated for everyone at the table if you had a Droid Master who basically at that point had five playable characters."***

**⚠ A BEAST IS A CHARACTER. A DROID IS A TOOL THAT MOVES.**

    Beast   one · LEVELS with you · chains · ⚠ CAN REFUSE
    Droid   ⚠ unlimited HELD · FIXED at purchase · NO chains · ⚠ NEVER REFUSES

**⚠ `BEASTS-NATURE-01`'s entire obedience system has NO DROID EQUIVALENT and will not get one.** **That is the sharpest difference between the two classes and it costs nothing.**

### Held and controlled — owner ruling

    ⚠ HELD        no limit. A Droid Master may own eight.
    ⚠ CONTROLLED  what `Command Protocol` gates. The rest stay on the ship.

**⚠ Swapping happens WHERE THE OTHERS ARE. Not an encounter-start choice, not an action — you go back to the ship.**

**⚠ THE FIRST DROID IS FREE and the rest cost credits.** **`DEATH-AND-DIFFICULTY-01 §5` already said the class gets one automatically and chooses its chassis.**

### ⚠ `Command Protocol` rebuilt — a SECOND time

**`PT-201`'s version: 2/3/4 droids ALL FOLLOWING ONE ORDER — the fix for a player taking 62% of the round.**

**⚠ The specialisation vision breaks it. An astromech and a battle droid do not want the same order.**

> **⚠ `PT-201` bounded the NUMBER OF ORDERS. `PT-566` bounds the SIZE OF EACH ORDER — the same fix on a different axis.**

**Each controlled droid may take ONE of: a MOVE, ONE basic attack, or ONE CHASSIS ACTION.**

**⚠ THREE OPTIONS AND NO CHAINS.** **Four droids is four small decisions from a menu of three, not four turns.**

**⚠ Anything beyond the menu costs the DROID MASTER'S OWN ACTION, one droid at a time.**

### ⚠ Chassis specialisation WAS ALREADY BUILT

**`DROID-SKILLS-01 §2.3` gates eight skills across four chassis. ⚠ Nothing new was needed.**

    Astromech  ⚠ repair, slice or treat — at YOUR ranks, its ability modifier
    Assassin   hide, or one `Stealth` / `Sleight of Hand` check
    Battle     ⚠ +2 its own Defence, OR grant COVER to an adjacent ally
    Remote     ⚠ scout — every creature within 12 squares, through cover

**⚠ The Astromech borrowing YOUR ranks is the Tach's `Nimble Fingers` shape — `PT-532`.**

### ⚠ UPGRADES are the progression, and they were written before the question

**`DROIDS-UPGRADE-01` — `PT-317`, `PT-318` — is the Droid Master's level table in everything but name.**

    SOCKETS   ported. Six types, 71 items, three tiers. SWAPPABLE.
    BAYS      authored. 3 / 6 / 9. ⚠ PERMANENT.

> **⚠ A DROID DOES NOT GET BETTER BY SURVIVING. IT GETS BETTER BECAUSE SOMEONE WORKED ON IT.**

**⚠ It was built for droid PLAYER CHARACTERS and answers a Droid Master question it was not written for.** **`PT-431`'s *"a purchased beast is fixed at its grade"* applies to every droid, permanently.**

### ⚠ Three things left open, and one is a CONTRADICTION

**⚠ `PT-145` says a controlled droid is a HENCHMAN. `PT-558` says a droid COMPANION dies permanently and is rebuilt.** **THOSE TWO DISAGREE, and the answer decides whether a destroyed droid is a shrug or a bill.**

**⚠ WHAT A DROID COSTS is unwritten, and `PT-225` gave CONSTRUCTION to the MACHINIST — so whether a Droid Master builds or buys needs that overlap resolved.**

**⚠ And the class has NO LEVEL TABLE. `Command Protocol 1/2/3` assumes a progression that is not written down — `PT-565`.**

## PT-567 — Seven chassis. ⚠ Three are companion-only, and four of seven barely fight

**Owner rulings. ⚠ AND THE OWNER REVERSED HIMSELF ON LEVELLING, CORRECTLY:** ***"You're right, Droid Master droids do not level. They require upgrades."***

### ⚠ Starting attacks, by chassis

    Astromech   ⚠ 1   `Blaster Integration` — and ⚠ IT MAY USE DROID ARMS
    Remote      ⚠ 1
    Probe       ⚠ 1   ⚠ NEW
    Assassin    ⚠ 2   RANGED ONLY, full chain access
    Battle      ⚠ 2   RANGED ONLY, full chain access
    Labor       ⚠ 2   ⚠ NEW — MELEE ONLY, and only adjacent
    Protocol    ⚠ 0   ⚠ NEW — ⚠ CANNOT TAKE A HOSTILE ACTION AT ALL

**⚠ A ONE-ATTACK CHASSIS HAS NO RANGED CHAINS.**

> **⚠ THE PRECEDENT ALREADY EXISTED AND I DID NOT INVENT IT.** **`ATTACKS-04` carries *"Astromechs and Remotes cannot take these"* on its `Rapid Fire`, aimed-shot and overcharge chains — `PT-333`.** **`PT-567` GENERALISES it.**

**⚠ `Droid` and `Battle` are RANGED ONLY, which is true of the playable species themselves — the companion versions inherit it rather than departing from it.**

### ⚠ The three new chassis are NOT PLAYABLE — owner ruling

**They exist to give the Droid Master options. ⚠ A player who wants to BE a droid still chooses from the original four.**

**Protocol** — `Int +2 · Cha +2 · Str −4 · Dex −2`. **⚠ NO WEAPON MOUNT OF ANY KIND — the only chassis that physically cannot be armed.** **Translates anything it has heard; `Persuade` and `Appraise` at YOUR ranks.**

**`Probe`** — `Dex +4 · Int +2 · Str −4 · Con −2`. **Hovers, `+4 Stealth`, scouts at 24 squares ⚠ from a square it cannot see you from.** **⚠ SELF-DESTRUCT once, ever: `3d6` in 2 squares, and it is gone.**

**`Labor`** — `Str +6 · Con +4 · Dex −4 · Int −2 · Cha −4`. **⚠ LARGE, 6 m, `+2` natural armour.** **Carries four times its Strength allowance, and ⚠ A MEDIUM CREATURE MAY RIDE IT — `MOUNTED-COMBAT-01`.**

### ⚠ FOUR OF SEVEN CANNOT MEANINGFULLY FIGHT, AND THAT IS THE TABLE-TIME FIX

> **A protocol droid's turn is *"it moves"* or *"it talks to that Rodian."*** **That is not a decision that costs a round.**

**⚠ `PT-201`'s 62% problem was FOUR COMBATANTS. This is ONE COMBATANT AND THREE SPECIALISTS.**

### Chassis price — ⚠ deliberately SHALLOW

    Protocol · Labor    2,000    ·   Astromech · Remote  4,000
    Probe               5,000    ·   Battle              7,000
    Assassin            9,000

**⚠ Owner ruling: *"not so much that the Droid Master feels he would have to start out with the most expensive thing; that would feel cheap otherwise."***

**⚠ FOUR-AND-A-HALF TIMES between cheapest and dearest, against `DROIDS-UPGRADE-01`'s socket items at 1 to 30,000 credits.** **THE UPGRADES ARE WHERE THE MONEY GOES, and the chassis is a choice of ROLE rather than of POWER.**

**⚠ THE FIRST DROID IS FREE.**

### ⚠ Still open

**⚠ `PT-145` says a controlled droid is a HENCHMAN — *"its own turn, its own initiative, its own declarations."*** **THAT CONTRADICTS `Command Protocol`, `MOUNTED-COMBAT-01` AND THIS DOCUMENT, all of which have companions act on the MASTER'S turn.**

**⚠ `PT-145` was ruled to answer *"whose declaration is it"* BEFORE `Command Protocol`, before mounted combat, before beast obedience.** **Every system built since has answered *"the master's."*** **NOT YET RESOLVED.**

**⚠ Whether a Droid Master BUILDS or BUYS — `PT-225` gave construction to the MACHINIST.**

## PT-568 — Attack credits: ⚠ droids get FEWER, and it resolves an open reading from `PT-89`

**`CLASS-ATTACKS-01 §3a` gave every class FOUR attack credits at 1st level and ⚠ NAMED THE COLLISION ITSELF:**

> ***"⚠ And it overrides the chassis block, which was not obvious… Two readings, and they cannot both hold."***

    ① credits carry ACCESS   ⚠ a droid Marksman spending one on melee ENTERS a
                             melee tree — the chassis block yields
    ② credits are TIERS      ⚠ a droid's credits are RANGED-ONLY, and `T` rises
                             to 40 against an access ceiling of 33

## PT-571 — ⚠ COMPANION and HENCHMAN are split. `PT-145` was overtaken by three systems

**`PT-145` ruled that everything a character controls is a HENCHMAN — *"its own turn, its own initiative, its own declarations."***

> **⚠ IT WAS RULED TO ANSWER *"WHOSE DECLARATION IS IT"* BEFORE `Command Protocol`, BEFORE MOUNTED COMBAT, AND BEFORE BEAST OBEDIENCE EXISTED.** **Every system built since has answered *"THE MASTER'S"* — and `PT-201` REBUILT A CLASS to make that true.**

### The split

| | ⚠ COMPANION | ⚠ HENCHMAN |
|---|---|---|
| **What** | a Beast Master's beast · a Droid Master's droid · a mount | ⚠ a hired NPC, a converted enemy, a temporarily overridden droid |
| **Turn** | ⚠ **the MASTER'S** | ⚠ **its own**, rolled into initiative |
| **Declarations** | ⚠ **the master's** | ⚠ **its own** |
| **Options** | ⚠ **a short FIXED MENU** — `PT-566` | anything a character can do |
| **Death, `Normal`** | ⚠ **dies** — `PT-558` | ⚠ the `Easy` rule: down at 0, up after combat |

> **⚠ A COMPANION IS NOT A SECOND CHARACTER SHEET. A HENCHMAN IS.**

**⚠ THAT IS THE WHOLE OF THE TABLE-TIME PROBLEM `PT-201` MEASURED AT 62% OF THE ROUND, AND IT IS WHY THE COMPANION CATEGORY HAD TO EXIST.**

### ⚠ `PT-145`'s mechanism SURVIVES for the cases it was written for

**`Field Override`'s capstone — a turned droid. `Cover Identity`. Any hired or converted NPC.**

**⚠ Those genuinely ARE temporary control of something that was its own creature, and giving it its own turn is CORRECT.**

**⚠ AN `Engineer`'s CONTROLLED DROID STAYS A HENCHMAN.** **The Engineer takes control of something that was NOT HIS; the Droid Master OWNS his.** **`PT-145`'s own line put both classes in one category and the distinction is ownership.**

### ⚠ A stale arithmetic line, corrected

**`FEATS-LIBRARY-01` carried: *"Droid Master at tier 3 — 1 character + 4 henchmen = 5 turns."***

> **⚠ FIVE BODIES, ONE TURN — `PT-571`.** **And each acts from a menu of THREE, `PT-566`.**

**⚠ The document was still doing the arithmetic that made `PT-201` rebuild the class, in a paragraph explaining why the rebuild was needed.**

### What changed, across four documents

    CLASS-ROSTER-01      "both are henchman classes" → COMPANION classes;
                         ⚠ `Command Protocol`'s ONE-ORDER rule marked SUPERSEDED

## PT-572 — Droid construction. ⚠ Building is cheaper at the top and DEARER at the bottom

**`rules/DROID-CONSTRUCTION-01.md`. Owner ruling: model it on KOTOR 2's lightsaber quest, and make it EASIER.**

### The model, read from the corpus

    u_l_emit_01    295 cr    u_l_cell_02   775 cr
    u_l_lens_01    300 cr    u_l_crys_01   980 cr    ⚠ ≈ 2,350 for a basic set

**⚠ THE LIGHTSABER'S PARTS ARE QUEST-GATED. A DROID'S ARE NOT** — owner ruling: *"available at droid merchant kiosks and whatnot."* **You do not travel the galaxy for a motivator.**

**⚠ NO DROID PARTS EXIST IN EITHER GAME'S ITEM CORPUS. Searched. This is AUTHORED against the lightsaber's SHAPE.**

### Four parts — three universal, one deciding the chassis

    ⚠ Chassis Frame    varies — it IS the chassis
    Motivator          900     without it the droid does not move
    ⚠ Processor Core   1,200   ⚠ THE DEAREST PART, deliberately: it is what
                               makes a droid a character rather than a machine
    Power Cell         700     an hour without one, then it stops

    ⚠ 2,800 credits of universal parts, plus a frame.

### ⚠ THE INTERESTING RESULT

    Protocol   built 3,200   ⚠ assembled 2,000   → you LOSE 1,200 by building
    Assassin   built 6,900   ⚠ assembled 9,000   → you SAVE 2,100

> **⚠ THE UNIVERSAL PARTS DO NOT SCALE, so they DOMINATE a cheap droid and VANISH into an expensive one.**

**⚠ Nobody builds a protocol droid; everybody builds an assassin droid. THAT IS WHAT A CRAFTING SYSTEM SHOULD DO** — and it falls out of flat part prices rather than being imposed.

### Who may build — `PT-225` EXTENDED, not overturned

**⚠ `PT-225` gave droid construction to the MACHINIST. `PT-572` adds the DROID MASTER and the ENGINEER — the two classes whose premise is droids.**

> **⚠ A Machinist BUILDS DROIDS AS A TRADE. A Droid Master builds THE ONES HE WILL USE. An Engineer builds ONE and usually stops.**

**⚠ The Machinist keeps what distinguishes it: the only one who can build FOR SOMEONE ELSE, and the only one whose `Repair` and `Scavenging` reduce the bill.**

### ⚠ Failure costs a DAY, not the parts

**`Repair`, `DC 15 + 5` per price tier. One day per 1,000 credits of parts.**

> **⚠ THAT IS THE DEPARTURE THAT MAKES THIS EASIER THAN THE LIGHTSABER.** **A quest component you cannot replace is a QUEST. A day is an INCONVENIENCE.**

**⚠ And an ASTROMECH IS A WORKBENCH — `SPECIES-CHAPTER-v2`'s `Portable Workbench`. A Droid Master with one can build anywhere.**

### ⚠ `PT-558`'s rebuild cost — CLOSED

> **⚠ THE CHASSIS FRAME SURVIVES. Wreckage is repairable.**

**A destroyed droid costs `2,800` and ONE DAY — the motivator, processor and cell. ⚠ NOT the frame.** **A destroyed Assassin droid costs `2,800`, not `6,900`.**

**⚠ EVERY BAY INSTALLATION IS LOST.** **`DROIDS-UPGRADE-01`: installations are PERMANENT and CONSUMED — they do not come out of a wreck. Socket items are GEAR and are recovered.**

> **⚠ THAT IS THE REAL COST OF LOSING A DROID AND IT IS NOT THE 2,800 CREDITS.** **A nine-bay droid at tier-3 socket prices has more value installed than the chassis ever cost.**

**⚠ A Beast Master pays the ACQUISITION PRICE AGAIN. A Droid Master pays `2,800` and loses everything he installed.**

### ⚠ And the henchman is the GM's — `PT-571` extended

**`PT-145`'s two modes: *"AUTONOMOUS — the GM or AI runs it"* and *"DIRECTED — the player runs it as a second character."***

**⚠ THE DIRECTED MODE IS WHAT BECAME THE COMPANION CATEGORY. What remains a HENCHMAN IS AUTONOMOUS ONLY — the GM or the AI runs it.**

**⚠ A player who overrides an enemy droid does not gain a character to play. They gain AN ALLY THE GM RUNS.**

### The category is OWNERSHIP. Breadth belongs to the CREATURE.

    ⚠ COMPANION   owned by the PLAYER · decided by the PLAYER · its own
                  initiative · DIES on Normal
    ⚠ HENCHMAN    owned by NOBODY · ⚠ decided by the GM or the AI · its own
                  initiative · the Easy rule

**`d20 + Dexterity`. No class modifies it — `PT-96`.**

### ⚠ Prestige entry runs ONE WAY — owner ruling

    ⚠ Soldier → Jedi Weaponmaster     ⚠ NOT LEGAL

**⚠ A Jedi who learns to shoot is a Jedi who learns to shoot. A soldier does not become Force-sensitive by taking a level.**

**Clone shock troopers WERE THE CORUSCANT GUARD — security police, bodyguards, RIOT CONTROL, prison guards, military police.** **⚠ NOT A FIREPOWER ROLE AT ALL.**

**⚠ AND THERE IS AN ERA-EXACT ONE: *"Tetan shock trooper — ELITE WARRIORS OF KRATH CULT."*** **Krath is Empress Teta, ~3997 BBY — Tales of the Jedi, FORTY YEARS BEFORE OUR SETTING, and inside `PT-574`'s source bounds.**

    Blademaster kills in REACH    Operative · Shadow Hunter  work UNSEEN
    ⚠ NOBODY    controls a CROWD or protects a PERSON

**⚠ AND IT TAKES `Weapon Focus`, NOT `Specialization`.** **That makes it THE ONLY PRESTIGE CLASS AN `Astromech` OR `Remote` MAY ENTER — `PT-577` stops those chassis at `Focus`.** **A security droid is entirely in genre.**

    now  ⚠ any ONE RANGED family

## PT-581 — Droid count reads from CHARACTER level. The Droid Master's level table

### ⚠ CHARACTER level, not class level — owner ruling

    ⚠ character level 7    2 controlled — the earliest possible entry
    ⚠ character level 15   3
    ⚠ character level 23   4

    `FEAT-SCHEDULE-01`     prestige FEAT columns read from THEIR OWN class level
    `CLASS-ATTACKS-01 §5`  ⚠ "Attack picks do not." They count from CHARACTER level.

> **⚠ AND THE FICTION SETTLES IT. THE DROIDS ARE OWNED, NOT CONJURED.** **A Droid Master who takes a Soldier level and LOSES CONTROL OF A DROID HE BUILT is absurd.** **Character level means multiclassing costs PROGRESSION, not PROPERTY.**

**⚠ Entry is `Engineer 6` or `Machinist 6`, so the earliest Droid Master IS character level 7 — entry and the first tier COINCIDE, and you never take the class and get nothing.**

### ⚠ FOUR IS A HARD CAP

**`PT-573` gave droids their OWN INITIATIVE. At four droids a Droid Master adds FOUR TURNS to every round — at a four-player table, EIGHT TURNS for one player's presence.**

**⚠ `PT-566`'s three-option menu keeps each fast; the spread keeps it from being a monologue. NEITHER SURVIVES A FIFTH.** **Stated here so it does not creep.**

### The level table

    1   Command Protocol · ⚠ ONE FREE DROID · Droid Upgrade 1
    2   Field Repair — 1d8 to a droid within reach, twice per encounter
    3   Droid Upgrade 2 ⚠ if character level 7+
    4   ⚠ Cross-Link — one droid may use another's CHASSIS ACTION
    5   ⚠ Salvage Rights — parts cost one fewer; a frame is always recoverable
    6   ⚠ Commandeer — take control of a droid that is not yours. ⚠ IT BECOMES
        A HENCHMAN, NOT A COMPANION — `PT-571`.
    7   Droid Upgrade 3 ⚠ if character level 13+ AND the chassis allows it
    8   ⚠ Chassis Focus — one chassis gains +2 attack and +2 Defence. PERMANENT.
    9   Field Repair improves — 2d8, three times, at 6 squares
    10  ⚠ Master Protocol — ONCE per encounter, every droid acts immediately
        after you instead of on its own initiative

> **⚠ `Master Protocol` IS THE ONE TIME THE OLD `PT-201` SHAPE IS LEGAL, AND IT COSTS THE CLASS'S CAPSTONE.** **What `PT-573` removed as a default returns as a once-per-encounter burst.**

**⚠ `Commandeer` uses `PT-571`'s henchman category CORRECTLY: a droid you take is not a droid you OWN, so the GM runs it.**

**⚠ `Droid Upgrade 1–3` are LEVEL-granted at 1 / 7 / 13 in `FEATS-LIBRARY-01`. The table grants them EARLIER to a Droid Master and GATES them so they can never OUTRUN the character-level grant.**

### ⚠ Two name collisions caught

**`Override` had 64 hits → `Commandeer`.** **`Doctrine` had 4 — and one is `Squad Doctrine`, `Command Protocol`'s OWN TIER 2 → `Chassis Focus`.**

**⚠ The second would have collided with the feat it sits beside in the same table.**

## PT-582 — `Command Protocol` is GRANTED, not taken. ⚠ THREE is the cap

### ⚠ It is not a feat you unlock — owner ruling

**⚠ REBUILT A THIRD TIME. `PT-201`, `PT-566`, `PT-582`.**

    ⚠ Command Protocol   Droid Master 1 · character level 7    2 controlled
    ⚠ Squad Protocol     Droid Master 4 · character level 15   3 — ⚠ THE CAP
    ⚠ Master Protocol    Droid Master 8                        ⚠ STILL THREE

> **⚠ GRANTED BY THE CLASS. It costs no feat slot and cannot be chosen.**

**⚠ BOTH GATES MUST BE MET.** **The TIER reads from DROID MASTER level; the DROID COUNT is confirmed by CHARACTER level — `PT-581`.** **A Droid Master 4 at character level 12 HOLDS `Squad Protocol` and still controls TWO.**

### ⚠ THREE IS THE CAP. It was four.

**⚠ THE THIRD TIER IS NOT MORE DROIDS. IT IS BETTER CONTROL.**

> **⚠ A LADDER THAT ONLY EVER ADDS BODIES ADDS TABLE TIME.** **The old one was `2 / 3 / 4` and all three tiers added a body — `Squad Doctrine` and `Master and Servants`, both WITHDRAWN.**

**`Master Protocol` — once per encounter, every droid acts immediately after you.** **⚠ THE OLD `PT-201` SHAPE, LEGAL AS A BURST, costing the ladder's top tier.**

**⚠ At three droids a Droid Master adds THREE turns — at a four-player table, SEVEN for one player's presence, down from EIGHT.**

**`PT-581` had `Master Protocol` at Droid Master 10. It is now the ladder's tier 3 at Droid Master 8.**

**⚠ `Master Handler` replaces it: controlled droids may act on a DELAYED INITIATIVE of your choosing, set once per encounter, and they may all take the SAME COUNT.**

> **⚠ IT DOES NOT ADD A DROID. It buys the one thing three separate initiatives cost you — acting together — WITHOUT spending `Master Protocol`.**

### ⚠ THE LEVEL TABLE IS NOT DROID-SPECIFIC, AND THERE IS NO ORGANIC VERSION

**Owner asked: *"the level table is for droid droid masters right? We also need it for organics naturally as well."***

> **⚠ NO. `Droid Master` IS A CLASS ANY CHARACTER MAY TAKE, and an organic Droid Master and a droid Droid Master READ THE SAME ROWS.**

**⚠ The one place a split may appear is `AGENDA-CURRENT` item 5, the droid/organic FEAT split — and that is about WHICH FEATS A DROID MAY HOLD, not about what this class grants.**

## PT-583 — ⚠ `Droid Upgrade` IS THE DROID'S FEAT. An organic Droid Master cannot hold it

**Owner: *"droid master should not have droid upgrade then, right? The upgrade is attached to the droid itself?"*** **⚠ CORRECT, AND MY LEVEL TABLE GRANTED IT ANYWAY.**

> **⚠ `PT-581` GAVE A DROID MASTER `Droid Upgrade 1 / 2 / 3` AT CLASS LEVELS 1, 3 AND 7.** **AN ORGANIC DROID MASTER CANNOT HOLD IT. HE IS NOT A DROID.**

**`FEATS-LIBRARY-01`: *"As a DROID gains experience ITS PROGRAMMING becomes more adaptable, ACCOMMODATING MORE SOPHISTICATED HARDWARE."*** **⚠ It describes THE BODY BEING UPGRADED — and `PT-577` caps it BY CHASSIS.**

### The split

    ⚠ Droid Upgrade   the DROID'S capacity to RECEIVE    level-granted 1 / 7 / 13
    ⚠ Installation    the MASTER'S ability to FIT        Droid Master 1 / 3 / 7

**⚠ `Installation 1–3` — authored, Droid Master only, granted by the class.** **It lets him install tier-1, 2 or 3 upgrades INTO DROIDS HE OWNS: his skill with a hydrospanner, not his own hardware.**

**⚠ BOTH ARE REQUIRED.** **A tier-3 socket item needs a droid holding `Droid Upgrade 3` AND someone holding `Installation 3` to put it in.**

> **⚠ AN `Astromech` CAPPED AT `Droid Upgrade 2` — `PT-577` — CANNOT RECEIVE A TIER-3 ITEM NO MATTER WHO IS WORKING ON IT.** **The cap now bites in two directions and stays coherent.**

**⚠ A DROID MASTER WHO IS HIMSELF A DROID HOLDS BOTH, SEPARATELY.** **His own chassis capacity and his skill at fitting are DIFFERENT THINGS and always were.**

### ⚠ `Command Protocol` is `PT-201`'s, not mine

**Owner asked whether I had just created it. ⚠ NO — `PT-201` built it, and it only appeared in `audit_classcoverage`'s missing-class list because a `####` HEADING LOOKED LIKE A CLASS ROW to the parser.**

**⚠ AND `CLASS-ROSTER-01` STILL CARRIED THE OLD VERSION, WRONG ON FOUR COUNTS:**

    ⚠ ONE ORDER    → each droid acts SEPARATELY from a menu of three. `PT-566`.

## PT-589 — HK availability locked. ⚠ BACKTRACKING permitted, and the setting already does it

### ⚠⚠ NO HK MODEL IS PLAYABLE IN A KOTOR 2 CAMPAIGN PACKAGE — owner ruling

    HKB-3 · ⚠ HK-24    ⚠ KOTOR 1 AND BEFORE ONLY
    ⚠ HK-48            ⚠ PRE-KOTOR 2 ONLY
    ⚠ HK-49            ⚠ POST-KOTOR 2 ONLY
    HK-47 · HK-50      UNIQUE, never for sale
    HK-51              EXCLUDED — 3668 BBY, SWTOR

> **⚠ THE KOTOR 2 WINDOW IS DELIBERATELY EMPTY.**

**⚠ AND THE SOURCES SUPPORT IT: *"Sometime after, the Republic BANNED the ownership, manufacture, and use of HK series droids"* — after the HK-50s hunted Meetra Surik across the galaxy.** **A campaign in that window is one where owning an HK is a CRIME and nobody is selling.**

### ⚠ BACKTRACKING — a later model may become an earlier one

**Owner ruling, AMENDING `PT-574`'s exclusions.**

> **⚠ THE DESIGN TRAVELS. THE NAME MUST CHANGE.**

**⚠ AND THE SETTING ALREADY DOES THIS, WHICH IS WHY IT IS SAFE:**

    ⚠ C-3PO   Cybot Galactica, 32 BBY      the LATER one
    ⚠ A-3DO   Duwani, Tales of the Jedi    ⚠ THE SAME DROID, 4,000 YEARS EARLIER

**⚠ WOOKIEEPEDIA CARRIES BOTH. The `3DO-series` IS the backtrack, and LUCASFILM MADE IT.**

### The rules

    ⚠ THE NAME CHANGES — a backtracked model is not called what the later one was
    ⚠ THE MAKER CHANGES to an era company where the later one does not exist yet
    ⚠ THE SOURCE IS INSPIRATION, NOT WARRANT — "backtracked from X", never
      "attested as X"
    ⚠ NO IMPERIAL MODELS. The prequel era is permitted; the Empire is not.

**⚠ NOT A LICENCE TO INVENT — `PT-574` STILL HOLDS.** **It is a licence to take a SHAPE the setting demonstrably reuses and give it the name it would have had.**

**⚠ EVERY BACKTRACKED MODEL IS MARKED and names what it came from.**

### Three models it produced

    ⚠ CZ-P3 Miniprobe    Czerka   ← SWTOR's `CZ-P9` and `EW-94`
    ⚠ SK-1 Seeker        Duwani   ← the prequel `DRK-1 Dark Eye`, a SITH probe
    ⚠ Prowler MK V       Duwani   ← the `Prowler 1000 seeker droid` — `PT-590`

> **⚠ CZERKA IS THE SAME COMPANY IN BOTH ERAS, which makes `CZ-` the cleanest backtrack on the roster — ONLY THE NUMBER MOVES.**

**⚠ `DRK-1` → `SK-1` because *"Dark Eye"* is a prequel-SITH brand and ours is a DIFFERENT SITH.**

**⚠ `Prowler 1000` → `Prowler 100` — the number drops a decimal place, WHICH IS WHAT A THOUSAND YEARS OF ITERATION LOOKS LIKE FROM THE OTHER END.**

**⚠ `ID9` AND `ID10` NOT BACKTRACKED.** **A two-character prefix with a single digit leaves NOWHERE TO MOVE without inventing.** **`Prowler` has a number that CAN move, and that is the whole difference.**

**⚠ `Probe` and `Remote` each went from ONE model to THREE and TWO — and not one name was invented from nothing.**

    ⚠ a droid model MAY NOT be invented from NOTHING
    ⚠ THERE IS NO THIRD CATEGORY

**Owner ruling, and it corrects a convention error I made.**

**⚠ I BACKTRACKED THE NUMBER AND KEPT THE FORMAT.** **`Prowler 1000` → `Prowler 100` moved the digit and left a LATER ERA'S NAMING SHAPE in place — which is exactly the half-measure `PT-589`'s own rule warns against: *"the design travels; THE NAME MUST CHANGE."***

**⚠ A backtrack changes the DESIGNATION SYSTEM, not just the number in it.**

## PT-618 — ⚠⚠ I RAN A GENERATOR THAT WROTE TO THE WRONG DIRECTORY, AND COMMITTED THE RESULT

**⚠ `PT-617` generalised `audit_source`'s derived-file check from ONE file to a LIST — and adding `FEATS-LIBRARY-01.md` to it made me RUN `gen_feats.py` TO TEST IT.**

> **⚠⚠ `gen_feats.py` WRITES TO THE REPO ROOT, NOT TO `rules/`.**

    _OUT = os.environ.get('KOTOR_OUT', abspath(join(_HERE, '..')))

**⚠ `KOTOR_OUT` IS UNSET, SO IT DEFAULTS TO THE PARENT OF `scripts/` — THE REPO ROOT.**

**⚠ IT CREATED A SECOND, DIFFERENT `FEATS-LIBRARY-01.md`:**

    ⚠ ./FEATS-LIBRARY-01.md          35,449 chars   258 entries · 93 chains
    ⚠ ./rules/FEATS-LIBRARY-01.md   107,622 chars   221 entries · 90 chains

**⚠ NOT COPIES. DIFFERENT DOCUMENTS WITH THE SAME NAME AND DIFFERENT COUNTS.**

### ⚠⚠ AND I COMMITTED IT

**⚠ `a2f8f11` CARRIES THE STRAY FILE.** **I read the gate output AFTER the commit ran in the same command — the gate said `DO NOT SEND` and the push had already happened.**

> **⚠ THE GATE IS ONLY A GATE IF IT RUNS BEFORE THE COMMIT.** **Chaining `gate && commit && push` in one shell line put the check and the action in the wrong order.**

**Removed from the index and from disk.**

### ⚠⚠ AND THE REAL FILE'S HEADER IS FALSE

**`rules/FEATS-LIBRARY-01.md` carries *"Generated by `scripts/gen_feats.py`. Do not hand-edit."***

> **⚠ IT IS HAND-MAINTAINED. Every feat edit this session — `PT-559`, `PT-568`, `PT-590`, `PT-615` — went into it BY HAND and none was lost, because the generator has never written there.**

**⚠ `PT-511`: *"a file marked DERIVED with no generator ROTS."*** **⚠ THIS IS THE INVERSE AND IT IS WORSE: A HAND-MAINTAINED FILE MARKED GENERATED INVITES SOMEONE TO REGENERATE IT AND LOSE EVERYTHING.**

**⚠ `FEATS-LIBRARY-01.md` IS EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED FROM `audit_source`'s derived list, WITH THE REASON WRITTEN IN THE SCRIPT.**

### ⚠ What the generalisation was still worth

**`CLASS-TABLES-AUTHORED.md` is now verified alongside `BEASTS-REFERENCE-01.md`.** **Two real derived files, both checked, and the third correctly kept out.**
